Sports.title: Jorge Linares Facing Deportation After El Paso Airport Arrest
Sports.content:
Former three-division world champion Jorge Linares is sitting in federal custody in El Paso, Texas, after immigration officers arrested him at the airport on Sunday. The 41-year-old Venezuelan retired in 2023, and now he is stuck in a legal battle outside the ring that looks far messier than anything he ever dealt with between the ropes.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement told reporters that Border Patrol and ICE agents picked up Linares at El Paso International Airport. According to the agency, Linares entered the United States on October 26, 2023, on temporary admission and stayed past his allowed time. ICE confirmed he will remain locked up at the El Paso Service Processing Center while his removal case moves forward.

His attorneys at Wilner & O’Reilly are fighting the government story. In a statement on Tuesday, his legal team insisted Linares is authorized to be in the country and has cooperated fully with officials. Still, his lawyers refused to say what exact status or paperwork he holds, leaving fans wondering how a former star ended up in detention after attending a ProBox TV card in town.

Linares broke the news himself on Sunday with a short Spanish post on X saying ICE had him in El Paso. WBA president Gilberto Mendoza confirmed the arrest on Monday and said he is staying in regular touch with the fighter’s family.

Fans remember Linares best for winning world titles at featherweight, super featherweight, and lightweight before retiring after his 2023 loss to Jack Catterall in Liverpool. He famously dropped Vasiliy Lomachenko at Madison Square Garden in 2018 before getting stopped by a body shot, and he hurt Devin Haney late in their 2021 title bout. Now, instead of enjoying retirement, Linares is waiting on immigration judges to decide if he can stay in the United States.

Sports.title: Jermell Charlo Wanted Errol Spence in Texas
Sports.content:
Jermell Charlo is talking mighty tough now that the fight is off the table. After watching Errol Spence Jr. return from a long layoff against Tim Tszyu in Australia, Charlo claims he is glad they never fought in Texas because he would have felt bad about what he would have done to his former gym mate.

It is easy to talk big from the couch, especially when you were trying to pick a shell of a fighter. Charlo wanted Spence for a comeback bout in Texas, mentioning a matchup between two former unified champions who both needed a payday after sitting on the shelf.

“If I’m going to come back and Errol’s been gone for a long time, let us come back and fight in Texas,” said Charlo to Fight Hub TV, arguing it was a better fight than Spence traveling to Australia for Tszyu.

What makes that sales idea so pathetic is the timeline. Charlo never called out the prime version of Spence before his horrific 2019 Ferrari crash in Dallas. Spence has looked like a shadow of his former self ever since that wreck, surviving retinal detachment surgery and a one-sided beating from Terence Crawford before stepping in with Tszyu.

“I really, really would feel really, really bad for what I would have done to him. So I’m glad that didn’t happen. And maybe one day in life we can shake hands again,” Charlo said.

Charlo called the bout terrible and trashed both fighters for having zero movement, though he still claimed Spence could have edged it with more aggression. That was a clear shot at Tszyu, suggesting the Australian was there for the taking against a diminished opponent.

Jermell is ignoring his own long stretch of inactivity since getting dominated by Canelo Alvarez in 2023. Nobody knows what Charlo has left in the tank either, and he waited around so long that Tszyu ruined his cash-out plan against Spence before he could pull it off.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Could Dump WBO Belt If Muratalla Bid Falls Short
Sports.content:
Whether Shakur Stevenson defends his WBO junior welterweight title against Raymond Muratalla or dumps the belt comes down to one thing on November 30: the size of the winning purse bid.

Dan Rafael reported Tuesday that their negotiating period expired without a deal, pushing the mandatory defense toward a purse bid where Stevenson gets 75 percent and Muratalla receives 25 percent. On paper, a 75 percent split sounds like easy money for the champion, yet the percentage means nothing until promoters put real cash on the table.

Since walking away from Zuffa Boxing over money, Stevenson has operated as a promotional free agent used to massive Saudi-funded paydays. Without Riyadh Season guaranteeing an inflated pot for this mandatory, traditional promoters have to bid strictly on what a Stevenson versus Muratalla main event can actually generate at the gate and on streaming.

Muratalla (25-0, 17 KOs) is a former IBF lightweight champion, and brings enough power at 140 pounds to make Stevenson work for twelve rounds. The problem is that Muratalla does not carry the name recognition or casual fanbase that Teofimo Lopez brought when Stevenson beat him in January. Promoters are not going to bid 15 million dollars for a risky fight against an opponent most casual fans barely know.

If the winning bid lands around 4 or 5 million, Stevenson’s 75 percent cut shrinks to roughly 3 to 3.75 million. Taking a steep pay cut off his recent Saudi numbers to fight a heavy-handed mandatory challenger makes zero business sense for a fighter chasing major names.

If the November 30 bid comes in way below his usual standard, Stevenson will likely vacate the WBO strap before he ever lets them strip him. Giving up the belt costs him leverage in unification talks at 140 pounds, yet the winning dollar figure on bid day will tell us immediately whether he keeps the title or walks away.

Without Saudi money artificially inflating the pot, platforms like Netflix and DAZN look strictly at return on investment, and Shakur’s commercial track record makes an eight-figure guarantee a tough sell.

The only way DAZN or a promoter like Eddie Hearn stretches their budget on November 30 is if they treat the Muratalla fight as a loss-leader to lock Shakur into a multi-fight deal.

They might swallow a loss on Muratalla just to secure the rights to put Shakur in unifications against Dalton Smith or Gary Antuanne Russell down the road. Otherwise, nobody is writing a Saudi-sized check for a one-off purse bid.

If the November 30 purse bid for Muratalla comes in embarrassingly low, say under $4 million or $5 million, Shakur is going straight to social media to laugh at the number before dumping his WBO junior welterweight title.

You already know how this script plays out. Stevenson has been sitting on the shelf since beating Teofimo Lopez in January, and he did not walk away from Zuffa Boxing just to take a massive pay cut against an unbeaten puncher most casual fans cannot pick out of a lineup.

With no Saudi money guaranteed to inflate the pot, promoters have to bid strictly on what Stevenson versus Muratalla can make at the box office.

The second those envelopes open, expect Stevenson to flood X with posts mocking the winning bid and claiming promoters want pound-for-pound talent on the cheap. He will tell fans he is a businessman first and insist nobody should expect him to fight a dangerous former IBF lightweight champion for chump change.

In the end, pride and purse expectations win every time. If the November 30 bid comes in weak, Shakur will drop that belt faster than a hot skillet and go looking for a bigger payday elsewhere.

In hindsight, turning down $7 million from Zuffa for a homecoming fight in Newark against Jose “Rayo” Valenzuela, only to potentially end up staring at a $3 million to $4.5 million share against a much tougher opponent in Muratalla, would look like a massive self-inflicted wound.

Sports.title: Chris Mannix Questions Diego Pacheco’s Prep for Fulghum
Sports.content:
Diego Pacheco has a preparation problem to answer for before taking an immediate rematch with Darius Fulghum. Chris Mannix said Pacheco told him before Saturday’s upset that he and trainer Buddy McGirt don’t watch tape. Fulghum’s camp studied Pacheco, and Sergio Mora saw the work show up in the opening seconds.

“Somebody in that team has got to be watching film and preparing specifically for your opponent,” said Mannix on his podcast. Mora agreed that the trainer should do the studying. He said he rarely watched much tape himself as a fighter, but his trainer would flag specific things an opponent did that Mora could take advantage of.

Mora saw Fulghum go after Pacheco’s lead arm almost as soon as the fight started. Within the first minute, Fulghum was getting low and making the taller man punch down, which gave him a chance to come over the top. He ended up outjabbing Pacheco despite giving up reach. When the distance closed, Mora thought Fulghum got the better of Pacheco there, too.

“Pacheco was a mean body puncher. Fulghum was meaner. He didn’t let him get mean,” said Mora.

Mannix credited Julian Chua with doing film work with Fulghum in Los Angeles alongside longtime trainer Darnell Pierce. The camp even looked at David Benavidez’s win over Oleksandr Gvozdyk, according to Mannix, studying how Benavidez slipped in anticipation of punches as he came forward. Fulghum told the broadcasters during fight week that he expected to get inside against Pacheco. Saturday showed why he was so sure.

Pacheco’s feet were a concern for both broadcasters. Mora said he had raised the issue before, pointing to the need for quicker movement in and out, feints with the feet, and better angles. That helps explain how Pacheco could have the longer jab on paper and still lose the battle at range. When Fulghum could draw the jab from where he wanted and close the distance on his terms, Pacheco had to do more with his feet to get back to a distance he could control.

Eddie Hearn wants Pacheco to go straight back in with Fulghum, and both broadcasters agreed. Mora called it “rematch or bust” and said he wanted to see Pacheco win decisively. Mannix floated April 2027 and said a second loss would leave the 25-year-old facing a long rebuild.

Pacheco now has twelve rounds of his own fight to work from. If the rematch happens, the first thing to watch is how he responds when Fulghum gets low and starts taking away the jab again. Fulghum made that work from the opening round. He has every reason to make Pacheco prove he can handle it the second time.

Sports.title: Josh Kelly’s Footwork Could Test Jaron Ennis’ Patience
Sports.content:
Trainer Stephen Edwards thinks Jaron “Boots” Ennis will stop Josh Kelly late in their junior middleweight unification, though he sees a familiar problem standing in the way. Kelly has the footwork to make Ennis chase him. What Edwards wants to see is whether Boots walks him down behind a steady jab or gets impatient trying to take his head off.

“His feet are a bigger deal than his hand speed. His hand speed won’t be a problem for Boots,” Edwards said to Sean Zittel’s channel. He brought up Amir Khan to explain the difference between throwing fast punches and throwing shots an opponent can see coming. Even if Kelly and Ennis look evenly matched for speed in the opening rounds, Edwards believes Ennis will read Kelly’s tells early.

Ennis’ corner has already dealt with this style

Derek “Bozy” Ennis trained Philadelphia southpaw Ray Robinson, who fought Kelly to a draw back in 2019. Edwards thought Robinson deserved the decision that night and believes having gone through that camp will give the Ennis corner plenty of confidence. Bozy brought up the draw himself at the launch press conference, so the history is already on both teams’ minds.

Kelly has obviously had years to improve since then. Edwards gave him full credit for beating Bakhram Murtazaliev, an opponent few wanted to go near. A 2019 draw only tells you so much about Kelly at 154 pounds today, especially after he proved he can beat a heavy-handed champion marching forward. The Robinson tape gives Bozy a starting point. The Murtazaliev win shows what Kelly can do when real power comes after him.

Ennis has his own history to study, too, and it goes deeper than one bad night. Across two full fights with Karen Chukhadzhian, Boots never looked comfortable dealing with that constant movement. In their rematch in front of his own fans in Philadelphia, Chukhadzhian tagged Ennis with clean right hands and made him look awkward for long stretches. It wasn’t until Chukhadzhian finally gassed out down the stretch that Ennis took control of the fight.

The problem for Kelly is that copying that blueprint takes more than quick feet. Kelly isn’t quite as slick as Chukhadzhian, and he doesn’t carry the same power or willingness to stand in the pocket and trade. Against Kelly, the temptation for Ennis will still be to load up on another power shot whenever the first one misses, giving Kelly room to step away and make him reset. Using a sharp jab to herd Kelly toward the ropes will make finding clean openings much easier, especially if Kelly lacks the pop to make Ennis respect what is coming back.

“Boots doesn’t choose the conservative route,” Edwards said. Ennis likes putting combinations together and hurting guys once he gets close. Kelly can use that aggression against him by making Ennis reach and getting away before the follow-up lands. How many rounds Kelly can pull that off without giving away points on the cards is another question.

Edwards expects the cost of all that movement to catch up with Kelly in the second half. In his view, Kelly will have to keep moving even when he wants a round to catch his breath, because standing in range gives Ennis the chance to land his heaviest shots. That is where Edwards sees the late stoppage coming. Kelly’s best chance to change that is turning his early escapes into real scoring opportunities. If all that footwork only keeps him safe, Ennis will take his time closing the distance and break him down.

Sports.title: Israil Madrimov Exposed Terence Crawford, And Walking Away Won’t Fix It
Sports.content:
Terence Crawford should come out of retirement to fight Israil Madrimov again if he wants his Mount Rushmore claim taken seriously. Beating Canelo Alvarez gave Crawford a historic achievement, but it did nothing to settle the argument over whether he deserved to beat Madrimov.

That is the stain on his legacy. Crawford left their August 2024 fight with a unanimous decision and the WBA junior middleweight title after looking completely out of ideas against the only prime A-level opponent on his resume. The scores were 116-112 and 115-113 twice, a narrow escape that looked like a gift decision to plenty of observers who saw him clearly lose.

“A win over Canelo will put me on Mount Rushmore, I really believe that,” said Crawford before their fight.

All that Mount Rushmore talk sounds like deep insecurity, as if Crawford is trying to talk himself into credentials he never earned. Truly secure all-time greats do not campaign for their own spot on the mountain. Listening to Crawford demand historical elevation after struggling so badly against Madrimov is like watching a PFC insist on being promoted to General right after failing an inspection.

Once Crawford asks for that kind of company, counting belts and pointing to an unbeaten record cannot be the whole discussion. His overall resume was already thin, padded out with unheralded contenders and aging names well past their best days. When he finally stepped in against a sharp, prime operator in Madrimov, his superiority vanished.

Madrimov gave him an awkward problem he could not solve. His feints, changes of position, and sharp right hands prevented Crawford from settling into the comfortable control he had enjoyed against lesser opposition. Crawford had to think before committing, hesitating for long stretches without throwing a punch.

The case for Madrimov winning rests on the cleaner, more effective work in the close rounds. Crawford’s supporters can point to his jab and late activity, which is precisely why running it back matters. This was not a beaten challenger begging for another payday. It was a prime opponent who exposed the limits of Crawford’s aura.

“I thought Israil Madrimov did enough to edge it here tonight,” said Eddie Hearn after the fight. Hearn promoted Madrimov, so his interest was obvious, yet his objection reflected what millions of viewers saw unfold in real time.

For fans who scored it for Madrimov, Crawford’s victory carries a permanent asterisk. Walking away without fixing it leaves a glaring hole in his career, especially since that shaky performance should have disqualified him from landing the Canelo sweepstakes in the first place.

The Canelo opportunity was already being discussed before Crawford faced Madrimov, creating an obvious financial incentive for the bigger attraction to survive. It explains why critics viewed the scorecards with suspicion, and why beating Canelo feels like an escape hatch rather than proof of all-time greatness.

Crawford could answer the boxing question tomorrow if he actually believed his own hype. Come back and face Madrimov again. Prove the first performance was an off night, take away Madrimov’s best weapons over twelve rounds, and earn the rank he keeps trying to claim.

There would also be a clear tactical reason to watch. Madrimov would need to turn his success with isolated clean punches into sustained offense, while Crawford would have to find ways to attack without spending rounds frozen by feints.

Crawford earned the money to retire, but he has not earned immunity from criticism. Until he clears up the mess he left behind against the best prime fighter he ever faced, his Mount Rushmore talk will keep sounding like a man trying to convince himself more than anyone else.

If Crawford wants another fight to save his legacy from that gift decision, Madrimov is the only call that counts.

Sports.title: Rafael Predicts WBA Will Let Teofimo Bypass Catterall
Sports.content:
Jack Catterall might win every argument with the WBA and still watch his biggest payday walk out the door. Dan Rafael thinks the sanctioning body will end up letting Teofimo Lopez bypass his mandatory to fight WBC welterweight champion Ryan Garcia in early 2027, simply because the sanctioning fees on a unification are too big to turn down.

“The Catterall side that thought that this was over was mistaken because it’s not over,” Rafael told Pro Boxing Fans.

Right now, that is Rafael’s read on how boxing politics usually play out rather than proof that a special permit has been approved. Lopez’s team insists they filed their request on November 5 and are appealing the WBA’s ruling, which leaves Catterall sitting in limbo despite doing everything by the rules.

According to Rafael, talks for Lopez against Garcia are already deep down the road, even if nothing is signed yet. He expects that fight to happen either as a two-belt unification or with just Garcia’s WBC title on the line if Teofimo dumps his strap.

For Catterall, the worst part is watching Teofimo keep his belt while taking the bigger money fight. Catterall beat Shakhram Giyasov in May for the secondary strap and turned down step-aside cash to force his shot, yet Rafael points out that big names almost always get greenlit when a unification is on the table.

“They’re going to see a lot of money that can be made on a sanction and involvement in a major event like Teofimo–Ryan Garcia,” Rafael said.

Even if the WBA stands firm and refuses the exception, Catterall still gets burned. Teofimo would likely vacate rather than risk his money fight against a skilled southpaw for a fraction of the Garcia money. Catterall would get upgraded to full champion by email, getting the belt without the career-defining fight he actually wanted.

WBA Orders Teofimo vs. Catterall breaks down the mandatory dispute and whether Lopez will vacate the title to chase the Ryan Garcia fight.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Risks Losing His Edge By Going Into Businessman Mode
Sports.content:
David Benavidez says he is done handing over 10 percent of his purse to a promoter once his December 5 cruiserweight unification against Michal Cieslak is in the books. After a decade with Sampson Lewkowicz, Benavidez told Reuters he wants to negotiate his own contracts starting next year.

“I paid my dues. After this, I’m saving the 10% for myself,” said Benavidez to Reuters.

Once fighters start thinking like businessmen instead of athletes, their careers usually hit a brick wall. In leagues like the NFL, NBA, or NHL, the schedule forces athletes to show up and compete every week regardless of who stands across from them. Boxing has zero structure like that, so a self-managed fighter can sit on the shelf for a year, turning down tough fights while praying for one giant lottery ticket.

Look at Shakur Stevenson right now for proof of how badly that mindset backfires. After beating Teofimo Lopez back in January, Stevenson wasted ten months chasing a Devin Haney payday that fell apart, lost his Zuffa Boxing deal, and got stuck with a dangerous WBO mandatory against Raymond Muratalla that brings little money.

Benavidez is heading down that same slippery slope after launching DB Promotions on Brian Custer’s channel in October. Even though he insists, “I’m still PBC all the way,” while keeping Al Haymon, TGB Promotions, and Luis De Cubas in his corner, his eyes are already drifting past the best fighters in his own division.

Assuming he beats Cieslak in Glendale, Arizona, to add the WBC strap to the WBA and WBO belts he took from Gilberto “Zurdo” Ramirez in May, Benavidez will hold three titles at 200 pounds. Instead of rushing to unify all four belts against Jai Opetaia, Benavidez told Reuters that facing Oleksandr Usyk does far more for his bank account.

Usyk holds all the leverage at the negotiating table and does not need Benavidez. If Benavidez spends 2027 acting like a cautious promoter instead of an active destroyer, his popularity and sharpness will vanish long before Usyk ever signs a contract.

Ghana News.title: MTN CEO Stephen Blewett hails 30 years of operations in Ghana, announces US$1.1bn investment
Ghana News.content:
The CEO of MTN Ghana, Stephen Blewett has said the company is excited to mark three decades in the country as it plans to invest US$1.1 billion over the next three years. He made the announcement at MTN Ghana’s 30th anniversary Stakeholder Dinner.

Welcoming guests including Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang, the Ga Mantse’s representative Nii Adote Odaawulu I, South African High Commissioner Linda Shongwe, Ministers of State, and MTN Group leadership, Mr. Blewett said MTN could not mark the milestone without the people in the room.

“Above all, I want to thank Ghanaians. For thirty years, you have embraced this brand, trusted it with your calls, your savings and your businesses, and grown with it,” he said. “MTN is what it is because Ghana made it so.”

From Spacefon to MTN

Mr. Blewett traced the journey back to 1996, when owning a mobile phone was a luxury and greeting a mother in another region could mean queueing at a communication centre.

That year, Scancom switched on Spacefon. Spacefon became Areeba, and Areeba became MTN.

“The name changed, but the purpose did not: to connect Ghanaians to each other and to opportunity,” he said.

Each decade added a milestone: the MTN Ghana Foundation in 2007, Mobile Money in 2009, and listing on the Ghana Stock Exchange in 2018, when thousands of Ghanaians became owners of the company. “We moved from 2G to 3G, to 4G, and now we stand on the edge of 5G. At each step, we asked the same question: what will this do for Ghana?”

32 million subscribers, 18.9m MoMo Users

Today, more than 32 million subscribers rely on MTN’s network, served by a Ghanaian team of over 2,000 people. Beyond them, hundreds of thousands of Ghanaians earn a living through MTN as MoMo agents, merchants, retailers, dealers, contractors and suppliers. “Our story is, and will always remain, a Ghanaian story,” Mr. Blewett said.

Mobile Money, which began as a simple way to send money home, now has about 18.9 million active users as at September 2026 — paying school fees, trading, receiving wages, saving and borrowing.

“For many women, traders and farming families, a MoMo wallet was their first financial account,” he said, adding that MTN will keep working with regulators, banks, agents and merchants to keep every customer safe.

US$1.1 Billion Investment, 500 New Sites

Looking ahead, Mr. Blewett announced MTN plans to invest US$1.1 billion over the next three years, with an unprecedented 500 new cell sites being rolled out this year.

Its new 5G spectrum will help extend coverage and ease congestion, while the company expands into home broadband, fibre, enterprise solutions and digital services.

“We recognise that some communities have waited too long for better service. Our customers rightly expect a dependable network, and we are determined to deliver it,” he said.

He called for telecom sites to be protected as critical national infrastructure, noting that when the network is disrupted, businesses cannot transact, services grind to a halt and families cannot stay in touch.

Bright Scholarship and Digital Skills

Mr. Blewett also highlighted MTN’s investment beyond the network, including meeting the latest Bright Scholarship recipients — 300 university students and 200 teachers pursuing studies in science, technology, engineering, mathematics and technical education.

“Their ambition reflects the spirit that has carried this company for thirty years,” he said.

Call for Stable Policy

Thanking the Vice President, Sector Minister Sam George, Ministers and regulators past and present, Mr. Blewett congratulated the National Communications Authority on its 30th anniversary and the Ghana Chamber of Telecommunications on its 15th.

He noted MTN operates in a demanding environment of rising costs, fibre cuts and a heavy tax burden, and called for continued collaboration on stable policy and regulation that allows investment to continue.

“When this industry is strong, Ghana’s digital economy is stronger,” he said.

Honouring the Pioneers

Mr. Blewett asked pioneers who joined when the company operated from a small office on Graphic Road — climbing masts in the rain and carrying equipment to sites on foot — to rise for applause.

He also paid tribute to former CEOs who led the company before him: Ghassan, Ebenezer Twum Asante — the first Ghanaian CEO — Selorm Adadevoh, Ahmad Farroukh, Brett Goschen, Michael Ikpoki, and Serame Taukobong.“Each left a legacy that continues to guide us,” he said.

Closing, he said mobile technology in Ghana had moved from the preserve of a few to an essential part of everyday life, made possible by the trust of customers and partnership of Government, regulators, shareholders and colleagues.

“Our commitment is clear: to keep investing in Ghana, to bring more Ghanaians into the digital economy, and to work hand in hand with all of you.”

Ghana News.title: Prof Fred Binka, pioneering malaria researcher and founding UHAS Vice-Chancellor, dies at 73
Ghana News.content:
Prof Fred Newton Binka

Ghana has lost one of its foremost public health experts, Professor Fred Newton Binka, a renowned malaria researcher and founding Vice-Chancellor of the University of Health and Allied Sciences (UHAS).

Prof. Binka, who was 73, was a physician, clinical epidemiologist and academic whose work significantly contributed to malaria research, infectious disease prevention and public health development in Ghana and across Africa.

Until his death, he served as Chairman of the Governing Council of the Ghana Health Service (GHS). He was also a former member of the Board of Trustees of the International Vaccine Institute (IVI).

Born in June 1953, Prof. Binka dedicated much of his professional life to strengthening health research and developing expertise in public health.

He became the founding Vice-Chancellor of UHAS when the university was established by the government in March 2012. He played a central role in building the institution and advancing its mandate to train health professionals and scientists.

His contribution to the university was recognised in June 2022 when UHAS named its School of Public Health after him.

The decision was taken by the university's Governing Council and management under the leadership of its Vice-Chancellor, Professor John Owusu Gyapong.

Before joining UHAS, Prof. Binka served as Dean of the School of Public Health at the University of Ghana, Legon.

He had earlier spent more than two decades working with the Ministry of Health, where he established the Navrongo Health Research Centre, which gained international recognition for its contribution to health research.

He also founded the INDEPTH Network, an international research network comprising 33 field sites across 24 developing countries in Africa and Asia.

His influence extended to international health policy and research. He served on more than a dozen World Health Organisation (WHO) expert committees and panels and chaired the GAVI Independent Review Committee.

He was also a trustee of several international non-governmental organisations involved in health interventions, particularly malaria control.

Prof. Binka obtained his MB ChB in Ghana, a Master of Public Health (MPH) in Jerusalem and a PhD in Epidemiology from the University of Basel in Switzerland in 1997.

His contributions to malaria research earned him several international honours, including the inaugural Rudolf Geigy Award in 2001 and the Ronald Ross Medal from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine in 2010.

Read Also: UHAS names School of Public Health after Foundation Vice-Chancellor Prof Fred Newton Binka

In a tribute, the International Vaccine Institute (IVI) announced his death and celebrated his contributions to research, education and public health.

Prof. Binka served on the institute's Board of Trustees between 2014 and 2020.

"IVI mourns the passing of Professor Fred Newton Binka, a pioneering malaria researcher, dedicated educator, and former member of IVI’s Board of Trustees," the institute said.

It acknowledged his role in training successive generations of scientists and health professionals, as well as his work in advancing infectious disease prevention in Ghana and beyond.

"We are grateful for his leadership and extend our heartfelt condolences to Prof. Binka’s family, friends, colleagues, students, and all those whose lives he touched," IVI added.

Ghana News.title: Don’t despair – Thomas-Asante stresses support for Black Stars
Ghana News.content:
Ghana striker Brandon Thomas-Asante has stressed the need for continued support for the Black Stars, adding that the team strives to meet fan expectations.

The Stars have endured a mixed bag of emotions from fans, following years of inconsistent performances.

This month’s victories over Somalia are Ghana’s first in the AFCON 2027 qualifiers, and coincidentally Ghana’s first wins in AFCON qualifying since 2023.

The Black Stars started the campaign with consecutive defeats to Ivory Coast and The Gambia.

Speaking to JoySports Atsu Tamakloe in an exclusive interview, the Coventry City striker said it was still important not to despair.

The Coventry City forward spoke exclusively to JoySports Atsu Tamakloe

‘‘We don’t want the fans to be panicking or worrying because they should know that we have an ear to listen to; we know what they want.’’

‘‘We can do what they want; we can overcome any obstacle to achieve that for them,’’ he concluded.

Ghana are currently third in Group C of the AFCON 2027 Qualifiers with six points, behind The Gambia on seven points and Ivory Coast on ten points.

The Black Stars need to win both remaining games, against The Gambia and Ivory Coast, to qualify for the tournament.

Anything else would give second-placed The Gambia the qualification advantage, as they already have a better head-to-head, having beaten Ghana 4-2 in Accra.

Ghana News.title: Great Osama, Davido and the gold rush that lasted 19 minutes! – Jimmy Aglah writes from the Republic of Uncommon Sense
Ghana News.content:
Once upon a time in the Republic of Uncommon Sense, a man who had spent years searching for gold beneath the soil of Amansie reportedly discovered that the richest deposits were not necessarily buried underground. Some were walking about on two legs, wearing designer clothes, carrying microphones and answering to the name Davido.

And so it came to pass that Great Osama, a businessman from Manso Akwasiso in the Ashanti Region, decided to bring Nigerian Afrobeats superstar Davido to his community for a musical performance. It was an ambitious undertaking, the sort that would make the village elders abandon their evening game of draughts and begin calculating how many cocoa farms one would have to sell to finance a single chorus.

The occasion was the third anniversary of NYC Hotel, owned by Great Osama, whose other claim to prominence is his association with small-scale mining. The reported cost of bringing Davido to town was a staggering US$600,000, an amount that could make even a bank manager request permission to sit down before continuing the conversation.

The figure remains unconfirmed, of course. But in Ghana, where rumours travel faster than ambulances on the Accra-Kumasi highway, the public had already converted the dollars into cedis, divided the amount by the number of songs performed and appointed itself the Auditor-General of Entertainment Expenditure.

Then came the performance.

Or, more precisely, the appearance.

Depending on whose stopwatch one consults, Davido reportedly entertained the gathering for somewhere between 19 and 30 minutes before departing. And suddenly, a celebration intended to announce the arrival of international entertainment in Manso Akwasiso became a national examination in mathematics, economics and the management of disappointment.

If the reported US$600,000 fee and the widely circulated 19-minute duration were both accurate, the arithmetic would produce approximately US$31,579 per minute. That is enough to make a Ghanaian schoolteacher reconsider the entire philosophy of monthly salaries.

At that rate, even clearing one's throat before singing would qualify as a major financial transaction.

Our elders say that when you invite an elephant to your funeral, you must first establish whether it is coming to mourn or merely to eat the plantain. But apparently, in the modern entertainment business, the size of the elephant is more important than the duration of its visit.

And the elephant, having visited, may depart before the family finishes serving the first round of drinks.

The videos that followed were hardly the promotional material one would expect from a hotel anniversary celebration. Great Osama was reportedly seen confronting members of Davido's entourage, visibly displeased with how matters had unfolded. There were reports of instructions concerning the opening of the venue gate, and the internet promptly transformed the confrontation into a courtroom where everyone was simultaneously prosecutor, judge and entertainment lawyer.

One faction accused Davido of treating the occasion like a brief stopover at a fuel station. Another wondered whether Great Osama had failed to appreciate the complicated economics of international celebrity appearances. A third group, naturally, was interested only in calculating how much money the musician might have earned while blinking.

But the most important question remains unanswered: what exactly did the contract say?

If the agreement specified a 20-minute appearance, then Davido may well have delivered precisely what was purchased. If it promised a substantially longer concert, the matter becomes rather different. Until the contractual terms are established, nobody can responsibly declare that either party failed to honour its obligations.

Unfortunately, contractual caution is not a popular occupation on Ghanaian social media. Why wait for evidence when a calculator and an internet connection can produce a verdict before breakfast?

But there is another dimension to this extraordinary drama, and it concerns the Republic's complicated relationship with gold.

GTO We Care

Great Osama is chairman of the Amansie South Small-Scale Miners Association. That fact alone does not make him an illegal miner, and no responsible person should confuse legitimate small-scale mining with galamsey merely because both involve digging holes in the ground.

Nevertheless, the mining connection has given the public an irresistible opportunity to examine the relationship between natural resources and extravagant entertainment.

For years, Ghanaians have been debating what the country's mineral wealth should produce. Better roads? Improved schools? Modern hospitals? Sustainable livelihoods?

Now, somewhere in Manso, the national conversation has acquired a new item: the cost of importing 19 minutes of Nigerian musical excellence.

To be fair, Great Osama is entitled to spend his legitimately earned money as he pleases. He is a businessman, not the Minister of Finance, and nobody has appointed social media commentators as trustees of his bank account. Indeed, bringing an international superstar to a community outside Ghana's major entertainment centres is an achievement in its own right. Ghanaian rapper Amerado has reportedly praised him for precisely that reason.

But Ghanaians have also earned the right to ask questions, particularly when an entertainment spectacle begins to resemble a supplementary budget presentation.

Imagine what would happen if a district assembly announced that it had engaged a consultant for a reported GH¢7 million, only for the consultant to appear, greet the assembly members, deliver a 19-minute presentation and disappear into a waiting vehicle.

By sunset, three parliamentary committees would be demanding explanations, four radio stations would be broadcasting special investigations, and somebody would have petitioned the Office of the Special Prosecutor.

Yet when the consultant carries a microphone and sings in Afrobeats, the matter becomes an artistic misunderstanding.

Meanwhile, Ghanaian musicians have been observing the proceedings with understandable interest.

Shatta Wale reportedly questioned why Great Osama had not consulted him, referring to their previous working relationship. He even joked about being paid US$2 million to entertain patrons throughout the day.

One can almost hear the collective sigh from the local entertainment industry. For years, Ghanaian musicians have been campaigning for greater recognition and investment, only to discover that a visiting international superstar can allegedly command enough money in one evening to finance a respectable collection of domestic concerts.

Perhaps the lesson is that our musicians have been approaching the business from the wrong direction. Instead of negotiating fees per performance, they should consider introducing a mineral-based pricing formula. One ounce of gold for the opening song, two for the chorus and a negotiated concession for an encore.

At least the audience would know whether it was purchasing entertainment or prospecting rights.

And just when the public thought the drama had reached its conclusion, Great Osama reportedly referred the matter to his lawyers, explaining that he had been advised against further public commentary.

This is where the Republic becomes particularly interesting.

The musician has performed. The audience has reacted. The organiser has expressed dissatisfaction. The lawyers have entered the arena. And somewhere, presumably, there exists a contract that may eventually explain what everybody was supposed to receive.

Our elders say that when a man buys a talking drum, he must first agree with the drummer on how long the music will last. Otherwise, the drummer may collect his money, beat the drum three times and announce that the ancestors have called him home.

But in this particular encounter, the ancestors were not the problem. The stopwatch was.

Whether the dispute ends in reconciliation, compensation or a better understanding of celebrity contracts remains to be seen. What is already clear is that the people of Manso Akwasiso have acquired something no advertising agency could easily manufacture: nationwide publicity.

Before last Sunday, many Ghanaians would have struggled to locate Manso Akwasiso on a map. Today, the community has become a compulsory subject in the national curriculum of entertainment economics.

Great Osama may not have received the performance he expected, but his hotel has received publicity that money alone might have struggled to purchase.

Davido, meanwhile, has demonstrated why international stardom is such a fascinating business. Ordinary workers are paid according to hours spent on duty. International celebrities can apparently inspire nationwide arguments about the monetary value of a minute.

And that brings us to the final lesson.

In the Republic of Uncommon Sense, we have always believed that gold is extracted from the earth through hard work, machinery, sweat and considerable investment. But the events at Manso suggest that there may be another method, one requiring no excavator, no washing plant and no geological survey.

All one needs is a microphone, a global reputation and an organiser willing to pay the asking price.

The musician arrives. The music begins. The stopwatch runs. The audience cheers. The organiser reaches for his calculator.

And before the arithmetic is complete, the gold has apparently crossed the border.

Fellow Republicans, if the reported figures are true, Davido did not come to Manso to perform at a gold mine. He came to demonstrate that the most profitable mining concession in Ghana might be a 19-minute performance contract!

-

Jimmy Aglah writes for the Republic of Uncommon Sense, where common sense is a scarce commodity, absurdity is government policy, and irony is the only thing that never goes on strike.

Ghana News.title: Tourism Society, University of Ghana to host three-day youth festival
Ghana News.content:
The Tourism Society of Ghana, in collaboration with the University of Ghana, Legon, is set to host a three-day festival to promote youth participation in domestic tourism and the preservation of Ghanaian culture.

The 2026 Youth in Tourism Festival (YOTOFEST) will take place from Thursday, November 19 to Saturday, November 21, at the VIP Car Park of the University of Ghana Sports Stadium in Accra.

The festival, which will be held under the theme “My Culture, My Pride – The Role of the Youth in Promoting Domestic Tourism,” seeks to encourage young people to explore Ghana's tourism attractions, appreciate their cultural heritage and contribute to the growth of the tourism industry.

The organisers say the initiative will provide a platform for tourism education, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, entertainment and engagement between young people and industry players.

Activities lined up for the three-day event include a Tourism Summit, Campus Tourism Tour, Tourism Fair and Exhibition, Bajoo Night and a Health Walk.

The Tourism Summit will bring together students, academics, tourism professionals and other industry stakeholders to discuss opportunities for young people in the sector.

Discussions are expected to focus on tourism entrepreneurship, cultural preservation, destination marketing, innovation and career opportunities within the industry.

Participants will also have the opportunity to experience aspects of Ghana's tourism offerings through a Campus Tourism Tour featuring the Visit Ghana double-decker tourism bus.

The Tourism Fair and Exhibition will provide a platform for hotels, travel agencies, tour operators, tourism destinations, hospitality businesses and other industry players to showcase their products and services.

Bajoo Night will add an entertainment component to the festival, featuring music, cultural performances and youth creativity, while a health walk will promote physical fitness and healthy living.

This year's festival will also coincide with the 20th anniversary of the Tourism Society of Ghana, providing an opportunity to reflect on the organisation's contribution to tourism education, professional development and industry promotion over the past two decades.

The organisers say the festival is intended to strengthen domestic tourism by encouraging Ghanaians, particularly the youth, to explore local destinations and support businesses operating within the tourism value chain.

Ghana's cultural heritage, including traditional festivals, historic castles and forts, palaces, indigenous cuisine, music, dance and crafts, presents opportunities for tourism development and job creation.

However, the organisers believe that sustained growth in the sector will depend partly on the willingness of young people to appreciate, preserve and promote these resources.

Call for corporate support

Ahead of the festival, the Tourism Society of Ghana is calling on corporate organisations, financial institutions, telecommunications companies, airlines, hospitality businesses and development partners to support the initiative.

The organisers say corporate participation will offer businesses opportunities to engage young consumers, showcase their products, establish partnerships and contribute to youth development and cultural preservation.

Organisations are being invited to participate through various sponsorship and partnership arrangements, including title sponsorship, platinum, gold and silver sponsorships, as well as official, supporting and media partnerships.

The organisers also envisage the festival creating opportunities for mentorship, internships, skills development and tourism entrepreneurship beyond the three-day event.

They say the partnership with the University of Ghana provides an opportunity to strengthen collaboration between educational institutions, tourism businesses and young people.

The organisers are urging corporate Ghana and other stakeholders to support YOTOFEST 2026, describing it as an investment in youth development, cultural preservation and the future of Ghana's domestic tourism industry.

Ghana News.title: Parliament demands independent probe into Manso Keniago deaths
Ghana News.content:
Parliament’s Human Rights Committee has called for an independent, impartial and transparent investigation into the deadly confrontation between personnel of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) and residents of Manso Keniago in the Ashanti Region.

The incident, which occurred on November 11, 2026, in the Amansie South District, reportedly resulted in deaths and injuries, triggering concerns over the conduct of the anti-illegal mining operation.

In a press statement issued on November 17, the Committee, chaired by Ernest Yaw Anim, said it was particularly concerned about conflicting accounts surrounding the incident, including the reported use of firearms, the number of casualties and allegations of assault against traditional authorities and other community members.

It said the circumstances leading to the confrontation must be thoroughly investigated to establish the facts and determine whether the conduct of the personnel involved complied with the law and applicable standards governing the use of force by law enforcement officials.

The Committee further called for anyone found to have acted unlawfully to be held accountable, regardless of their official position or status, insisting that no individual should be shielded from accountability because they acted under official authority.

It also urged the authorities to preserve evidence, including firearms, ammunition records, operational orders, medical and post-mortem reports, photographs and video recordings, while ensuring that witnesses and affected families are protected from intimidation or reprisals.

The Committee said it would engage the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, NAIMOS, the Ghana Police Service and the Commission on Human Rights and Administrative Justice (CHRAJ) as part of its oversight responsibilities.

It stressed that although the government has a responsibility to fight illegal mining and protect the country’s natural resources, such operations must respect the Constitution, human dignity and the right to life.

“The fight against illegal mining must be pursued with determination, but never at the expense of the rule of law, human dignity and the sanctity of human life,” the statement said.

The Committee extended condolences to the bereaved families and wished injured persons a speedy recovery.

Ghana News.title: Knights and Ladies of Marshall celebrate 100 years of Catholic service and charity
Ghana News.content:
The Noble Order of the Knights and Ladies of Marshall is marking its 100th anniversary with a series of activities celebrating a century of commitment to the Catholic Church, charity and service to society.

The Order, which was established in Ghana on November 18, 1926, has since expanded beyond the country and supported religious, educational and community development initiatives.

Speaking on JoyNews’ AM Show on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, Past Supreme Knight, Sir Knight Brother Dr Peter Acquah, and Substantive Past Supreme Knight, Sir Knight Brother Anthony Kemavor, reflected on the organisation’s history and its contribution to the Church and society.

Mr Kemavor described the Knights of Marshall as “a group of Catholic men who are dedicated to the Catholic Church primarily, and of course their nations”.

He said the organisation had expanded from Ghana to Togo, Benin, Côte d’Ivoire, London, Sierra Leone and Liberia, with members supporting the Church and wider society through acts of charity.

According to him, members provide support to priests, seminaries and other Church institutions, while also promoting the teachings contained in papal encyclicals.

Dr Acquah described the Order’s 100-year journey as “very productive, successful, spiritually rewarding”.

He said its work had extended beyond the Catholic community, including outreach to young people through its junior councils.

He also highlighted the contribution of the organisation’s founding fathers to education, particularly their advocacy around the establishment of St Augustine’s College between 1926 and 1936.

Dr Acquah, an environmentalist, also used the interview to raise concerns about illegal mining, describing it as a national challenge that required urgent attention.

“It is an issue which we must address as a country, as a matter of urgency,” he said.

Mr Kemavor said preparations for the centenary celebrations began after the Order's 90th anniversary.

He disclosed that the organisation, through Marshallans Relief and Development Services, had invested approximately GH¢5.7 million in charitable activities.

The figure excludes projects undertaken directly by local councils and courts, he added.

As part of the centenary legacy, the Order will present a kindergarten project to the Diocese of Sekondi-Takoradi through the Bishop.

The celebrations begin on Wednesday, November 18, with a candlelight procession to St Paul's Cathedral, followed by a Mass in honour of the Order's 13 founding fathers.

The programme will also include a main anniversary ceremony expected to be attended by the Chief Justice and the Apostolic Nuncio.

A banquet and awards night are scheduled for Saturday, November 21, while a thanksgiving Mass will be held on Sunday, November 22, 2026.

In his concluding remarks, Dr Acquah reaffirmed the Order's commitment to “charity, fraternity, and service”.

“Charity is love, and God is love,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Parliamentary committee engages Northern chiefs on proposed Anti-Witchcraft Accusations Bill
Ghana News.content:
Parliament’s Human Rights Committee has engaged the Northern Regional House of Chiefs to seek traditional authorities’ support for the proposed Anti-Witchcraft Accusations Bill currently before Parliament.

The meeting formed part of the Committee’s advocacy efforts to raise awareness of the proposed legislation and strengthen collaboration with traditional leaders in tackling harmful witchcraft accusations and related practices.

Discussions focused on protecting the rights and dignity of vulnerable people, particularly women and older persons who are often targets of such accusations.

The Committee said the engagement was also intended to address harmful practices while encouraging traditional authorities to play an active role in safeguarding the rights of affected persons.

It expressed appreciation to the Northern Regional House of Chiefs for hosting the delegation and to Songtaba for facilitating the engagement.

The Committee said efforts to protect cultural heritage must go hand in hand with respect for human dignity and fundamental human rights.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
