Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good.

While Kyiv has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The timing of the strike comes at a significant moment, ahead of Putin meeting the leaders of China and the US. This could cloud his moment back in the spotlight.

The Crimean Bridge was built by Russia after it invaded and illegally annexed Ukraine's southern peninsula in 2014.

The $3.6bn (Â£2.7bn) piece of infrastructure is widely seen in Russia and Ukraine as Putin's personal pet project: His close tycoon friend Arkady Rotenberg built it, and then Putin personally opened it by driving a lorry over it in May 2018.

World.title: Philippines police ask prosecutors to charge Thomas Markle over child sex abuse material
World.content:
Police in the Philippines have asked prosecutors to charge Thomas Markle Sr, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, with possession of and intent to distribute child sexual abuse material.

Cebu province prosecutor Graeme Elmido told the BBC that police had filed documents requesting that Markle be charged on Monday.

Earlier this month, Markle, 82, was separately arrested and charged in the US with possession of child sexual abuse material. The FBI said agents seized about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books that they allege contained child sex abuse material, from storage units Markle rented.

Markle, who is in custody in the US, has previously denied the allegations. The BBC has contacted Markle's attorney for comment.

Elmido told the BBC that Philippine National Police had asked prosecutors to charge Markle with "two counts of intent to distribute CSAEM [child sexual abuse and exploitation material], and one count of possession of CSAEM material".

Last month, police in the Philippines obtained a warrant to examine devices allegedly removed from Markle's former home in the country.

Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old video tapes, were handed to officers by Meghan's half brother Thomas Markle Jr.

Earlier this month, Markle Sr was arrested and charged in the US. He had initially been placed under house detention at his assisted living facility in Florida, but was taken back into custody last week after prosecutors alleged he removed his ankle monitor.

Meghan Markle has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls.

In a previously shared statement after the allegations against her father emerged, Meghan wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."

She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".

Correction 18 November: An earlier version of this story said that police in the Philippines have charged Thomas Markle Sr with possession of and intent to distribute child sexual abuse material. The story has been updated to clarify that police have asked prosecutors to charge him with possession of and intent to distribute child sexual abuse material.

World.title: 'It was really scary': Mother describes sheltering during Russia strikes on Kyiv bridge
World.content:
The alarms warning of a ballistic missile threat went off just before 23:30 on Monday in Kyiv. Moments later came the boom of explosions.

Once again, the main bridges over the broad River Dnipro that cuts through the city were the target and this time the Russian missiles hit what they wanted.

Close to one end of the Pivnichnyi (Northern) bridge there is a large crater and in the pouring rain, water now rushes through it to the river below. Chunks of tarmac and metal are scattered around.

At its broadest point, the jagged hole is about eight metres wide.

The crossing is closed to all traffic apart from the occasional fire engine or police car passing at high speed. By contrast, nearby roads are jammed with cars and trucks, forced to take long detours.

Anyone in a hurry to move around this city has to walk, or cycle, across the bridge, picking their way through the wreckage. In the miserable weather, that also means getting very wet.

Masha and her family moved to a flat next to the bridge because they had been living by a power plant that kept getting hit by Russian missiles.

Last night, she was in the kitchen of their new place when the Russians struck the bridge. She thought her windows would be blown out of their frames by the explosions.

"It was really scary. We had no idea they'd hit here so much. It's like we're cursed," Masha told me, describing grabbing her child and running into the corridor for protection.

But somehow, she still managed to sound cheerful.

"It's difficult, but we're used to it. And we try to take the positive from everything. Like: we survived today! So we can be happy about that."

World.title: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
World.content:
A Palestinian woman in her 70s has been shot dead, and several other people wounded, in a village in the occupied West Bank where Israeli settlers recently moved in, the Palestinian health ministry says.

There are conflicting accounts of what happened. Local Palestinians said there was an attack by settlers in part of al-Duyuk al-Tahta, near Jericho, which is meant to be under the full control of the Palestinian Authority.

According to the Israeli army, there was a Palestinian car-ramming attack on an Israeli vehicle. It said rocks were then thrown at the Israelis, who opened fire in response. It did not mention the fatal shooting of a woman.

There have been high tensions in the area since a group of settlers recently set up a new outpost.

They moved into eight houses in the village on 4 November after buying them, they have said, in a secretive operation. The properties are in an area where Israel retains full security control.

All settlements are illegal under international law.

World.title: INEC pledges not to tamper with metadata of election results on IReV
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has pledged to preserve the metadata attached to election results uploaded to its Result Viewing Portal (IReV) during the 2027 general elections.

The commission’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, gave the assurance on Tuesday in Abuja during a stakeholder roundtable on election results tabulation organised by Yiaga Africa.

During the event, one participant from MundX analytics, an election observatory technology platform, asked about INEC’s preservation of the metadata for election results uploaded on IReV.

The participants expressed concern that the electoral commission may delete the metadata of uploaded results, which can make it difficult to track the circumstances surrounding their submission.

The Metadata attached to results uploaded to IReV can provide information such as the time a result was uploaded, the device used to upload it and the location from which the upload was made.

The participant cited findings from a review of results uploaded to IReV during previous elections, which allegedly identified instances of results uploaded before voting began.

According to the participant, some results were uploaded as early as 5 a.m. on election day, while multiple results were uploaded using the same mobile device.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The participant said such patterns raised concerns about possible irregularities and underscored the importance of preserving metadata to enable independent scrutiny of election results.

But the INEC Director of ICT, Mr Bayode, assured that the commission will not tamper with the raw data of the uploaded results.

“I can assure you those metadata will remain intact,” he replied.

Mr Bayode said he could not speak for previous elections, but said the commission still has the metadata for the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Ekiti and Osun elections.

According to him, the results uploaded during those elections showed greater consistency, with no discrepancies identified on the portal.

World.title: Why Enugu Government wants National Sports Festival postponed
World.content:
Enugu State has formally requested a postponement of the 23rd National Sports Festival, seeking to move the competition from its scheduled 26 November to 11 December, 2026 dates to the first week of May 2027 over concerns about the readiness of key sporting facilities.

The request was made by the Enugu State Ministry of Youth and Sports in conjunction with the Local Organising Committee (LOC) following an assessment of facilities at the Nnamdi Azikiwe Stadium and Awgu Games Village, which are central to the successful hosting of the national sporting event.

The National Sports Commission (NSC) is yet to make a decision on the proposed change of dates.

In a statement signed by LOC Media Officer Brian Okechukwu on behalf of the committee, the organisers explained that the request followed an internal inspection aimed at determining whether the facilities would be ready to accommodate athletes and officials before the scheduled start of the festival.

According to the statement, although the contractors handling the projects had expressed confidence in meeting the original completion deadlines, the level of work outstanding raised concerns about whether the facilities would satisfy the required standards in time for the competition.

“Although the contractors handling the projects expressed confidence that the facilities would be completed within the expected timeframe, the Enugu State Ministry of Youth and Sports and the LOC, after a careful assessment, observed that the level of work remaining raised concerns about the readiness of the stadium and Awgu Games Village to meet the required standards before the commencement of the Games,” the statement read.

The full statement

However, the organisers maintained that preparations outside the sporting infrastructure were progressing well, disclosing that accommodation and other logistical arrangements were already in place.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Commissioner for Youth and Sports and LOC Chairman, Lloyd Ikechukwu Ekweremadu, said shifting the festival to May 2027 would give the state sufficient time to complete the outstanding projects and ensure that the facilities are delivered to the expected standards.

The committee also disclosed that zonal eliminations had been concluded, with preparations now underway for the closed-camping phase ahead of the festival.

Despite the proposed adjustment to the calendar, Enugu State reaffirmed its commitment to delivering a successful edition of the National Sports Festival, stressing that the additional preparation time would help guarantee proper sporting facilities, adequate safety measures and seamless coordination.

The organisers insisted that the decision was driven by the desire to provide athletes, officials, spectators and other stakeholders with a memorable experience rather than compromise the quality of the competition by proceeding with facilities that may not be fully ready.

“The postponement is aimed at ensuring that Enugu State delivers a world-class National Sports Festival characterised by adequate sporting facilities, the highest standards of safety, effective coordination and a memorable experience for athletes, officials, spectators and other stakeholders from across the country,” the statement added.

History of postponement

The National Sports Festival has a long history of postponements, with uncertainty over hosting dates repeatedly disrupting its biennial schedule.

The last edition tagged the Gateway Games and hosted by Ogun State, suffered at least two postponements before eventually taking place from 16 to 30 May 2025.

Initially scheduled for November 2024, the festival was first moved to 12–26 January 2025 in May 2024 by the then Minister of Sports Development, John Enoh. However, in December 2024, the National Sports Commission announced another shift to May 2025 following technical assessments that identified the need for further facility improvements and better event preparations.

World.title: First Lady’s food relief reaches vulnerable Akwa Ibom residents
World.content:
The Renewed Hope Initiative (RHI), on Monday, distributed food items to vulnerable households in Akwa Ibom State under its Food Outreach Scheme.

The initiative, championed by the First Lady Oluremi Tinubu, reaffirmed its commitment to supporting vulnerable Nigerians through sustained humanitarian interventions.

Mrs Tinubu, represented by the Wife of the Vice-President, Nana Shettima, said the scheme was designed to provide nutritional relief to disadvantaged groups.

She said the programme, inaugurated in March 2024, targeted persons with disabilities, widows and other vulnerable groups to strengthen family well-being across Nigeria.

“The Food Outreach Scheme was launched in March 2024 to provide direct nutritional relief to persons with disabilities, widows and other vulnerable groups, thereby strengthening the well-being of families across Nigeria,” she said.

She said the programme had received consistent support from partners committed to supplying two truckloads of food items to RHI monthly.

“Through this steady support, two states benefit from the programme monthly.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We have so far successfully distributed food items to 32 states and the Federal Capital Territory,” she said.

She identified the Abdul Samad Rabiu Africa Initiative (ASR Africa) as the donor of the food consignment distributed in Akwa Ibom.

The First Lady appreciated ASR Africa and another partner, who preferred anonymity, for their generosity and commitment to supporting vulnerable Nigerians.

“Our goal as RHI, as an umbrella of compassion and empowerment, is to complement the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu.

“We are doing so by ensuring that every Nigerian has the support required to thrive, irrespective of status or circumstance,” she said.

Commendation for Gov Eno

Mrs Tinubu also commended Governor Umo Eno of Akwa Ibom State for his hospitality and the Coordinator of the Office of the First Lady of Akwa Ibom for implementing RHI programmes.

Eno, represented by his deputy, Akon-Etim Eyakenyi, commended the First Lady for prioritising the welfare of vulnerable Nigerians.

He said the state had constructed more than 500 compassionate homes for vulnerable residents, with each beneficiary receiving N500,000 to establish a small business.

According to him, more than 600 elderly citizens receive N50,000 monthly on a rotational basis, while residents aged 65 and above enjoy free healthcare services.

Earlier, the Coordinator, Office of the First Lady of Akwa Ibom, Helen Eno-Obareki, said 500 vulnerable households would benefit from the food outreach programme.

She described the intervention as a demonstration of empathy, purposeful governance and shared humanity, aimed at providing relief, dignity and hope to disadvantaged families.

She said RHI had supported 750 elderly citizens with financial assistance and provided business grants to 1,000 petty traders across the state.

According to her, 750 persons with disabilities had also received empowerment grants, while 500 women benefited from business capitalisation support.

She said the support was provided under the RHI-Tony Elumelu Foundation Women Economic Empowerment Programme.

The coordinator added that another 500 women received business tools and equipment, while 200 women and young people benefited from agricultural training and start-up support.

She urged stakeholders to ensure transparency, fairness and accountability in distributing the food items, particularly to widows, elderly citizens and persons with disabilities.

Ubon Udoh, managing director of ASR Africa, reaffirmed the organisation’s commitment to sustainable development through investments in health, education and social development.

He said the organisation committed $100 million annually to development interventions, with $50 million allocated to Nigeria and the remainder to other African countries.

Mr Udoh said ASR Africa currently has 84 projects in Nigeria and 16 across the African continent.

“Partnerships are the only way that we can expand our impact, expand the scope of what we’re doing, and pool our resources together to make the real kind of difference,” he said.

(NAN)

World.title: EDITORIAL: Safeguarding the electoral process from compromise
World.content:
From “hanging chads” to “mail-in ballots”, even in the most sophisticated democracies, it does not take much (whether through accidents or by deliberate actions) to bring the electoral process into disrepute. It is sad, therefore, that barely eight weeks before the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) conduct of the January/February 2027 general elections, a sense of foreboding about the elections should have been triggered by the intrusion of Artificial Intelligence (AI), and a slew of appointments and transfers of personnel at INEC.

In the wake of public complaints over irregularities in INEC’s preliminary display of the voters’ register on 9 and 15 October, follow-up investigations by the commission revealed that AI was used by some of its officials to generate the profiles of fake voters in the register during the 2025/2026 Continuous Voter Registration exercise. According to INEC’s Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, subsequent technical reviews of the register resulted in the removal of 1,608,660 such voters, most of which consisted of the dead and duplicated names. A total of fifty-four officials across ten states of the country have been identified as complicit in the breach.

By admitting to this snafu, and through the decision to begin a mock assessment of its accreditation system and electronic transmission of results on 28 November, Mr Amupitan does the country and its electoral institutions a great service. But it is no less important to ensure that results from over-voting would no longer be transmitted to the IReV, as happened during the 2023 elections, than it is to ensure that staff responsible for conduct that might bring elections into disrepute are not just punished, but are seen to be so sanctioned.

The country’s past problems with the credibility of elections, and their inflammation of the public trust deficit, make it imperative that the commission heaves as closely as it can to the letter and spirit of its enabling statutes, and the laws of the land. Yet not all that is legal is expedient. PREMIUM TIMES is accordingly worried by the optics around President Bola Tinubu’s appointment of Professor Mustapha Aliu as National Electoral Commissioner in charge of the North-west states of Sokoto, Zamfara, Kebbi, Jigawa, Kano, Katsina and Kaduna. Given that this zone holds the key to victory in any presidential election, with its consideration as the highest vote bank in the country, it matters a lot that the new INEC commissioner is a brother to Governor Ahmed Aliu of Sokoto State.

INEC’s redeployment of Oluyemi Adeyemi-Showunmi, an administrative secretary, from its Lagos office to its headquarters in Abuja, where she will oversee the commission’s operations, likewise threatens expedience (in this case, the need to ensure that our elections are accepted as free and fair, before, during and after the polls) in favour of what the law permits. Should it matter that Mrs Adeyemi-Showunmi is the wife of Segun Showunmi, a member of the APC Presidential Campaign Council and outspoken supporter of President Tinubu?

Should Mrs Showunmi’s professional competence and career suffer in order to convey the sense of a properly run election? A big part of the problems with these questions lies with the governance of the electoral process. We worry that an arrangement that allows a participant in an election, in this case the president, to be the sole authority in appointing the INEC Chairman and the 12 other members of his administrative team might not conduce to engendering a sense of impartiality on the part of the appointor, nor assure the integrity of the electoral process.

We at PREMIUM TIMES insist that Section 63 (2) of the Electoral Act 2026 is at odds with reason and optimism for the conduct of a credible election in 2027. This section empowers a returning officer to accept and declare ballot papers without official marks or the stamp of INEC, if the officer is satisfied that they are from the book of ballot papers furnished to the Presiding Officer. It is a clear window for the manipulation of votes.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Still, all of this is to cavil. Even if the will were there, we do not have enough time to change these provisions of the law. And it is doubtful if a change in the rules midstream would not have the exact effect of impugning the entire process. Mr Amupitan has one task and only one task: to organise free and fair elections next year. Surely, it cannot be too much to demand that he does this well.

World.title: 140 UNIBEN graduates earn 1st class honours
World.content:
A total of 140 undergraduates of the University of Benin (UNIBEN) have earned First-Class Honours as the institution prepares to graduate 11,357 students at its 2025/2026 convocation.

Edoba Omoregie, vice-chancellor of UNIBEN, disclosed this on Tuesday in Benin at a pre-convocation news conference.

Mr Omoregie, a professor, explained that 8,789 undergraduates and 2,568 postgraduate students would receive various degrees.

“The Senate of the university has found the 8,789 undergraduate graduands worthy in character and learning to be awarded their first degrees.

“140 undergraduates earned First-Class Honours, 2589 obtained Second-Class Honour, Upper Division, 4465 Second-Class Lower and 513 Third-Class degrees,” he said

The vice-chancellor said no student would be awarded a pass degree.

Mr Omoregie disclosed that 484 of the postgraduate students had earned doctoral degrees, while 44 would receive Master of Philosophy degrees.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The postgraduate category also comprised 1,409 master’s degree recipients and 631 postgraduate diploma graduands.

The vice-chancellor said the university would also confer honorary doctorate degrees on three distinguished alumni and award the title of professor emeritus to a retired professor.

Recorded achievements

Mr Omoregie described the 2025/2026 academic session as peaceful and successful, attributing the achievement to commitment of the university’s stakeholders.

On academic development, he said all 34 programmes presented for accreditation during the session received full accreditation.

He added that the university’s Doctor of Veterinary Medicine programme had been restored and accredited by the National Universities Commission.

Mr Omoregie said the institution had expanded from 17 faculties when he assumed office to 22, alongside the establishment of five centres and institutes.

“In less than two years in office, we have introduced a lot of innovation in line with best global practices in order to reposition the University of Benin as one of the best academic, if not the best academic institution in this country,” he said.

He also highlighted the university’s digital transformation efforts, particularly the development of an in-house student information management portal.

According to him, the portal manages the records of certificate, diploma, undergraduate and postgraduate students and supports transcript processing.

He said the initiative had reduced the university’s dependence on external service providers and improved the management of academic records.

According to him, convocation activities will begin on 24 November with an interfaith service and the Founder’s Day lecture.

The lecture, titled: “The Wealth Beneath Our Feet and the Wealth Within Our Minds: Rethinking Leadership, Education, and National Development,” will be delivered by an alumnus and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan.

He said the convocation lecture, scheduled for 26 November, will be delivered by Attahiru Jega, a professor and former chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission and special adviser to the President Bola Tinubu on Presidential Livestock Reform.

According to him, the lecture is titled: “Reinvigoration and Revitalisation of the Nigerian University System: What Is to Be Done?”

The vice-chancellor thanked the university’s staff, students, alumni and other stakeholders for their contributions to its development.

(NAN)

World.title: Bank official testifies on N500m disbursements from ONSA account to private company during Dasuki’s tenure
World.content:
A bank manager told the FCT High Court in Abuja on Tuesday that the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) sent N500 million to a private company while Sambo Dasuki was in charge of the office.

Obazele Anthony, the fourth prosecution witness presented by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), said Real Properties Investment Limited (RPIL) received “N500 million from NSA” on 20 November 2014.

Mr Dasuki served as NSA between 2012 and 2015, at the height of Boko Haram attacks in Nigeria’s North-east, during the administration of then-President Goodluck Jonathan.

The EFCC accused him, along with former Sokoto State Governor Attahiru Bafarawa, his son Sagir Bafarawa, former Minister of State for Finance Bashir Yuguda, and Dalhatu Investment Limited, of N19.4 billion in arms-procurement fraud.

Since 2015, Mr Dasuki and his co-defendants have been facing 25 counts of misappropriation, criminal breach of trust and receiving stolen property.

The charges accuse them of diverting N19.4 billion from the NSA office’s account. The money was said to be meant for procurement of arms to firm up the offensive against Boko Haram terrorists during former President Goodluck Jonathan administration, between 2014 and 2015.

This case is one of the twin indictments Mr Dasuki is facing before separate judges of the FCT High Court regarding his management of the arms procurement funds.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He and his co-defendants in the two cases denied the allegations.

Utilisation of N500 million

Led in evidence by EFCC’s lawyer Rotimi Jacobs, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), on Tuesday, Mr Anthony narrated the utilisation of the N500 million transferred into Real Properties Investment Limited by ONSA.

The company transferred N1.5 million to an individual identified as “Alhaji Mutiu Idowu”, N7.5 million to Kalaks Investment Limited, N1 million to Real Oil Mills and N140,000 to Adekola Adeoye.

Similarly, it also sent N10 million to Mr Idowu, N100 million to Senator Rashidi Ladoja, N250 million to Meristem Wealth Management Limited and a fixed deposit of N100 million.

Mr Ladoja is a former governor of Oyo State, was a Third Republic senator and is the present Olubadan of Ibadan. Details of his connection to the case remains sketchy at the current stage of the prosecution’s case.

Witness not privy to transactions’ purpose

Defence lawyers – A.O. Ayodele for Mr Yuguda, A.A. Usman for Mr Dasuki and James Olatoke, a SAN, for the Bafarawas – took turn to cross-examine the witness.

The witness confirmed during the rounds of question that the bank did not flag the transactions as suspicious.

The prosecution witness, who maintained that he neither worked with ONSA nor knew the purpose of the transactions, said the payments to the individuals and firms listed were not on the authority of the NSA.

He confirmed that he was not the compliance officer, did not author the documents EFCC presented in court, and was not involved in any of the transactions.

He named the compliance officers who signed the Real Properties Investment Limited account statement. He said the officials were still alive.

The witness also confirmed that “somebody signed on behalf of some of the compliance officers,” whose names were listed on the documents.

He also noted that Mr Bafarawa was not a beneficiary of any of the transactions.

Thereafter, the witness was discharged, and the trial judge, Yusuf Halilu, adjourned the case until 15 December.

World.title: Heirs Holding to play leading role to play key role at inaugural West Africa Integration and Investment Summit
World.content:
Heirs Holdings, the pan-African investment group founded by African investor and philanthropist Tony O Elumelu, will play a leading role at the inaugural West Africa Integration and Investment Summit (WAIIS 2026), taking place 16-18 November in Sierra Leone.

As a Principal Partner of the Summit, the Group is bringing its senior business leadership, investment expertise and extensive operating experience across critical sectors of the African economy to advance the region’s integration and investment agenda.

Mr Elumelu, Group Chairman of Heirs Holdings and a member of the Summit’s Private Sector Advisory Board, is leading private sector mobilisation for the event, convened under the leadership of His Excellency Julius Maada Bio, President of Sierra Leone.

He will be joined by senior executives from across the Group’s portfolio, including Obong Idiong, CEO of Heirs Technologies, who will speak at the Investment Opportunity Session on connecting West Africa’s markets through payments, data and digital networks and Peter Ikenga, CEO of Transcorp Power, who will co-chair the power session alongside Mamadou Sangafowa-Coulibaly, Côte d’Ivoire’s Minister of Mines, Oil and Energy.

The Summit brings together African Heads of State, policymakers, institutional investors, development finance institutions and business leaders to accelerate economic integration and unlock investment opportunities across West Africa.

A longstanding advocate of Africapitalism and a business turnaround expert, Elumelu champions the principle that Africa’s development must be driven by African entrepreneurs and businesses, with long-term private investment creating both economic and social wealth. His leadership at WAIIS reflects a conviction that regional integration must move beyond policy commitments to practical commercial partnerships, cross-border investment and the development of competitive African enterprises.

Heirs Holdings’ prominent role at WAIIS is reinforced by its scale, investment footprint and track record of building businesses across sectors critical to Africa’s economic transformation. As of 31 March 2026, the value of its portfolio companies stood at approximately US$15.08 billion. With investments and operations spanning 24 countries and a workforce of more than 40,000 people across the Group and its portfolio companies, Heirs Holdings is a significant pan-African private-sector investment platform.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

For Heirs Holdings, West African integration represents a significant opportunity to expand the region’s economic potential and attractiveness to investors. A more connected region creates larger markets, strengthens intra-regional trade, facilitates the movement of capital, attracts investment, creates jobs, and enables African businesses to achieve greater scale and compete more effectively in the global economy.

As governments, investors and business leaders convene in Sierra Leone, Heirs Holdings reaffirms its commitment to working with public and private sector partners to turn regional integration into a commercial reality that will create lasting economic and social value across the continent.

Heirs Holdings is a leading pan-African investment company. Its investment portfolio spans the energy, power, banking, insurance and financial services, technology, real estate, hospitality and healthcare sectors, operating in twenty-four countries worldwide.

Heirs Holdings is inspired by Africapitalism, the belief that the private sector is the key enabler of economic and social wealth creation in Africa. Driven by this philosophy, Heirs Holdings invests for the long-term, bringing strategic capital, sector expertise, a track record of business success, and operational excellence to its portfolio companies.

World.title: Tinubu campaigns in Kebbi, approves dry port as ex-governors declare support
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu on Tuesday approved the full operationalisation of the Tsamiya Inland Dry Port in Kebbi, describing the facility as strategic towards boosting the state’s economy.

He also thanked the people of the state for their massive turnout and warm reception during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at the Haliru Abdu Multi Purpose Stadium in Birnin Kebbi. President Tinubu said he would not take their support and confidence for granted.

One of the campaign’s highlights was former governors declaring they would work for President Tinubu’s re-election because he supported the state in times of need.

The former governors are Adamu Aleiro, Sai’du Dankingari and Minister of Budget and Economic Planning Atiku Bagudu.

The president reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to complete ongoing landmark infrastructure projects, especially the Illela-Badagry Superhighway, which passes through Kebbi, as well as other federal road networks within Kebbi State.

He commended Kebbi State Governor Nasir Idris for complementing the federal government’s road-construction efforts and promised to expand the state’s agricultural programmes.

“We will expand the existing agricultural programmes. We will support rice mills in Birnin Kebbi, Argungu, Bagudo and Yauri.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We will ensure that the Zuru–Rijau Road is actualised, while the Koko–Dabai road will soon be completed through the Kebbi State Government platform. We will rehabilitate the Goronyo–Argungu irrigation scheme and the Zauro Polder Project so that your farmers can farm year-round,” the president said.

On security, President Tinubu pledged to strengthen further the national security architecture and support sub-nationals’ capacity to fight crime by signing the state police bill into law.

“We are mindful of the challenges in Zuru, Danko/Wasagu, Sakaba, Bagudo, Arewa, Shanga and some parts of Maiyama. We shall work together to end insecurity.

“In the meantime, we have deployed more troops to the state. We have provided more equipment to the military and police. We have approved new operating bases in Zuru, Bagudo and Yauri.

“By the grace of God, the days of bandits terrorising our innocent farmers are numbered, as we step up efforts to ensure that no farmer in Kebbi will be afraid to go to his farm again,” the president assured.

He further stated his administration’s determination to ensure peaceful elections while thanking APC leadership, supporters, and residents of Birnin Kebbi for their solidarity and impressive turnout.

In his remarks, Vice President Kashim Shettima reminded the audience of the support President Tinubu gave to late former President Muhammadu Buhari, enabling him to consolidate and win the 2015 presidential election.

He urged the northern voters to reciprocate the gesture.

The vice president told the gathering that President Tinubu sacrificed his resources and comfort to give the North what it wished in 2015. He also thanked the North for giving the president 60.2 per cent of the votes that gave the APC victory in 2023.

“The North repaid that kindness, and we are even more grateful that you are prepared to do the same in the coming election in January because you have rejected the lies, the distortions, the half-truths.

Earlier, the host governor, Nasir Idris, commended the president for graciously approving his request to fully operationalise the Kebbi Inland Dry Port and other critical road projects in the state.

Governor Idris assured the president of their support towards his re-election bid as a mark of appreciation for his support for the state’s socio-economic development.

The APC National Chairman, Nentawe Yilwatda, commended some guests’ testimonies on President Tinubu’s commitment to infrastructure development in the country, especially in education, health, and security.

He assured the president that the North has resolved to support his re-election in 2027.

AbdulAziz Yari, the director-general of the APC Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), thanked Kebbi residents for the massive turnout and commended the president for his massive investment in the state’s economy.

Mr Yari urged Kebbi residents to come out en masse and vote for the president in the forthcoming 2027 general elections.

He said the creation of the Federal Ministry of Livestock Development was deliberate, aimed at addressing farmer-herder clashes in the north and supporting the ongoing construction of the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, designed to ease traffic along the corridor in line with the vision of Nigeria’s founding fathers.

Mr Yari urged voters to disregard the deceitful voices of the opposition parties.

The Kebbi APC Presidential campaign rally was attended by First Lady Oluremi Tinubu, Governors Uba Sani of Kaduna, Dauda Lawal of Zamfara, Mala Buni of Yobe, Babagana Zulum of Borno and Ahmad Aliyu of Sokoto.

Others include Speaker of the House of Representatives Tajudeen Abbas; Senators Adams Oshiomhole and Ali Sheriff; Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning Doris Uzoka-Anite; Minister of Housing Muttaqha Darma; and former governors Ahmed Yerima of Zamfara, Ibrahim Shema of Katsina, and Abdullahi Ganduje.

The APC campaign train has continued to criss-cross the country, engaging party stakeholders and Nigerians across the six geopolitical zones.

Bayo Onanuga

Special Adviser to the President

(Information & Strategy)

November 17, 2026

World.title: Barau, Atiku, others mourn late Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
World.content:
Femi Ajasa

By Henry Umoru & Olasunkanmi Akoni

ABUJA—THE presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar; Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin (APC, Kano North) has mourned the passing of Mr. Olufemi Ajasa, the Online Editor of Vanguard Newspapers.

Also, Chairman of Ikeja Local Government Area, Lagos, Akeem Dauda, mourned the death of Mr. Ajasa, describing his passing as a painful loss to the media industry and the journalism profession.

Ajasa passed away on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital, LUTH, after a brief illness at the age of 44, according to the management of Vanguard Media Limited, publishers of the Vanguard Newspapers.

Ajasa’s death painful loss to journalism, Vanguard — Atiku mourns

Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has described the death of Vanguard Media Limited’s Online Editor, Olufemi Ajasa, as a painful loss to the journalism profession and the media organisation, extending his condolences to the management, staff and family of the deceased.

Atiku, in a condolence message on his X handle on Tuesday, expressed sadness over Ajasa’s death at the age of 44, saying his passing was a reminder of how suddenly a life devoted to work, family and service could be cut short.

He wrote: “Ajasa’s passing is a deep loss to @vanguardngrnews and to the journalism profession. Behind every story published and every deadline met is a commitment to keeping the public informed.

“His colleagues have lost a valued teammate, the media community a respected professional, and his family a beloved son, husband, father and brother.”

Atiku also extended his condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the newspaper’s Editor, Eze Anaba, and everyone who knew and worked with the late journalist.

“I extend my heartfelt condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, Editor Eze Anaba, and all who loved and worked with him,” the statement added.

Memories

“May the memories they shared bring comfort in this difficult hour, and may God grant his family strength to bear this immeasurable loss”, he wrote. In a condolence message by his spokesperson, Ismail Mudashir, Senator Barau described the late Ajasa as a thoroughbred professional and one of the finest minds in Nigeria’s digital journalism space.

He said: “Femi Ajasa’s dedication and commitment to truth and accuracy set him apart and distinguished him among others. His death is a painful loss, not only to his immediate family, the Vanguard family, but to the entire Nigerian media industry.”

He noted that Mr. Ajasa’s journalism journey, which began as a photojournalist with the National Mirror in 2012, through TheNewsGuru and Pulse, to his return to Vanguard in June 2022 as Online Editor, was marked by excellence, integrity and selfless service to the country through his noble profession, journalism.

Senator Barau extended his heartfelt condolences to the Ajasa family of Ajido, Badagry, Lagos State, Management and Staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the Journalists union and all his friends and professional associates.

“We pray that God will grant his family, colleagues and loved ones the strength and fortitude to bear this irreparable loss, and grant his gentle soul eternal rest,” he said.

On his part, Dauda said the late journalist’s dedication, professionalism and contributions to the growth of digital journalism would remain part of his enduring legacy.

He noted that Ajasa was a committed media professional whose career journey, spanning several reputable media organisations, reflected his passion for journalism, commitment to excellence and determination to advance the evolving media landscape.

Dauda particularly commiserated with the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the immediate family of the deceased, his friends and professional colleagues over the irreparable loss.

“Take solace in the impactful life and professional contributions of the late Ajasa, whose passing at the age of 44 is a painful reminder of the fragility of life,” he stated.

Dauda also prayed that Almighty God would comfort the bereaved family, grant them the strength to bear the irreparable loss and grant the departed journalist eternal rest.

Vanguard News

World.title: Nvidia says no return for ousted CEO, reports revenue boom
World.content:
(FILES) Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Photo by Philip FONG / AFP

US chip giant Nvidia on Tuesday ruled out any comeback for ousted CEO Jensen Huang, who was forced out in a spy scandal, and reported that it had doubled revenue in the third quarter to more than $115 billion, beating expectations.

Huang sought to be reinstated despite resigning last week over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, but his successor — interim CEO Colette Kress — said that it was now “business as usual” at the company as it charts a way ahead without him.

Harvey Jones, the chair of the company’s board, said in an earnings call that “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.”

Investors scoured the upbeat results for evidence that the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the Nvidia crisis, which highlighted a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies.

“Our momentum is real. Nvidia is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” Kress said in her first remarks since being appointed by the board last week.

She forecast stronger revenue growth of 75 percent in next fiscal year, up from 70 percent.

Huang’s bid on Tuesday to get his job back was the latest twist for the company at the center of an AI boom that has propelled markets to record highs and boosted global economic growth.

The recent upheaval has battered shares of Nvidia — which has lost $700 billion in market value since the scandal broke — and Huang is to be questioned by US lawmakers on December 1 over national security concerns.

A charismatic promoter of AI, his fall triggered immediate calls from Elon Musk and others for his return, and even President Donald Trump said he “would not mind” seeing Huang back at Nvidia, downplaying the espionage allegations.

– Battle over AI chips –

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said, hours before the earnings release.

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

As the spy scandal deepened, Washington on Monday announced new restrictions on AI chip exports, drawing condemnation from Beijing.

The new US export curbs and the wider Nvidia scandal risk casting a shadow over talks between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, which starts this week in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

Under Washington’s new rules, data centers anywhere in the world will need a US license to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under US arms embargoes.

The rules also require licenses to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil — countries the US Commerce Department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion” of the chips.

The changes are a response to a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on US hardware not available for export to China.

While the loophole has been known to authorities, the revelation of Huang’s affair has drawn intense scrutiny to the practice.

His lover Alice Huang, who is not related to the 63-year-old, is a former executive of Megaspeed — a Singapore-based cloud computing firm under US criminal investigation for allegedly helping Chinese companies procure advanced Nvidia AI chips in circumvention of export controls.

Investors are watching for signs of whether Kress will slow Huang’s aggressive investment strategy, which saw him commit tens of billions of dollars to AI companies.

Huang on Tuesday sounded a note of contrition in his statement, saying “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life.”

World.title: Kwara APC Reps candidate unveils people-centred agenda
World.content:
APC House of Representatives for Ifelodun/Offa/Oyun federal constituency in 2027 election Dr Rafiu Ajakaye flanked by Chairman of Kwara NUJ Correspondents’ Chapel Biola Azeez of Nigerian Tribune on the left and his Deputy Ibrahim Alege on Tuesday after the News Keg Program

…Says serving as AbdulRazaq’s CPS was greatest privilege

By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin

ILORIN — The All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Ifelodun/Offa/Oyun Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives election, Dr Rafiu Ajakaye, has unveiled a legislative agenda focusing on security, education, youth employment, women’s economic empowerment and rural development.

Ajakaye, a former Chief Press Secretary to Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, said his aspiration to represent the constituency was driven by a desire to provide accessible and effective leadership rather than pursue personal ambition.

He stated this on Tuesday while speaking on the News Keg programme organised by the Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) at its secretariat in Ilorin.

Presenting his manifesto titled, “Manifesto of Purpose: A Covenant with the People of Ifelodun/Offa/Oyun Federal Constituency”, Ajakaye described his service as the governor’s spokesperson as a major privilege in his professional career.

“Serving as the Chief Press Secretary to Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq was one of the greatest privileges of my life,” he said.

He described public office as a responsibility that should be directed towards improving people’s lives.

Ajakaye cited his involvement in the 2021, 2024 and 2025 teachers’ recruitment exercises under the AbdulRazaq administration as an experience that reinforced his belief in merit-based employment opportunities.

According to him, the exercises demonstrated the importance of involving the right people in recruitment processes to ensure fairness and create opportunities for qualified applicants.

“Leadership is not about occupying an office. It is about inspiring hope, solving problems, expanding opportunities, and shaping a future in which every citizen can live with dignity,” he said.

The candidate, who hails from Alabe community in Ifelodun Local Government Area, said his background, academic training and professional experience had shaped his approach to governance and public service.

He said his experience as a journalist, public relations practitioner and public servant, particularly his years as the governor’s spokesperson, had exposed him to policymaking and the importance of transparency, competence and integrity in governance.

On security, Ajakaye identified banditry and kidnapping as major concerns affecting rural communities, saying the activities had disrupted livelihoods and economic activities.

He pledged to advocate stronger legislative oversight of security agencies, improved welfare and equipment for security personnel, intelligence-led operations and community-based security strategies.

He identified insecurity in parts of Ifelodun Local Government Area as a major priority, promising to make it the foremost issue on his legislative agenda if elected.

“Security is number one on my legislative agenda. I understand the pains of my people because that is where I come from, If elected, I will champion stronger legislative oversight of security agencies,” he said.

On education, the APC candidate said he would advocate reforms to align the country’s education system with technological developments and labour market demands.

He identified science, technical, vocational and digital education as areas requiring greater attention.

Addressing youth unemployment, Ajakaye promised to support legislation that would promote entrepreneurship, improve access to finance for small businesses, strengthen vocational training and encourage young people to embrace agriculture.

On women’s economic empowerment, he said he would pursue policies to support women-owned businesses through affordable financing, cooperative initiatives, improved market access and sustainable income-generating opportunities.

He also pledged to promote rural infrastructure, agricultural modernisation, small business development and improved public services, insisting that development should extend to every ward and community in the constituency.

World.title: Matawalle’s support group targets release of 2,000 inmates
World.content:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto

SOKOTO — The Tinubu Again Movement (TAM), a political support group associated with the Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, has announced plans to facilitate the release of 2,000 inmates in Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states through the payment of court-imposed fines and other lawful interventions.

The proposed initiative is aimed at assisting indigent inmates whose continued detention is linked to their inability to pay fines and those eligible for release under applicable laws.

The group announced the plan on Tuesday during its participation in the presidential campaign rally of President Bola Tinubu in Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State.

Hundreds of its members participated in the rally, wearing branded outfits and carrying banners bearing the images of Tinubu, Vice-President Kashim Shettima and Matawalle.

The supporters also marched through major streets of the state capital, expressing support for the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Speaking on the proposed intervention, TAM spokesman, Mallam Yusuf Dingyadi, said the initiative was designed to assist deserving inmates who could not secure their release because of financial constraints.

He said the movement would identify eligible beneficiaries and work towards settling outstanding fines in accordance with the law.

“Our intention is to facilitate the release of 2,000 inmates across Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states by identifying deserving cases and assisting those whose continued detention is linked to their inability to pay relatively small fines.

“We believe that imprisonment should not become a permanent barrier to rebuilding one’s life, particularly for individuals who qualify for release under the law but remain in correctional facilities because of their financial circumstances,” Dingyadi said.

He added that the intervention was intended to support family reunification and the reintegration of eligible former inmates into society.

Dingyadi also disclosed that the movement was planning humanitarian interventions for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and other vulnerable communities across the three states.

According to him, the proposed programmes would include the distribution of food, clothing and other essential relief materials, as well as empowerment initiatives.

“We are equally concerned about the humanitarian challenges confronting internally displaced persons in Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states. We intend to support them through the provision of foodstuffs, clothing and empowerment opportunities to cushion their hardships and restore their dignity,” he said.

On the proposed inmate-release programme, Dingyadi said the group would engage relevant correctional authorities, judicial institutions and other stakeholders to identify eligible beneficiaries and ensure compliance with existing laws.

He stressed that the initiative was not intended to interfere with judicial decisions but to support lawful processes for the release of inmates who had met the relevant conditions for discharge.

Beyond the humanitarian initiative, the TAM spokesman said the group’s participation in the Kebbi rally reflected its commitment to grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027.

He said the movement planned to expand its political activities across the North-West through engagements with communities and political stakeholders.

If implemented, the proposed intervention could provide relief to affected inmates and their families, while drawing attention to the challenges faced by indigent persons unable to meet court-imposed financial obligations.

World.title: Immigration vows to fix gaps in Visa & Residency Reforms
World.content:
.As Army pledges stronger partnership on border security

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The Nigeria Immigration Service NIS on Tuesday undertook a stakeholders’ assessment of its Visa and Residency Reforms, one year after the scheme was rolled out, promising to confront all the weak points.

Comptroller General of the NIS, Kemi Nandap, made the pledge in Abuja, while declaring open a one-day stakeholders’ sensitization workshop on the Nigeria Visa and Residency Reforms.

At the event, the Nigerian Army also pledged a stronger partnership with the Service in securing the country’s borders, especially in areas where a large portion of the frontier remains porous.

The Chief of Civil-Military Affairs (Army), Major General Musa Etsu-Ndagi, who represented the Chief of Army Staff COAS, said: “Nigeria has a land border of 4,047km and there is a large portion of it that remains porous. The Nigerian Army will continue to support the NIS in manning the borders especially in those areas”.

On the reforms, the CGIS who was represented by the Deputy Comptroller General DCG in charge of Visa and Residency, Dr Franca Usiwoma Nwanneka, said; “As we assess the implementation of the reforms over the last one year, we have reasons to appreciate the progress made so far. However, we must also be ready to identify the areas where we have not done well and take the necessary steps to address them”.

The workshop was held under the theme: “Assessing the Implementation of the Nigeria Visa and Residency Reforms: Stakeholders’ Engagement and Strategies for Improved Service Delivery.”

Nandap said the purpose of the meeting was to look at the progress made since the introduction of the reforms, discuss the challenges encountered and identify areas where improvements are needed.”

She acknowledged that users may have run into difficulties since the introduction of these reforms. “These may include payment difficulties, technical issues and other concerns relating to the use of the portal. I want to assure you that the Service is willing to listen to your concerns and consider useful recommendations that will help us improve our operations,” she said.

According to her, the reforms were introduced “to address some of the challenges associated with the old manual processes, reduce delays, improve transparency, strengthen national security and make our immigration services more accessible to the public.”

Nandap listed the electronic visa (e-Visa) among the major gains, noting that it became operational on 1st May, 2025, and replaced the traditional Visa-on-Arrival arrangement.

“Applicants can now receive decisions on their visa applications within 48 hours, subject to meeting the necessary requirements and security checks,” she said.

She added that the e-Visa had “improved transparency, reduced unnecessary human interference and strengthened our ability to monitor visa applications and approvals.”

The Comptroller General also cited the creation of the F9A and F9B visa categories for adult and minor Nigerians returning with foreign passports respectively, which she said had “helped to address the needs of Nigerians in the diaspora who find themselves in this situation.”

On work permits, Nandap said the Electronic Temporary Work Permit (e-TWP) became operational on 1st August, 2025, replacing manual procedures that “sometimes resulted in delays.” According to her, biometric capturing machines had improved the identification and verification of applicants, while insurance requirements were introduced to improve the management of foreign nationals undertaking temporary work in Nigeria.

The e-TWP, she explained, is also linked to the Service’s border management system through the Landing and Exit Card facility, which “will assist in monitoring the movement of foreign nationals and ensuring that they comply with the conditions of their stay in Nigeria.”

The third pillar of the reforms, the electronic Comprehensive Expatriate Residence Permit and Automated Card (e-CERPAC), also took effect on 1st August, 2025. Nandap said the system had improved the handling of residence permit applications, renewals and status regularisation, and led to the introduction of the Investors Residence Permit in support of the Federal Government’s drive to attract investment.

She said the e-CERPAC’s integration with the border management system “will make it easier to verify the residence status of expatriates at our entry and exit points.”

The immigration boss stressed that the Service could not succeed alone, and called for the support of “relevant Ministries, Departments and Agencies, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Nigerian Missions abroad, security agencies, the private sector, international organisations and employers of expatriates.”

Urging participants to contribute actively, Nandap said: “Our goal is to have an immigration system that provides efficient services, protects the security of our country and supports the economic development of Nigeria.”

World.title: FMCGs seek NAFDAC automation to cut registration delays, fake licences
World.content:
From Left: Director, National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (North-West), Dadi Mullah; Project Director, FMCG Festival, Flora Mbeledeogu, and President, Okearin Traders Association, Paulinus Ugwu at the Day 3 of FMCG Festival held in Lagos.

By Cynthia Alo

Fast-Moving Consumer Goods, FMCG, manufacturers and small businesses have urged the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, to automate most of its paper processes involving product registration and licence renewal to reduce delays and curb circulation of counterfeit products and fake registration numbers.

They said prolonged approvals were forcing some manufacturers to rely on intermediaries, exposing them to exploitation, including the use of fake NAFDAC registration numbers.

The call was made recently at the 2026 FMCG Festival in Lagos.

Speaking on behalf of manufacturers, Project Director of the FMCG Festival, Flora Mbeledeogu, said renewal of NAFDAC licences remained a major challenge, and that NAFDAC needed more hands and automation to make registration and renewal faster and more seamless.

Mbeledeogu said: “We need NAFDAC to employ more hands and automate our systems so that when a consumer brand wants to renew its NAFDAC certificate or licence, they can do so without having to raise an arm and a leg. It has to just be a seamless process, just like it is in other countries in Africa where you just need to upload the required documents on the portal; within 24 hours, receive notification for factory inspection; officials inspect and take samples; analysis is done;by 48 hours, the product registration number is issued. We need to get to that point.”

She warned that delays could expose smaller manufacturers to exploitation by intermediaries who claim to facilitate registration and renewal processes.

She urged the agency to address the bottlenecks before the next edition of the festival.

Responding to the concerns, Director, NAFDAC, North-West Zone, Dadi Mullah, said the agency’s processes were designed to ensure products met required health and safety standards.

He disclosed that food product registration could take up to 120 working days, covering facility inspection, laboratory testing, regulatory assessment and final approval.

Mullah said one challenge was that some small businesses wanted to produce from their domestic kitchens without meeting the facility requirements prescribed for commercial production.

He said NAFDAC could not allow such businesses to supply the wider market without complying with Good Manufacturing Practices, GMP.

He said: “The only thing I know that many of you will complain about is our facility requirement. We insist that unless the facility meets minimum good manufacturing practices requirements, we will not allow you to produce.Your kitchen cannot produce the kind of products for the international market.”

Speaking on delays in registration and renewal processing, he said NAFDAC’s laboratories handled a large volume of applications, making it difficult for applicants to expect immediate results.

He attributed part of the delays in Lagos to inadequate personnel at the agency’s food registration office.

He disclosed that NAFDAC had previously recorded more than 8,400 pending applications partly to having only one Local Office Director (LOD) handling applications at the office adding, “There was only one LOD in the food registration office, and until that person processes all those products, it sits in Lagos pipeline, moving slower.”

He said the agency had deployed additional LODs across its zonal offices to reduce the backlog.

He expressed optimism that the additional personnel would accelerate the process in the coming months, while urging manufacturers to continue providing feedback on delays and other challenges.

He added that to encourage registration of products , NAFDAC had discounted registration fees for micro, small and medium enterprises, MSMEs, since 2020.

According to him, no product registration fee exceeds N100,000, while some micro businesses pay between N40,000 and N60,000.

He said laboratory analysis could cost about N500,000, with the agency bearing part of the cost.

Mullah maintained that manufacturers did not need agents or intermediaries to obtain registration, advising businesses experiencing difficulties with the online process to approach the agency’s support desk for assistance at no cost.

He warned that anyone caught dealing in counterfeit products would face the law, saying offenders could be sentenced to seven years in prison.

” For now, anyone that is just dabbling into that, wherever, whenever we catch such a person, we will make sure that the law deals with you.”

He said consumers and traders could use NAFDAC’s online verification platform at registration.nafdac.gov.ng to confirm whether a product’s registration number was genuine.

He explained that the platform provides information such as the product name, packaging details, registration number and expiry date, enabling consumers to identify fake products.

He advised consumers to examine product labels, storage conditions and registration numbers before purchasing or consuming regulated products.

He also asked them to report suspected counterfeit products through the agency’s website, email and social media platforms, rather than merely complain about their circulation in the market.

The NAFDAC official further called for stronger collaboration with traders and distributors to identify and remove unregistered and counterfeit products from markets.

Supporting the call, President, Okearin Traders Association, Paulinus Ugwu , said traders had established a task force in the market to identify and remove counterfeit products.

Ugwu called for closer collaboration between traders and NAFDAC, noting that regulators could not know everything happening in markets without the cooperation of those operating there.

He said traders were also interested in promoting locally manufactured products, particularly those produced by small businesses, and called on manufacturers to bring their product samples for consideration by distributors.

In his keynote address, the Chief Operating Officer of Berger Paints Nigeria Plc, Kayode Momoh, urged manufacturers to strengthen supply chains, local sourcing, product quality and innovation to remain competitive.

Momoh said innovation must go beyond developing new ideas to ensuring that products could be produced, delivered and sustained consistently in the market.

He also called for a stable and predictable regulatory environment to give manufacturers confidence to invest for the long term.

World.title: Abia making steady progress under my watch — Otti
World.content:
Pledges support for emerging talents to attain global recognition

By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has said the state is making steady progress, expressing optimism about its development prospects under his administration.

Otti spoke at the grand finale of the 13th edition of the Vision Africa Icons Talent Show 2026 in Umuahia, where he highlighted his administration’s efforts to reposition the state’s economy and promote development across various sectors.

The governor, who was represented by his Chief of Staff, Pastor Caleb Ajagba, also pledged government support for the discovery, development and international promotion of indigenous talents.

He said the administration was committed to creating opportunities for gifted young people to develop their abilities and gain recognition beyond Nigeria.

Reflecting on the state’s development journey, Otti said his administration had prioritised efforts to harness Abia’s economic and human resources.

“Before Otti came on board, Abia was lying fallow and prostrate. Nothing good was being said of Abia State. Today, Abia is being celebrated as a place of excellence,” he said.

The governor said purposeful leadership and collaboration were important in unlocking the state’s human and creative potential.

He assured participants in the talent show that the government would support successful contestants in pursuing opportunities for international recognition.

Otti also disclosed that the state government would partner with Vision Africa International to advance the initiative.

“Everybody that emerges here today is going global. His Excellency is going to make sure that global stardom is achieved,” he said.

He described the talent show as consistent with his administration’s commitment to identifying, nurturing and promoting the abilities of young people.

Earlier, the Chairman of the occasion, Noah Dallaji, represented by Theo Ubani, said Africa’s human talent remained one of the continent’s major competitive advantages.

“I tell people that Africa has talent to offer. We might not offer the best in technology, but what we can offer is talent,” he said.

In his welcome address, the founder and President of Vision Africa International, Archbishop Sunday Onuoha, called on political leaders to create conditions that would enable disadvantaged citizens to benefit from peace and development.

Onuoha, who is also Co-Chairman of the Interfaith Dialogue Forum for Peace, said Nigeria’s diversity should promote unity rather than division.

He urged Nigerians to work together across their differences to build a peaceful and prosperous country.

The 13th edition of the Vision Africa Icons Talent Show was held under the theme, “The Sound of Peace: Breaking Barriers, Building Bridges.”

World.title: Itsekiri youths suspend campaign rally boycott after governor’s intervention
World.content:
Governor Oborevwori of Delta State

Itsekiri apex youth bodies, Ugbarajo Itsekiri Youths, UIY, and Itsekiri National Youth Council, INYC, have reiterated their opposition to the inclusion of the Ijaw in the Warri South ward delineation.

They expressed surprise at the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC’s, decision to upload wards with names that have no historical, geographical or traditional relationship with Warri South, saying the move could trigger serious crises.

They, however, decided to temporarily suspend mass action against all forms of political activities in Warri Kingdom following the intervention of Governor Sheriff Oborevwori.

The INYC President, Appearance Efejuku, and UIY President, Joseph Okotie, made this known in a statement.

The statement read: “Sequel to the memorandum of threat issued to the general public over the readiness of the Itsekiri apex youth bodies, UIY and INYC, to prevent the hosting of all forms of campaign rallies in any part of Warri Kingdom until all issues associated with the illegal creation of wards for the Ijaws are addressed satisfactorily, the Governor of Delta State, Right Honorable Elder Francis O. Oborevwori, invited us, leaders and other stakeholders, for a closed-door meeting, wherein he requested to know why the issuers of the threats took such a position. According to him, as of the last time he checked, the entire Itsekiri nation endorsed him and Mr. President. Thus, if this issue raised in the memo is not addressed, it could be misconstrued as a change in the position of the Itsekiri nation against the APC as a political party.

“In response, the leadership of the two youth bodies was very categorical in their vehement opposition to any inclusion of Ijaws by any consideration into Warri South ward delineation.

“As this would amount to disrespecting the directive of the President (His Excellency Bola Ahmed Tinubu), who asked the Itsekiris and the Urhobos of Warri South to go and meet, sort out the issues, and get back to him. They also said that the President further stated that if the parties involved in these delineation issues were not satisfied, he would have no other option than to take the Supreme Court judgment back to the Supreme Court for proper interpretation.

“They were therefore surprised to wake up one day and be told, in flagrant disregard of this directive of the President, that INEC had uploaded wards with names that have no historical, geographical or traditional relationship with Warri South.

“This, according to the bodies, is a recipe for serious crises if INEC is not made to retrace its steps.

“Thereafter, the Governor appealed to the leadership of the youth bodies to sheath their swords so he could take this issue back to the President for better clarification.

“Additionally, it was stated that the only ward structure that was operational before now was the 12-ward structure, and it is what will be used to conduct the 2027 general election.

“Consequent upon all that was mentioned, the leadership of UIY and INYC met and hereby resolved to temporarily suspend all forms of intended mass action and mobilisation towards stopping all Itsekiris from attending this rally. We therefore call on all members and critical stakeholders of our organisations to be on internal vigilance to monitor the activities of all political parties in the Kingdom to ensure that these ward delineations are not weaponised as a tool to undermine the Itsekiri people in their homeland of the Warri Federal Constituency.

“All these positions were corroborated by the Urhobos of Warri South who were in attendance at the meeting.”

World.title: Benue: Can Gov Alia Survive Gang-up against His Re-election in 2027?
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

George Okoh, in this report, examines the political intrigues, shifting alliances and emerging threats confronting Governor Hyacinth Alia of Benue State as he walks an increasingly precarious political tightrope ahead of the February, 2027 gubernatorial poll in the state.

The road to the 2027 governorship election in Benue State is becoming increasingly complicated for Governor Hyacinth Alia. Over three and half years after his historic emergence as governor on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), the Catholic priest-turned-politician is facing a political environment considerably different from the one that brought him to power in May, 2023.

Although Alia remains the incumbent governor, his journey towards securing another four years in Government House, Makurdi, is surrounded by political uncertainties, internal party disagreements, strained relationships with influential stakeholders and an increasingly competitive opposition.

The question confronting political observers is no longer simply whether Alia wants a second term. It is whether he can successfully navigate the complicated political terrain between now and the 2027 poll.

Akume factor: A political marriage under strain

Perhaps the greatest political challenge confronting Governor Alia is his troubled relationship with the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume

The political alliance between the two men was instrumental in APC’s remarkable victory in Benue State in 2023. Akume brought his extensive political network, established grassroots structures and years of political experience, while Alia brought enormous popularity among ordinary people and the attraction of a relatively new political personality.

Together, they dismantled the People’s Democratic Party’s longstanding dominance of Benue politics.

However, the relationship subsequently deteriorated over disagreements concerning appointments, political influence, party leadership and control of the APC structure in the state.

What initially appeared to be a disagreement between political allies has developed into a major struggle for supremacy within the ruling party.

Reconciliation efforts between the two camps have stalled, with parallel party structures and disagreements over leadership continuing to threaten party cohesion.

This is a serious problem for Alia. In politics, an incumbent governor may control the machinery of government, but controlling government is not necessarily the same as controlling the political party that produced him.

The governor therefore faces a delicate balancing act: maintaining his political independence while avoiding a complete breakdown of relationships with influential APC stakeholders.

Absence of influential stakeholders

Another troubling development was the inauguration of Alia’s 2027 re-election campaign council on November 6, 2026.

A source said several influential APC stakeholders, including Akume, serving senators and members of the House of Representatives from Benue State, were conspicuously absent.

The development raises questions about the level of political cohesion within the ruling party.

A campaign council is expected to demonstrate unity, organisation and collective commitment. When prominent political figures are absent from such an important event, it inevitably generates questions about the depth of support for the candidate.

Alia cannot afford to underestimate the importance of these political actors. Many have established relationships with party members and grassroots mobilisers across the state’s 23 local government areas.

Even if the governor enjoys considerable personal popularity, a fractured political structure could complicate his re-election campaign.

Opposition looking for an opportunity

The political situation is also changing on the opposition side. Former governor Samuel Ortom remains an important political figure whose influence cannot simply be dismissed. Former President of the Senate, Senator David Mark and the emerging African Democratic Congress political platform also represent another dimension of the opposition challenge.

Meanwhile, the PDP has its own political calculations and governorship ambitions.

The reported emergence of discussions involving politicians from different camps suggest that political realignments could significantly alter the contest.

The possibility of cooperation between individuals who were previously political opponents presents an additional challenge for the incumbent.

The 2023 election was fought under different political circumstances. The APC enjoyed a relatively united structure and an alliance that brought together several powerful political interests.

Another issue affecting Governor Alia is his frosty relationship with the Chairman of the APC in the state, Mr Austin Agada.

For the past three years, Alia has refused to recognize Agada as the APC state Chairman despite a Court of Appeal judgement that dully recognized him as the state chairman of the party. Rather, the governor has thrown his weight behind Mr Benjamin Omale who was appointed as the caretaker chairman by the Umar Ganduje-led national leadership of the party then.

As it stands in the state, Agada has secured an enforcement of his victory at the court and may go for Alia’s jugular.

World.title: Oloko: I’ll Lobby to Get Lagos’ 37 LCDAs Listed in the Constitution
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Peoples Redemption Party’s candidate for Lagos Central in the 2027 general election, Afolabi Lookman Oloko, in this interview, speaks on his agenda for the senatorial district and how he would ensure quality and effective representation if elected in January, 2027, among other issues.

You’re running for Lagos Central under the PRP. What specifically about the current representation in the Senate made you decide to step up at this time?

Generally and as we all can see, Nigeria calls and as compatriots, some of us have answered…so, I have only chosen to heed the call of fatherland in what I call an over-riding public interest.
