“A new dawn. A high-flying Lagos!” That’s your tagline. In practical terms, what does a high-flying Lagos Central will look like to you in your first four years in the Senate?

Chief of such dreams is to get the 37 LCDAs constitutionally recognised. You see, the job of the legislature is sub-divided into three…one, to make laws for peace and good governance…two, to play oversight roles on the MDAs and ministries and in so doing, acting as a check on the executive and lastly and of course most widely known, to represent the people of their various Districts and Constituencies at the centre. To that extent, I hold up the Constitutional recognition of the 37 LCDAs in Lagos State as my joker. It’s so central to us – we, the people at the Lagos Central District…I remember a Comrade who made similar case for the same argument in 2019- Tosin Akande- his name, a Barrister at Law…his bid, though, unsuccessful, his courage cannot be wished-away.

It is worthy of emulation and here, I am on the same path. As a perfect example, the rise of Barrack Obama in the US White House cannot be isolated from the efforts of previous Afro-American civil rights leaders like Rosa Parks, Martin Luther King (MLK, Jnr), Rev. Jesse Jackson, Muhammed Ali, Marcus Garvey, Malcolm X etc…Obama was just a culmination of the aggregate contributions of these erstwhile leaders of Black consciousness.

In the same vein, we won’t stop the fight for the people at the grassroots until we get there – to the Promised Land. Ironically, it was the President who started the good fight as the Governor of Lagos State in 2001/2002, Akande leveraged on it in the build-up to the 2019 National Assembly elections and now- 2026, I am here to make my attempt on the same subject…God willing, we will get there. This time, the attempt will count if God wants it so.

You said “I will put citizens of Lagos Central District first and at the every Legislative decision.” Can you give us two specific bills or motions you’d sponsor in your first year that will directly reflect that “People First” promise?

Motions, to the lawmaker, are like what business ideas are to an entrepreneur or what patents are to inventors, you don’t put them up in the public without recourse to time. When we get there, we will put up much more promises. My campaign promise on the 37 LCDAs and plans for the youths and women, suffice for now.

Your pact includes making it a legislative action plan to get the 37 LCDAs recognized as LGAs. What’s your actual legislative strategy to get that constitutional amendment through the National Assembly, considering it’s failed multiple times before?

Lobbying! That’s the only strategy…or do you want us to include wailing and cheap blackmail as some are wont? (Laughs)…we have to reach out to friendly lawmakers to make them see reason- devoid of ethnic or tribal bigotry because of the Constitutional provision in Section 8 where-upon we will need the Constitutional ratification of two-thirds support of the 36 States of the federation…so, you can see that it’s enormous task…quite herculean but I’m confident, we will get there. We will have to do several handshakes across the Niger. Intense lobbying!

You mentioned plans for Gender Equity, Youth Advancement, and Social Inclusion. What are three concrete, fundable programs you’ll push for women and youths in Lagos Central — Eko, Lagos Island, Surulere, etc?

On our GE-YA-SI programme, we will organise job fairs to help reduce the burden of youth unemployment…we will establish the Education Support Scheme to help the very indigent students in school to do school fees subvention. For example, help pay half of the school fees of those on exceptional academic standing from 70% up but cannot pay and who are in public universities and polytechnics, only.

Women empowerment programmes will focus on women in order to preserve the home. I am happily married and it is my joy to see our women, get married, stay married and be happy in their homes and with their jobs and vocations. My kind of affirmative action is not to prod women and men against one another. No! The goal is family-centred; not gender-biased.

You pledged to advocate for a safer, united and more prosperous Lagos. Lagos Central has issues with housing, traffic, and small businesses. Which of these is your top priority and how will you use your Senate seat to address it?

This is the beauty of separation of powers. Housing is clearly an executive item. I will not promise what the law has not empowered me to do. I will be very unambiguous about it from here…I’ll not deceive the people. Ditto the issue of traffic and so far, Lagos is doing well with LASTMA. Let me seize this occasion to recognise their efforts and lightly caution their men and women on over-zealousness. Such that, the people of Lagos State attest to their relevance in the emerging Lagos of our dreams. Personally, LASTMA as an Agency has my pass mark!

You wrote “Proper and Better with Results Lagos.” What mechanisms will you put in place to make yourself accountable to Lagos Central constituents? Town halls, quarterly reports, constituency office metrics?

I talked about some of my programmes for young people and unique programmes for women empowerment. I stand by my promises…Our women empowerment programmes will focus on women in order to preserve the home. Members of the Lagos Central district public should stay on red alert!

The PRP has been around since 1978 but has limited Senate seats currently. How do you plan to build alliances across party lines in the 11th Senate to actually get your bills passed for Lagos Central?

I mentioned it extensively before…that will be pursued aggressively. Already the Hausa community in my District are being engaged and from Lagos, emissaries will be raised for such alliance purposes.

See, it’s beautiful and only will be more beautiful if the people of Lagos Central can give me a chance to represent them in the Senate. I am the new dawn that Lagos is waking up to. (Smiles and points at self with both hands).

As a Senator, many of the issues in Lagos Central like waste, roads, and local policing fall under state/LG. Where do you draw the line between what you’ll do at the National Assembly versus what you’ll lobby the Lagos State Government to do?

I already drew the line on a previous question. When such line-drawing and perhaps, truth-telling is rife again, myself and my team will draw it for the people to see in the name of transparency in government, it’s a constant engagement of the populace. The people of the District and my team are partners in progress so the lines must be constantly kept open.

World.title: RMAFC Seeks National Framework to Cut Oil Dependence
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

James Emejo in Abuja

Chairman, Revenue Mobilisation, Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC), Dr. Mohammed Bello Shehu, yesterday called for a practical national framework to diversify Nigeria’s revenue base and reduce dependence on oil.

He said efforts to mobilise additional revenue must translate into concrete policy actions.

Shehu made the call during a two-day strategic planning retreat for the proposed National Revenue Summit held at Zuma Rock Resort, Zuba, Niger State, where he charged participants to develop actionable recommendations backed by clear responsibilities and implementation timelines.

He said the retreat was designed to establish a roadmap for the summit, including its objectives, thematic areas, stakeholder participation and expected outcomes, stressing that the engagement must go beyond discussions to deliver measurable results.

The proposed summit is expected to bring together representatives of the federal, state and local governments, revenue-generating agencies, private sector operators, academia and development partners to identify sustainable sources of revenue for financing infrastructure and other national development priorities.

Shehu said the initiative aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s economic reform agenda, particularly efforts to expand non-oil revenue and strengthen fiscal sustainability.

Speaking in an interview, Chairman of RMAFC’s Mobilisation and Diversification Committee, Hon. Victor O. Eboigbe, said the Commission was seeking a national policy framework to guide the three tiers of government in broadening their revenue sources.

Eboigbe, who represents Edo State on the Commission, said the framework would strengthen RMAFC’s constitutional advisory role on revenue generation and help governments improve their fiscal capacity.

“One of our very important functions is to advise the three tiers of government on how to increase their revenue,” he said.

He stressed that diversifying away from oil had become imperative in view of the enormous funding requirements of Nigeria’s infrastructure and development ambitions.

Also speaking, Vice Chairman of the committee and Federal Commissioner representing Abia State, Hon. Oti Nkechi Linda, said the summit would explore untapped revenue opportunities across sectors while addressing economic wastage.

She said the Commission planned to take the diversification campaign across the six geopolitical zones, engaging government institutions, private sector operators, young people and other stakeholders.

Oti also attributed improvements in the Commission’s institutional capacity to the leadership of Shehu, saying this had strengthened its ability to discharge its mandate.

Director of the Mobilisation and Diversification Department, Dr. Khadija Suleiman Kumo, said the retreat marked the beginning of detailed preparations for the summit, which would focus on expanding the Federation’s revenue base to support national development projects.

The retreat, which ended November 17, was expected to consolidate the Commission’s position on revenue mobilisation, administration and compliance, while identifying practical opportunities to improve revenue generation across the three tiers of government.

World.title: BA Cancels London-Lagos Flight After Runway Excursion at Heathrow
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Chinedu Eze

A British Airways flight scheduled to operate from London Heathrow Airport to Lagos was cancelled on Tuesday after its aircraft veered off a taxiway and became stuck in a grass verge shortly before departure.



The incident involved flight BA75, operated with a Boeing 787-10 Dreamliner bearing registration number G-ZBLF. The aircraft was preparing to fly to Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, with 215 passengers reportedly on board.



According to reports, the aircraft had pushed back from Terminal 5, Gate C56, at approximately 10:40 a.m. local time and was taxiing towards the runway when it left the designated paved route. Its nose landing gear became lodged in the grass, preventing it from continuing towards the departure runway.

The aircraft did not take off, and the incident led to the cancellation of the scheduled service. Photographs from the scene showed the front landing gear stuck in the muddy ground beside the taxiway.



There were no reported injuries among passengers or crew members.



Heathrow Airport confirmed that it was assisting after the aircraft left the taxiway. Airport personnel and emergency teams responded to the incident, while arrangements were made to help passengers leave the aircraft and return to the terminal.



British Airways apologised to affected customers over the disruption, saying its teams were working to arrange alternative travel so passengers could continue their journeys as quickly as possible.

The cancellation left travellers facing unexpected changes to their schedules, particularly those who had planned onward connections or other engagements in Lagos.



The airline did not immediately provide a detailed explanation of what caused the aircraft to leave the taxiway.

World.title: APC Accuses ADC, NDC of Instigating Protests Against Tinubu
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

• ADC: Nigerians don’t need sponsor to be angry over current hardship

•NDC: Tinubu’s N11.2tn pipeline security spending exceeds defence budget

•Obi takes campaign for democracy to US Congress, seeks support

Emmanuel Addeh, Adedayo Akinwale and Sunday Aborisade in Abuja





The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) has accused the opposition African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) of sponsoring protests, spreading fake news and orchestrating disruptions at its campaign rallies.

However, in a response to the allegation, the ADC dismissed it as an attempt to deflect public anger over the economic hardship in the country, stressing that Nigerians needed no political sponsors to express their dissatisfaction with the Bola Tinubu’s administration.

The two parties traded accusations yesterday, with the APC alleging that opposition elements were mobilising hoodlums to create tension and violence ahead of next year’s general election.

In the statement issued by the APC-PCC spokesperson, Dele Alake, the ADC alleged that the opposition had perfected plans to sow disharmony and introduce violence into the campaigns.

Alake recalled that hours before the flag-off of the APC presidential campaign rally in Kaduna on October 24, 2026, the party had alerted Nigerians to an alleged plot involving deepfakes, artificial intelligence-generated images, fake news, sponsored protests and other forms of propaganda.

He said the intention was to manipulate public opinion and spread falsehoods about the country, Tinubu, the APC and the processes leading to the elections.

“These unpatriotic and disingenuous plots by opposition elements have started unfolding. Their major objective is to deceive Nigerians and the international community by driving a narrative of discontent against President Tinubu,” he stated.

The APC cited the alleged desecration of an Abuja mosque last Friday, claiming that thugs were mobilised to pelt the presidential motorcade with stones.

The council commended security personnel attached to the presidential convoy for exercising restraint, as well as Tinubu for directing the police in Abuja to release those detained over the incident.

It also expressed concern over alleged attacks on APC members and supporters in the South-east, where it claimed some were being threatened and labelled saboteurs for refusing to support the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi.

The council further alleged that opposition-sponsored agents were destroying APC campaign billboards under the cover of darkness.

“This is unacceptable and antithetical to democratic ideals,” Alake said, urging the ADC and NDC leadership to stop what he described as the dangerous recruitment of young Nigerians into activities that could put their lives at risk, while their own children enjoyed comfortable lives abroad.

Nigerians Don’t Need Sponsor to be Angry, Says ADC

However, the ADC-PCC, in a response, rejected the allegations, accusing the ruling party of attempting to blame the opposition for the anger of Nigerians over the government’s economic policies.

In a statement signed by its Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the ADC said the APC could not attribute public dissatisfaction to an opposition plot when the hardship confronting Nigerians was a consequence of the administration’s policies.

“For three and a half years, President Bola Tinubu has plucked the feathers from the Nigerian people with policies that have made food, fuel and basic survival painfully expensive. Now he scatters a little campaign grain and expects the wounded to follow him singing his praises,” the opposition party stated.

The ADC challenged the APC to provide evidence linking it to the alleged sponsorship of protests and violence, arguing that a ruling party controlling the federal government should not make such serious allegations without substantiation.

It also questioned the circumstances surrounding the alleged attack on Tinubu’s motorcade, pointing to what it described as conflicting accounts from the presidency and the APC campaign council.

“The Presidency earlier denied that the President’s motorcade had been pelted. Now the APC campaign council says people were detained for pelting the convoy with stones and that President Tinubu directed their release. Which account should Nigerians believe?” the ADC asked.

It further questioned why those detained over the incident were released if there was evidence of their involvement, and why the alleged sponsors had not been identified and prosecuted.

“If the APC has evidence that the ADC armed or sponsored those people, why were those detained released? Why have the alleged sponsors not been identified and prosecuted? A government with evidence of such a serious offence should hand it to investigators, not fling accusations at its opponents,” the statement added.

The ADC denied sponsoring violence or recruiting young people to confront political opponents, condemning attacks on campaigners, supporters, places of worship and public property, irrespective of political affiliation.

The opposition party also challenged the APC to answer questions about reports and images of money allegedly being distributed at its campaign events, arguing that the ruling party could not dismiss every crowd that refused to cheer the President as being sponsored by the ADC.

“Nigerians are entitled to judge this government by the cost of living and by their own daily experience. Calling their anger an opposition plot will not make it disappear,” Shaibu said.

The ADC urged the APC to produce evidence for its allegations or withdraw them, insisting that Nigerians were capable of assessing the administration’s performance and making their own political choices.

NDC: Tinubu’s N11.2tn Pipeline Spending Doubles Defence Budget

Also, the NDC has questioned the transparency of the federal government’s management of pipeline security expenditure, alleging that the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) has an opaque N11.2 trillion balance linked to energy security costs and other deductions from oil revenues.

The opposition party, which expressed concern over what it described as questionable financial disclosures in NNPC’s audited accounts, said the amount was more than twice the N4.91 trillion allocated to all defence and security agencies in the 2025 budget.

It also claimed that the disputed sum was more than three times the N3.10 trillion allocated to the Ministry of Defence for the Army, Navy and Air Force combined.

The NDC, therefore, demanded an immediate forensic audit of the N11.2 trillion balance, insisting that the government must account for every naira spent on protecting the country’s oil infrastructure while the Armed Forces continue to grapple with inadequate funding for military equipment.

In a statement issued yesterday by the spokesperson of its National Campaign Council, Dr. Constance Ikokwu, the party said the financial disclosures raised serious questions about the government’s spending priorities, particularly against the backdrop of escalating insecurity across the country.

The statement, titled, ‘How Tinubu’s Administration Presides Over an Opaque N11.2 Trillion Pipeline Security Bill That Doubles the Entire Military Budget While Starving Our Armed Forces and Insecurity Continues to Escalate’, alleged that the amount recorded as ‘other receivables from the federation’ was tied to energy security costs and unverified off-budget deductions.

According to the NDC, the disparity between the alleged pipeline security expenditure and allocations to the country’s military establishment demands urgent public scrutiny.

“While insecurity continues to escalate across Nigeria, with citizens abducted, slaughtered on farmlands and forced to pay crippling ransoms, this administration presides over books showing trillions tied to protecting oil conduits, even as our Armed Forces remain starved of modern weaponry,” the party said.

It added: “Strip away the accounting jargon, and this N11.2 trillion expenditure looks like nothing more than a massive political patronage slush fund disguised as ‘energy security’. Are patronage payouts to political allies now worth more than Nigerian lives?”

The opposition party, however, acknowledged that protecting the country’s oil pipelines and other critical petroleum infrastructure was essential to national economic security.

It argued that the government should adopt modern surveillance technologies and transparent expenditure mechanisms, rather than allow huge sums to accumulate under what it described as poorly explained financial arrangements.

The NDC cited fibre-optic sensors, surveillance drones, satellite radar and transparent Host Community Development Trusts as some of the technologies and institutional mechanisms that could strengthen pipeline protection while reducing security costs.

It maintained that the government should prioritise investments in modern equipment for the Armed Forces instead of allowing substantial oil-related security expenditures to remain outside transparent public scrutiny.

The party also questioned the structure of military spending, citing figures which it said showed that 75.9 per cent of the 2026 core defence budget of N3.15 trillion was devoted to personnel costs, while only 14.7 per cent, representing N464 billion, was allocated to capital expenditure on military equipment.

It further alleged that only seven per cent of the 2025 Defence Capital Budget had been released, describing the situation as evidence of the funding challenges confronting the country’s security establishment.

The NDC argued that the alleged funding imbalance could undermine the operational capacity of the military at a time when troops were confronting multiple security threats across different parts of the country.

It said: “Instead of 21st-century technology and empowering our Armed Forces, where 75.9 per cent of the 2026 core N3.15 trillion budget goes to personnel and only 14.7 per cent (N464 billion) to capital weapons, after just seven per cent of the 2025 Defence Capital Budget was released, this government chose opaque patronage.”

The party outlined three demands which it said were necessary to restore public confidence in the management of the country’s petroleum revenues and security expenditure.

First, it demanded an immediate forensic audit of the N11.2 trillion NNPCL energy security balance, with full disclosure of payments made to private contractors and a clear breakdown of legacy deductions.

Second, it called for comprehensive disclosure of funds released for military capital equipment and troop welfare in 2025 and 2026.

Third, it demanded an end to what it described as off-budget deductions, insisting that all oil revenues should be paid into the Federation Account and subjected to appropriation by the National Assembly.

The NDC maintained that Nigerians were entitled to know how much the government spent on protecting oil infrastructure, the identities of contractors involved, the services rendered and the extent to which the expenditure had improved security in oil-producing communities.

It also argued that transparency in the management of petroleum revenues was particularly important because of the country’s persistent security challenges and the competing demands on scarce public resources.

“A government that prioritises opaque political patronage over human life while insecurity continues to escalate has lost its moral legitimacy,” the party declared.

The opposition party subsequently urged Nigerians to support its presidential ticket of Peter Obi and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, saying the candidates were committed to changing the country’s political and economic governance structure.

“The Obi/Kwankwaso ticket believes that Nigeria must work for all, and not a few,” it said.

The statement did not, however, provide a breakdown of the individual transactions making up the 11.2 trillion balance or identify the private contractors allegedly involved.

Obi Takes Campaign for Democracy to US Congress, Seeks Support

Meanwhile, the presidential candidate of the NDC in the 2027 general election, Mr. Peter Obi, has taken his campaign for Nigeria’s democratic development and institutional reforms to the United States Congress, urging stronger international cooperation and support for the country.

Obi, who arrived in Washington DC on Monday, November 16, according to his post on X, Tuesday, disclosed that he held a series of meetings with members of the United States House of Representatives and Senate, alongside other influential American figures, to discuss Nigeria’s development, security, economic prosperity and the future of its democracy.

The former Anambra State governor also used the engagements to canvass international support for strengthening Nigeria’s democratic institutions and ensuring that future elections are free, fair, transparent and credible.

In his statement announcing his engagements, Obi said his discussions with American lawmakers and other stakeholders focused on critical issues affecting Nigeria and the urgent need for accountable leadership.

He said, “These discussions focused on vital matters affecting Nigeria’s development, the well-being of our people, and the future of our democracy.”

Obi began his engagements with an interview with prominent American television commentator, Glenn Beck, during which he discussed Nigeria’s development challenges, responsible management of the country’s human and natural resources, and the need for accountable leadership.

He also met with several American political figures and stakeholders, including Congressman Marlin Stutzman, Congresswoman Beth Van Duyne, Congressman Todd Tiahrt, Suzanne Bock Grisham and retired United States Army Colonel Albert V. Short.

A major highlight of the visit, according to Obi, was his address on Capitol Hill, where he emphasised the importance of international cooperation in addressing Nigeria’s security challenges, strengthening national unity and promoting economic prosperity.

He also drew attention to the need to protect Nigeria’s democracy and strengthen institutions responsible for guaranteeing credible electoral outcomes.

The NDC presidential candidate maintained that the country’s democratic future must be determined by Nigerians through a process that respects the votes and fundamental rights of citizens.

“Our conversations also addressed the protection of Nigeria’s emerging democracy and the strengthening of democratic institutions to ensure elections are free, fair, transparent, and credible, accurately reflecting the will of the Nigerian people,” he stated.

Obi, who has consistently advocated prudent management of public resources and accountable governance, argued that Nigeria possessed the human and natural resources required to become one of the world’s leading nations but needed responsible leadership and resilient institutions to realise its potential.

He said the country urgently required leaders committed to national unity, security, economic development and the welfare of citizens.

“Nigeria has immense potential to emerge as a leading nation within the global community. What is urgently required is accountable leadership, responsible stewardship of our resources, resilient institutions, and an authentic commitment to the security, unity, and well-being of every Nigerian,” he said.

World.title: Jonathan: There’s Global Apprehension About Likelihood of Crises After 2027 Polls
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

• Warns against rising political intolerance, violence, says parties are run like cult groups

• Insists concerns are that next elections may degenerate into destructive ethnic rivalry

Chuks Okocha in Abuja





Former President Goodluck Jonathan has alleged global apprehension about the possibility of trouble following next year’s general election.

Jonathan said, “People are worried all over the world. Rather than the confidence and optimism we should be inspiring, there is growing apprehension about the likelihood of crises that may follow our elections.”

He warned Nigerian politicians against rising political intolerance ahead of the 2027 elections, cautioning that political parties should not be run like rival cult groups.

Jonathan gave the warning yesterday in Abuja at the third edition of the National Peace and Awareness Conference, organised by Goodluck Jonathan Foundation (GJF).

The 2026 edition of the conference was themed, “Safeguarding Trust and Strengthening Social Cohesion in a Politically Competitive Environment.”

Jonathan, who is Founder of the foundation, decried what he described as an unbearable level of political intolerance, thuggery, and the exploitation of young people as instruments of violence across the country.

He said as a former president, he had received calls from Nigerians and friends of the country across the world expressing concern over the direction Nigeria was heading.

According to him, “We must not ignore these concerns by the people, and we must do everything to prevent it as a nation and as a people.

“Among the issues demanding urgent attention is the growing pulse of political intolerance. It is becoming unbearable. We are running political organisations and campaign teams as cult groups.

“Cult groups are always rivals; you see the other cult group as an enemy, so you must attack, kill, and maim. That is not politics. We must not manage our political systems as cult groups.”

Jonathan also expressed concern over an increasing unwillingness among political actors to accommodate opposing views or recognise the legitimate right of others to compete for political power.

He stated, “All of us have the right to compete for any level of election, from councillorship and state assembly to the presidency.

“This is compounded by political thuggery. The exploitation of our very young people as instruments of violence and acts of political brigandage is happening across the country, and it is very worrisome.”

The former president expressed concern over controversies surrounding conflicting judicial pronouncements and “window shopping” for favourable courts by politicians.

He warned that eroding public confidence in the judiciary could push citizens towards self-help and anarchy.

Jonathan stated that it was worrisome to see courts of coordinate jurisdiction giving conflicting pronouncements on the same matter, and sometimes lower courts sitting as appellate courts over superior courts.

He said, “A growing concern in Nigeria again is like, I wanted to say window shopping of courts, but that is not a correct description.

“People will go to courts where they think those who operate those courts are their friends, and they can carry something from Sokoto to Yenagoa, and from Yenagoa to Kano.

“They are making those of us who are not lawyers start asking what is happening in the country.

“The National Judicial Council (NJC) needs to look into some of these and streamline approaches to litigation in Nigeria so that people will have confidence in the courts.

“When citizens begin to lose faith in the courts and resort to self-help, the consequences can be very disastrous.”

Jonathan compared politics to a football match, explaining that while politicians and parties are the players, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) serves as the referee.

He equally likened the courts to the Video Assistant Referee (VAR), and the general public to the supporters, urging citizens, traditional rulers, and religious leaders in mosques and churches to actively reject political excesses rather than remain silent.

He stated, “There are growing concerns that our coming elections may degenerate into destructive ethnic rivalry at both the national and state levels, because the pattern of emerging issues could now ignite ethnic rivalry.

“There is nothing as bad as when ethnicity or religion is brought into elections and becomes confrontational; you can no longer solve the problem.

“Nothing could be more dangerous to our national existence than the deliberate encouragement of ethnic rivalry.

“We must never allow political ambition to undermine the bonds that hold us together as one nation and one country, both at the national and state levels.”

Jonathan reiterated his call to overhaul the country’s political recruitment process ahead of 2027 by prioritising competence and national interest over primordial sentiments.

He said, “Let us choose competence over prejudice, service over personal ambition, and national interest over narrow considerations.

“Our democracy must produce leaders capable of uniting our people and advancing our collective development.”

In her remarks, Executive Director of GJF, Ms Ann Iyonu, called for urgent measures to rebuild public trust in Nigeria’s democratic institutions and strengthen social cohesion ahead of the 2027 polls.

Iyonu warned that political realignments, persistent insecurity, economic pressures, and declining public confidence in institutions were converging to create a fragile pre-election environment capable of deepening national divisions if not responsibly managed.

She stated that recent public opinion data, including the pre-election fact-finding mission of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) to Nigeria, underscored the urgency of the dialogue.

Iyonu stated, “A 2026 Afrobarometer survey released last week on Nov. 11 reveals a troubling deficit of public trust in Nigeria’s electoral process, with fewer than four in 10 Nigerians expressing confidence that the 2027 general elections will be free and fair.

“A majority anticipate electoral abuses, including vote buying, political violence, disregard for electoral laws, failure to count valid votes, and the announcement of inaccurate results.

“At the same time, the findings show that Nigerians remain committed to democracy, with a clear majority indicating their intention to vote and expressing a preference for candidates whose policies address the nation’s pressing challenges.

“These findings serve as a stark reminder that strengthening trust in democratic institutions and processes is not merely a political imperative, but a peace and security necessity.”

World.title: Fani-Kayode Meets S’African DIRCO DG, Raises Concern over Killings, Mistreatment
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Michael Olugbode in Abuja

Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Ambassador Femi Fani-Kayode, yesterday, held a meeting with the Director-General of South Africa’s Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO), Mr Zane Dangor, following an earlier invitation by the South African government aimed at sustaining cordial and mutually beneficial relations between the two countries.

The meeting, which was convened against the backdrop of recent developments in Nigeria-South Africa relations, provided an opportunity for both sides to discuss matters of mutual concern, including events over the weekend.

During the engagement, Fani-Kayode expressed serious concerns over the recent killings of Nigerians in South Africa, as well as the hardship and alleged mistreatment faced by Nigerian nationals, warning that Nigeria’s patience over the persistent challenges confronting its citizens was wearing thin.

He maintained that such treatment was contrary to international law and human rights principles, stressing that the protection of Nigerians remained his foremost responsibility and a fundamental obligation of his diplomatic mandate.

He also expressed displeasure over the manner in which South African Presidential Spokesperson, Vincent Magwenya, handled the recent controversy, with DIRCO indicating that the concerns raised would be addressed.

In a post on X after the meeting, Fani-Kayode described his engagement with Dangor as excellent and constructive, noting that both parties discussed mutual concerns regarding bilateral relations and recent events.

“Honoured to have had an excellent meeting with the DG of South Africa’s @DIRCO_ZA (Department of International Relations and Cooperation), Mr Zane Dangor, this morning.

“Mutual concerns regarding our bilateral relations and the events over the weekend were discussed,” he stated.

He said Nigeria looked forward to building on the outcome of the meeting and strengthening the longstanding relationship between both countries, founded on mutual respect, friendship and cooperation.

The High Commissioner also expressed his readiness to work closely with DIRCO and South Africa’s Minister of International Relations and Cooperation, Ronald Lamola, towards further strengthening ties between the two nations.

Meanwhile, the Nigerian High Commission, has dismissed media reports suggesting that Fani-Kayode was reprimanded or issued a warning by South African authorities during the meeting.

The mission maintained that the engagement was cordial and constructive, stressing that the High Commissioner was neither reprimanded nor warned.

It described the meeting as a diplomatic engagement in which both parties exchanged views on issues of mutual concern while reaffirming their commitment to diplomatic protocols and longstanding bilateral relations.

Both sides also expressed willingness to sustain dialogue and work towards resolving outstanding concerns in the interest of the two countries.

The meeting came amid recurring concerns over the safety of Nigerians in South Africa, including allegations of xenophobic attacks, violence, discrimination and other forms of mistreatment against foreign nationals.

Nigeria and South Africa maintain longstanding diplomatic, political and economic relations, with cooperation spanning trade, investment, regional security and multilateral engagements.

However, incidents involving attacks on foreign nationals have periodically strained relations, prompting diplomatic interventions and calls for stronger protection of citizens.

World.title: In Bid to Cut Hotel Costs, FG Moves to Activate Underutilised Government Facilities
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Ndubuisi Francis in Abuja

The Federal Ministry of Finance (FMF) has moved to slash avoidable government expenses on hotels and other privately-owned venues by promoting the use of existing meeting facilities owned by Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs).

The initiative which is being driven by the ministry’s Efficiency Office (E-Office), and designed to address the cost implications of government institutions hiring external venues for official meetings while suitable government-owned facilities remain underutilised.

The latest move is coming over a year after the former Finance Minister, Wale Edun, floated the yet-to-be effective BisonFly Project, a strategic initiative aimed st streamlining and reducing air travel costs across MDAs through a centralised, technology-driven booking system.

On the new drive to cut costs associated with hotels, a statement issued on Monday by the FMF’s Head, Information and Public Relations Unit, Efe Ovuakporie, said the E-Office was working towards a more coordinated system in which MDAs can identify and access available meeting facilities across government, reducing unnecessary venue-hire costs while ensuring that public infrastructure delivers greater value.

According to the statement, a key component of the initiative was the compilation of a comprehensive directory of meeting facilities owned by MDAs nationwide.

The directory, which will be published on the Federal Ministry of Finance’s website upon completion, is expected to provide government institutions with information on available facilities and make it easier to identify suitable venues for official engagements.

“The arrangement also presents an opportunity for institutions with available meeting facilities to earn revenue from their use by other MDAs, while promoting better utilisation of existing infrastructure and reducing dependence on commercial venues.

“The development is consistent with the Efficiency Office’s mandate to promote value for money, reduce government overhead expenditure, monitor the utilisation of public assets and identify opportunities for eliminating waste across government institutions.

“In furtherance of this mandate, the Office recently undertook an inspection of shared government facilities across the five South-Eastern states of Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo. The exercise covered selected Federal Secretariats, Federal Polytechnics, Federal Medical Centres and Federal Universities.

“The inspections assessed the condition, availability, utilisation and maintenance of the facilities, with particular attention to identifying areas where improved management could enhance their usefulness and reduce avoidable expenditure.

“Among the observations were underutilised office spaces and facilities, deteriorating furniture, fittings and equipment, and the need for improved maintenance of some offices and common areas. The teams also identified opportunities to improve the use of conference facilities and strengthen the organisation, storage and preservation of official records,” the statement said.

It added that the E-Office engaged the management of the institutions visited on practical measures to address the identified gaps, including regular maintenance schedules, proper asset inventories, improved records management and more effective arrangements for sharing available facilities.

The findings, the statement explained, will contribute to recommendations for strengthening the management of government assets, improving institutional cooperation and ensuring that infrastructure provided with public funds is put to productive use.

“The Office stressed that the inspections are intended to identify areas for improvement and promote more responsible management of public resources, rather than apportion blame to the institutions concerned.

“Through these interventions, the Federal Ministry of Finance is reinforcing the need for government institutions to look inward, maximise the use of existing assets and eliminate expenditure that can be avoided through better planning and resource sharing,” it noted.

World.title: Benni McCarthy’s explosive comment shocks the media in Kenya
World.content:
McCarthy was adressing the media after Kenya lost 2-1 to South Africa in Nairobi on Tuesday night.

Relebohile Mofokeng scored twice in the second half to secure all three points for Pitso Mosimane’s side. Mohammed Bajaber pulled one back late on, but Kenya could not avoid defeat.

BENNI MCCARTHY TAKES AIM AT KENYAN CRITICS

The result was followed by a fiery response from the former Bafana Bafana striker, who made it clear that criticism from social media users does not affect his peace of mind.



According to Pulse Kenya, the 48-year-old was asked about the criticism surrounding his leadership and responded by questioning the circumstances of some of his online detractors.

His comments about people struggling to afford basic necessities have particularly attracted attention.

“When I go home, I put my head on the pillow. I sleep like a baby. My family, my life is complete. I don’t have to worry about hot water. But somebody is sitting on his phone; maybe he hasn’t eaten for two weeks.

“But he can quickly say, ah, that goat’s torn us, or whatever. So maybe I have to pay mind to watch somebody who doesn’t matter in my life one bit. So I don’t mind,” McCarthy added.

“I just keep doing my job, and I try to do the best that I possibly can with the players. As long as I’ve got the respect of the players, the people that I surround myself with, my technical team, my life is peachy.”

PRESSURE GROWS AFTER HARAMBEE STARS DEFEAT

The comments come at a difficult time for McCarthy, whose team have collected just two points from their four Group D qualifying matches.



Kenya had previously held Bafana to a 2-2 draw in Johannesburg, but could not repeat that performance in front of their home supporters.

McCarthy has also faced questions about his tactical decisions and the team’s progress. However, he remains focused on his relationship with the players and technical staff rather than criticism from outside the dressing room.

Kenya are already assured of a place at the 2027 AFCON as co-hosts with Uganda and Tanzania.

World.title: What Relebohile Mofokeng said after his brace for Bafana Bafana
World.content:
Mofokeng scored twice as Bafana Bafana won 2-1 over Kenya at Nyayo National Stadium in Nairobi on Tuesday night. His second-half contribution secured three important points and lifted South Africa back to the top of Group D.

Pitso Mosimane’s team now have 10 points from four matches, while Guinea have nine in second place. With two qualifying fixtures remaining, Bafana Bafana have taken control of their campaign to reach the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.

There will be the trip to Guinea and the visit of Eritea. Both games will be played in March 2027 before the tournament in Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya in July.



RELEBOHILE MOFOKENG ON HIS BAFANA COMMITMENT

The attacking midfielder known as President Yama2K has stressed that his priority is giving everything whenever he gets the opportunity to represent his country.

The Orlando Pirates product found the breakthrough in the 68th minute before completing his brace in the 86th. Kenya managed a late response, but South Africa held on to claim the win.

Speaking after the match, Mofokeng said he was proud to wear the national team shirt and insisted that his performances are not about answering his critics.



“When I get to the pitch, I give my all, and when I go out, you must know that I left everything on the pitch,” said Mofokeng after the game in Nairobi.

“I’m very proud to play for my country, and I’ll just keep on going. I think when getting onto the pitch it is not about proving a point to anyone; I’m just doing what the coach [Mosimane] wants.

“If someone doesn’t believe in me, I just have to work hard; it’s not criticism – they just don’t believe in you, and you have to work on it. Sometimes people criticise us, and sometimes it’s true. Take the criticism and work on it,” he added.



MORE EFFECIENCY INfRONT OF GOAL

Mofokeng also addressed South Africa’s missed opportunities in the first half. Bafana had drawn 2-2 with Kenya in the previous meeting at Orlando Amstel Arena, making Tuesday’s result particularly important.

“Coming back to the missed chances in the first half, even at home we missed many chances, and that’s why we drew against the Harambee Stars [last Friday at the Orlando Amstel Arena], and the coach said we have to use our chances; then the game will change, and that’s what happened.

“After we scored one goal, the game changed, and we created more opportunities, and that worked for us,” Mofokeng added.

World.title: Rassie banned again: Why 17 November is his unlucky date
World.content:
Rassie Erasmus is banned for a third time as World Rugby reacts to his criticism of referees and match officials. Image: South Africa Rugby.

World Rugby has completed a “triple” after suspending Rassie Erasmus for a third time.

The global sport body has banned the Springboks’ tactical mind for six matches.

Here’s why 17 November has become synonymous with Rassie’s disciplinary issues.



2026: Rassie BANNED FOR SIX MATCHES

The latest punishment was meted out to the Springboks Director of Rugby on Tuesday, 17 November.

This followed Rassie’s divisive comments about officiating during the 19-21 loss to France on 14 November.

He addressed the media in Dublin on Monday, heading into the decisive Nations Championship clash against Ireland.



The South African tactician gave a scathing review of the TMO and overall officiating.

His comments centred on what he described as a series of knee-drop tackles by the French that were not called out.

Rassie also suggested that Ireland’s Sam Prendergast, who was cited for a hip-drop tackle against Fiji, would escape a suspension due to a technicality.



The comments struck a nerve with World Rugby, and the Springboks coach was immediately suspended.

Statement: SA Rugby is requesting a full misconduct hearing for Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus following his sanctioning by an independent World Rugby panel for comments made in a press conference in Dublin on Monday – more here: https://t.co/ENZJLXa4Tp pic.twitter.com/yotTxRCp4K — Springboks (@Springboks) November 17, 2026

2022: Rassie receives a two-match SUSPENSION

Exactly four years earlier, the South African coach was pinged for a series of rants on Twitter (X).



His outrage stemmed primarily from the Springboks’ 26-30 loss to France in Marseille.

The match stoked controversy, according to Rugby365, with referee Wayne Barnes dishing out two red cards.

Rassie’s tweets appeared to direct criticism at the referee for several of his decisions.



However, the Springboks coach claimed that his videos were aimed at “our SA fans on what we should do better.”

Despite his clarification, World Rugby suspended Rassie on 17 November, condemning his “public criticism of match official selection, performance, or integrity.”

2021: Rassie suspended for two months

Once again, Rassie was in the crosshairs over his criticism of refereeing after a crucial loss.



This time, he slammed Nic Berry after the British and Irish Lions won the first Test 22-17 in Cape Town.

The Springboks had two tries disallowed, with South African TMO Marius Jonker under fire over his reviews.

Rassie posted a video analysing the performance of the officials, which World Rugby took to heart.



According to Business Day, his criticism breached Regulation 18 on misconduct and the code of conduct.

“Match officials are the backbone of the sport, and without them, there is no game,” read a statement at the time.

Rassie was handed a two-month suspension from all rugby and a matchday ban until 30 September 2022.



World Rugby also stated that he was fined £20,000 and had to apologise for his comments.

World.title: DStv prices: How much more do Zimbabweans pay compared to South Africans?
World.content:
DStv subscribers in Southern Africa face different monthly subscription costs depending on where they live, with currency exchange rates providing an interesting picture of how much households pay for access to premium entertainment.

Zimbabweans are paying more than their South African counterparts for the top-tier DStv package when the subscription fees are converted into rand.

Zimbabwe’s DStv Ultimate costs approximately R1 016

DStv introduced a revamped package structure in Zimbabwe on 5 November 2026, with the former Premium package renamed Ultimate.



According to the broadcaster, DStv Ultimate costs US$60 per month and offers more than 130 channels, including premium entertainment and sports coverage.

The package includes access to football, rugby, cricket, Formula 1, MotoGP, golf and tennis, among other sporting events.

Using the US dollar-to-rand exchange rate of R16.9357 recorded on 18 November 2026, the monthly subscription works out to approximately R1 016.

This means Zimbabwean subscribers effectively pay around R1 016 monthly for the top-tier package.

South Africans pay R979 for DStv Premium

Meanwhile, South African subscribers pay R979 per month for DStv Premium through a satellite decoder, excluding the Access Fee.

The package offers more than 130 channels, including the broadcaster’s premium entertainment offering and all SuperSport channels.



Subscribers can also access major sporting competitions, including international rugby, Formula 1, cricket, football and golf.

DStv also offers a discounted Premium subscription of R799 per month for qualifying customers who 

However, the standard month-to-month satellite subscription remains R979.

How much more do Zimbabweans pay?

Based on the prevailing exchange rate, Zimbabweans effectively pay approximately R37 more per month than South Africans for their respective top-tier packages.

This represents a difference of around 3.8%.

Over 12 months, the difference amounts to approximately R446, assuming the exchange rate and subscription prices remain unchanged.

Although both countries offer packages with more than 130 channels, their channel line-ups and local content offerings are not necessarily identical.

The comparison also excludes decoder costs, additional services and any applicable payment charges.

The figures therefore provide a snapshot of the difference in monthly subscription costs rather than a direct assessment of the value subscribers receive in each country.

dstv prices: zimbabwe vs south africa

While the top-tier subscription attracts attention, the differences extend to some of DStv’s lower packages.

A comparison of the broadcaster’s latest monthly satellite subscription prices shows how much viewers in the two neighbouring countries pay for different levels of entertainment.

World.title: Is this why Pitso Mosimane keeps benching Mbokazi?
World.content:
Will TLB force his way back into the side in the next round of internationals? Photo: @unplayable_za / x

Mbekezeli Mbokazi is in an unfamiliar situation as Bafana Bafana boss Pitso Mosimane continues to snub him. What’s going on?

Mbokazi snubbed again by Pitso Mosimane as Bafana win

Chicago Fire defender Mbekezeli Mbokazi was on the bench again for South Africa as they held out for a 2-1 win against Kenya on Tuesday. The 21-year-old made a cameo off the bench in the 71st minute for Pitso Mosimane’s side, and was an unused substitute last Friday in a 2-2 draw with the Harambee Stars. Mbokazi is not 100% match fit after a long spell on the sidelines, although if he’s fit enough to come off the bench, he must be almost there in terms of a starting berth. Ime Okon has started Bafana’s last 12 fixtures (both friendly and competitive), so it makes sense that he stays in the side for the sake of continuity. Until Mbokazi can displace one of Okon or Olwethu Makhanya, he might need to settle for a place on the bench. Next, Mbokazi will focus on Chicago Fire’s double-header MLS Playoff with Charlotte on 23 and 28 November.

Starting XI in the 2-1 win over Kenya

Williams; Matuludi, Okon, Makhanya, Kabini; Mokoena, Sithole; Appollis, Mbatha, Mofokeng; Rayners.



When are Bafana Bafana next in action?

South African fans must wait until March 2027 for their next AFCON qualifier. However, the 2-1 win against Kenya leaves them in a healthy position. Pitso Mosimane’s men are sitting pretty atop Group D with 10 points after four outings, and remain unbeaten.

Is Pitso right to stick with Okon and Makhanya as his central defensive pairing? Add your thoughts by clicking the red comments banner below!

World.title: Orlando Pirates news: Sebelebele, Lungu, Dlamini, Makhaula
World.content:
Orlando Pirates could be without Kamogelo Sebelebele and Ghampani Lungu for their Carling Knockout Cup semi-final against Stellenbosch FC, with both players currently battling injuries.

Sebelebele picked up an injury during the MTN8 final against Mamelodi Sundowns last month. According to KickOff, the right-back is expected to return to action early next month, potentially providing a boost to the Pirates squad.

His return would give Abdeslam Ouaddou another option in defence as the Soweto giants look to maintain their momentum across domestic and continental competitions.



Meanwhile, Lungu was forced to withdraw from Zambia’s squad for their two AFCON qualifiers due to injury. The winger has made a promising start to his Orlando Pirates career, but fitness concerns have threatened to disrupt his progress.

The extent of Lungu’s injury remains unclear, although he could also miss Saturday’s encounter against Stellenbosch.

Should Lungu be unavailable, Ouaddou could consider bringing in Bulelani Sigomoshe, who has only played a handful of matches for the Buccaneers.

Orlando Pirates could make surprise decisions

Makhehlene Makhaula or Kabelo Dlamini. Both experienced midfielders have struggled for game time this season under the Pirates coach and could be in contention for an opportunity.

With CAF Champions League games coming thick and fast, the duo could come in handy as the Buccaneers will need more legs and experience against top teams in the continent.

Orlando Pirates play Stellenbosch on Saturday in the Carling Knockout Cup, looking to reach their second final of the season.



Should Dlamini and Makhaula be given a chance?

World.title: 2026 festive season FUEL prices catch big break
World.content:
It looks like good news for festive season fuel prices. Going off mid-month data from the Central Energy Fund (CEF), petrol prices are set for a big cut in December 2027, with diesel prices looking close to breaking even after levy relief is withdrawn.

As such, the CEF shows these over-recoveries (decreases) at the midpoint of November 2026 (price per litre):

Petrol 93: -R3.06

Petrol 95: -R3.31

Diesel 0.05% (wholesale): -R1.15

Diesel 0.005% (wholesale): -R1.54

Illuminating paraffin: -R2.05

FESTIVE SEASON FUEL PRICES

But don’t forget that the National Treasury is partly reversing fuel-levy relief in December, too. This means adding R0.50 a litre to petrol and R1.50 to diesel for festive season fuel prices. Netting off the levy change gives the following changes for December (prices per litre):



Petrol 93 -R2.56

Petrol 95 -R2.81

Diesel 0.005% -R0.04

Diesel 0.05% +R0.35

Paraffin -R2.05

Applied to November 2026 prices (inland), that suggests petrol falling below R30 per litre. 93 will fall from R29.87 to about R27.31 and petrol 95 from R30.24 to about R27.43. Unfortunately, diesel 0.005% will remain near R31.56, and 0.05% diesel around R31.20. Note these figures are only an estimate and not the final announcement for festive season fuel prices.

GOOD NEWS FOR MOTORISTS THIS FESTIVE SEASON

10ppm low-sulphur diesel is becoming more widely available around the country, although at higher cost. Image: File

Of course, the CEF’s averaging period isn’t finished yet, but diesel remains some R13 a litre dearer than before the US-Iran war. Back in January 2026, the 50ppm price was R17.76 at the coast. Relief for diesel users this month is only a pause, not a recovery. So, when fuel levy relief ends on 5 January 2027, prices could rise again, barring a change of fortunes and significant price recovery.

So, petrol drivers, wait for the cut and fill up on or after Wednesday 2 December if you can. If your vehicle is a diesel, there’s no rush. But consider budgeting extra for January 2027 incase the levy relief brings price hikes in the New Year.



But what do you think? Are you happy to see some relief coming to festive season fuel prices? Or will you rather fly to your holiday destination? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

Masandawana have already won the MTN8 this season and will look for another trophy before the end of the year.



When are Sundowns playing Chiefs?

Both teams will be desperate to reach the final, particularly Chiefs, who will be hoping to continue their recent success in knockout competitions.



The last time Amakhosi reached a cup semifinal, they faced Sundowns in the Nedbank Cup. Chiefs emerged 2-1 winners before going on to lift the trophy in 2025.

Many Chiefs supporters will be hoping for a repeat of that memorable campaign as they look to overcome Sundowns once again and book their place in another cup final.

Can Chiefs win another cup match against Masandawana on Sunday?

World.title: Naked man causes N1 traffic chaos, throws punches at traffic officers
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Traffic came to a standstill on the N1 north near 14th Avenue on Wednesday morning after a naked man caused disruptions on the highway.

The man had parked his vehicle on the side of the highway before walking into the middle of the road and making noises as motorists drove past.

Videos widely shared on social media show motorists and emergency services personnel attempting to engage with the man, apparently without success.

In another video, the man is seen assaulting two Gauteng Traffic officers who attempted to restrain him.

A social media user also claimed that the man had damaged one of the passing vehicles.

The Johannesburg Metropolitan Police Department (JMPD) said investigations were ongoing and that it would issue a media statement once the facts surrounding the incident had been established.

World.title: Chinese robots learn from humans in tech hub Shenzhen
World.content:
SHENZHEN - At a park refreshment stand in China's tech capital Shenzhen, a humanoid robot grabs a cup and pulls a lever to form an ice-cream spiral, then hands the customer their order.

It's the kind of futuristic scene the country is keen to showcase as world leaders including Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin head to Shenzhen, a manufacturing hub north of Hong Kong, for this week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.

Chinese robots are famous for their slick dance moves, but artificial intelligence engineers are trying to train them up to join the workforce -- using reams of data captured by humans in headcams to help hone the machines' skills.

Although they still struggle with complex tasks like cleaning or ironing on their own, robots are already taking on more simple roles across the country.

"Mum, look!" a girl exclaimed when she spotted the ice-cream humanoid and its colleague that makes coffee -- treats on sale for around $4 each -- as passersby film the spectacle on their phones.

A human must regularly refill beans and empty coffee grounds for the robo-barista, but the pair's movements are driven by an AI model, according to maker AI² Robotics.

The startup said 200 of its humanoid servers are deployed in China, and up to 300 coffees are sold each day in the Shenzhen park.

"We're getting data feedback from many real scenarios," said CEO Guo Yandong, such as different light conditions that could help robots adapt to unpredictable environments.

- 'Workshop of the world' -

In China, 83 percent of people surveyed by Ipsos this year said they were excited by products and services that use AI, the highest of 32 countries including the United States, where just a third of people agreed with the statement.

Industrial spending in China on robots using so-called "embodied AI", which allows them to perceive their surroundings and act accordingly, leaped 230 percent year-on-year in January-May 2026, tax authorities said.

World.title: Anthropic set to price IPO in key test for AI boom
World.content:
NEW YORK - Anthropic prices its blockbuster IPO on Wednesday, giving ordinary investors their first chance to bet directly on a stand-alone AI giant in a test of how long the artificial intelligence spending boom can last.

AI stocks have swung sharply as investors question whether heavy spending on the technology will pay off.

Wall Street is also digesting the US midterm election results, which gave control of both chambers of Congress to Democrats, who are more wary of AI.

Nvidia, the chipmaker at the centre of the AI buildout and an early investor in Anthropic, has been shaken by the resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang after he admitted to an affair with a woman whom US intelligence reportedly believes could be a Chinese spy.

- IPO windfall -

Pricing is the step at which Anthropic and its underwriting banks set the final cost for shares sold to investors who placed orders in the offering, typically after markets close the evening before trading begins.

The maker of the Claude AI models said in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission last week that it plans to sell 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each.

Trading is expected to begin Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT," and the shares could quickly rise above the offering price. SpaceX shares jumped 19 percent on their first day of trading in June.

According to the filing, Anthropic's revenue has surged, reaching $17 billion in the third quarter, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier. Its annualized run-rate revenue was about $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from the end of September.

At the top of the range, the offering would raise about $64.4 billion, valuing the San Francisco-based company at about $1.4 trillion, including employee stock options and restricted shares.

Siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, now the company's chief executive and president, founded Anthropic with several colleagues five years ago after leaving ChatGPT-maker OpenAI.

Anthropic had been expected to raise up to $100 billion, which would have been the largest IPO on record.

Instead, the offering will likely fall short of the $86 billion that Elon Musk's SpaceX raised in June at a valuation of $1.77 trillion.

Earlier estimates had put Anthropic's valuation as high as $2 trillion, but such estimates fell as AI stocks slid on Wall Street.

Seven tech companies, including Google, Nvidia, AMD and Microsoft, have agreed to buy $26 billion of non-voting shares at the IPO price in a separate private placement. The companies are investors in Anthropic or major suppliers of its computing power.

According to an analysis by SaaStr, a software industry publication, Anthropic's more than 5,000 employees are set to bank more than $200 billion in the IPO, a windfall that could ripple through the San Francisco economy.

In the filing, Anthropic's seven co-founders pledged to donate 80 percent of their personal equity in the company to charity.

Anthropic has also said it will put 5 percent of its shares into a new public benefit fund. Together with the founders' pledge and an employee donation matching program, that would dedicate roughly 20 percent of the company's shares to public purposes.

Anthropic's IPO filing gives extensive space to the risks of the technology, reflecting the company's focus on safety even as it builds ever more powerful models.

It warns that advanced AI systems "could pose catastrophic or existential risks to society if not developed and deployed responsibly."

It also says the company's public positions on AI regulation and safety could expose it to "political backlash, or disproportionate regulatory action."

The warning refers to Anthropic's feud with the Trump administration, which ordered federal agencies to stop using its technology and labelled it a supply-chain risk after the company refused to let the Pentagon use Claude for domestic mass surveillance or lethal autonomous weapons.

World.title: Zverev serves up emphatic win to reach ATP Finals last four
World.content:
TURIN - World No. 1 Alexander Zverev was imperious on serve as he blasted past third-seed Ben Shelton 6-2, 7-6 (7/4) on Tuesday to book a place in the last four of the ATP Finals in Turin.

With one round of matches to play in the John McEnroe Group, Zverev's straight-sets win eliminated young Spaniard Rafael Jodar who lost earlier to Frenchman Arthur Fils.

"If I focus on myself and play good tennis the results will take care of themselves," said Zverev after the victory.

In a battle of big servers, Zverev broke in the opening game of the match.

The German then held to love. Shelton staved off two break points in the third game, the American forcing his only two break points of the match in the next game but ultimately unable to take them. He immediately dropped serve again.

Zverev, also dominating baseline rallies, clinched the set in the eighth game.

Shelton's serve steadied in the second set, although he was unable to touch the Zverev serve. Zverev did not drop a point on serve until he was 40-0 up in the 12th game with the tiebreak looming.

Zverev had won all six of his previous matches with Shelton, most recently in the US Open final, and taken all five tiebreak sets the pair had played. This one went the same way.

After Shelton, who had looked increasingly desperate in the later stages, put two routine forehands long, the American took a point off the Zverev serve with a blazing return. He immediately handed the initiative back to the German with two more errors. After another ace to bring up match point, Zverev finished after 94 minutes with a ferocious forehand pass.

"I don't care how I win the match point as long as I win it. But it was a highlight a little bit," said Zverev.

- 'So many matches' -

In the early match, Frenchman Arthur Fils fought back to beat Jodar 4-6, 6-2, 6-2 to keep his hopes of a place in the last four alive.

Jodar, 20, started brightly before requesting medical help after the first set and won only four games after that.

"The first set was a bit 'so-so' with a little bit of frustration," Fils said.

"But I'm very happy with how I handled the second and the third, and a little bit of relief now," he added.

Jodar is the first player to reach the Finals in his debut season on the ATP Tour with the highlight of a gruelling campaign coming with a quarter-final at the French Open.

"I'm better now, but it was tough obviously, because I felt that I couldn't compete and physically, I wasn't at the level today, especially in the last two sets," Jodar said of his injury.

"It has happened to everyone on tour because we're playing so many matches.

"It's a thing that we have to deal with and we have to move on and think about what we can do to prevent these situations," he added.

Fils's victory ended France's 15-year wait for a win at the ATP Finals since Jo-Wilfried Tsonga's semi-final success in 2011.

Fils has one group game left when he faces Zverev on Thursday while Jodar plays Shelton.

The top two from the two four-man pools advance to the semi-finals.

World.title: French forever chemicals slayer dreams of worldwide ban
World.content:
PARIS - As the son and grandson of French winemakers, Nicolas Thierry says he took up the battle against forever chemicals after seeing so many of his friends and family hit by illnesses linked to pesticides.

Becoming one of five new winners of the Earthshot prize, founded by Britain's Prince William and campaigner David Attenborough, could help the Ecologist lawmaker's campaign to make a French clampdown on forever chemicals worldwide.

Thierry has said he will give away his one million pound ($1.3 million) prize to groups fighting pollution and the long-lasting substances.

The 50-year-old told AFP ahead of the award, announced Tuesday in Mumbai, that he had been "revolted" by the level of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances -- PFAS or forever chemicals for short -- in farming and consumer goods and the impact it had on his entourage.

"That was the foundation of my activism -- the issue of chemical pollution, pesticides, and their impact on health," he said of his battle, which culminated in the French parliament passing heavy restrictions on PFAS in 2025.

"PFAS are the health scandal of the early 21st century. In France, we managed to pass a very ambitious law, but the challenge today is to turn off the tap on this pollution globally, given that these pollutants are found everywhere," he said.

- 'Poisoned' victims -

Thierry knows the campaign will not be easy. "My first thoughts are for all the victims, past and present, who have been silently poisoned for years," he said after the award was announced.

Forever chemicals are virtually indestructible synthetic substances which build up over time in the air, soil, rivers, food and the human body. Studies have linked them to cancers, liver damage and elevated cholesterol.

After a spell in a regional assembly, Thierry, an expert karate practitioner, was elected to the French parliament in 2022. Backed by scientists, consumer groups and health activists, he made PFAS his number one target.

"We planned things out over two or three years, carrying out high-impact initiatives so that people would start hearing about it," he said.

The 2025 law bans the production, import or sale of cosmetics, textile and other products containing PFAS. Only certain industrial clothes or items needed for emergency services were exempted.

A tax on companies that discharge PFAS was introduced in September.

"He combines technical expertise with an ability to move an issue forward," said Emilie Sarrazin, an Ecologist regional lawmaker in Thierry's home region of Gironde in the southwest. "He has truly done meticulous, masterful work."

Thierry's next target is tobacco, which is blamed for 75,000 deaths a year in France. After his law against PFAS passed, Thierry registered a new bill that seeks to ban the sale of tobacco to anyone born after 2014.

World.title: City Power battles 5,000+ outage calls after Joburg storms
World.content:
JOHANNEBSURG - City Power says it is dealing with more than 5,000 electricity outage reports after severe storms battered parts of Johannesburg on Tuesday evening, leaving several areas without power.

The utility says it received 5,100 outage calls across the city, with Roodepoort among the worst-affected areas.

Several substations were affected, including Florida, Robertville and Christiaan De Wet

City Power spokesperson Isaac Mangena says the storms disrupted operations and hampered repair efforts, with flooded roads preventing teams from reaching some affected areas.

“The storms yesterday actually disrupted some of our operations, especially moving into the evening, when our teams were unable to keep up with the amount of work we had to deal with.

“In the evening, we were sitting at more than 5,100 outage calls across the City of Johannesburg, with the Roodepoort area hardest hit by the storms.

“We lost several substations, including the including Florida, Robertville and Christiaan De Wet substations. This was just in Roodepoort.

READ MORE | Man's body recovered after Soweto flood tragedy

“Tshepisong also went off due to some of the flooding.

“But the main impact is not really the outages themselves, but the response, as our teams have been unable to access certain areas because of flooded roads, especially around Florida and around the Peter Road areas.

“Trees were also uprooted in areas such as Hurst Hill and Lenasia.

“This delayed our teams in dealing with some of the issues until the rain and storms subsided,” he added.

World.title: New dawn for MK Party in KZN's Richmond Municipality
