He said established procedures exist for raising concerns and proposing changes to the law. His remarks, as reported, do not say who is formally proposing to change the term limit.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Zambia Email address Follow

Why the Term Limit Matters

Hichilema won the 13 August 2026 election with a clear majority of the vote, according to the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ), and was sworn in on Tuesday 1 September. Under the current two-term limit, this second term is his last.

That is why any move to change the limit draws attention at home and abroad. Zambia is a major African copper producer, and investors in the United States and elsewhere watch its politics for signs of stability; our election report and inauguration report give the background.

In early October 2026, Andeleki, a member of parliament for Kazungula North, argued that two terms are not enough for a president to complete long-term programmes, according to Zambian news reports. That earlier view is the counterweight to his 18 November message that Hichilema is not seeking a third term, and the reports we have seen do not reconcile the two.

Scene from President Hakainde Hichilema’s second inauguration at National Heroes Stadium, Lusaka, 1 September 2026. Photo: THE ONE PEOPLE, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Who Plans to March

A consortium of civil society organisations (CSOs, non-profit citizens’ groups) notified police in early November that it planned a peaceful procession on 25 November. The Zambia Youth Organisation Consortium, a group of youth bodies, has separately announced a march in favour of removing the limit, and its vice-chair, Boas Kanyama, says it expects about 63,151 young people.

Reports say police will not clear the marches, but we have not seen the decision itself. Our wider Zambia explainer sets out how the country’s politics and its copper economy fit together.

What It Means for You

Travellers and investors with plans in Lusaka around 25 November should check their own government’s official travel advisory for Zambia. The government’s message is that the term limit is not in play, so watch whether that holds after the planned date.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether police will reverse their decision, or whether either group will march regardless. We could not obtain the original statements of the minister or the police.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Hichilema seeking a third term?

Home Affairs Minister Clement Andeleki says he is not. Hichilema began a second five-year term on 1 September 2026.

Are the 25 November marches allowed?

Zambian news reports say police declined to clear the marches this week. We could not obtain the police statement, so this is not confirmed.

What is the term limit in Zambia?

Zambia’s constitution limits a president to two terms. Hichilema was first elected in 2021 and re-elected in 2026.

World.title: Darfur Leader Urges UN Action on Detainees
World.content:
Photo: Dr. Ondřej Havelka / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

Musa Hilal, a Darfur tribal leader who backs Sudan’s army, urged the United Nations and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) on Tuesday 17 November 2026 to act to free detainees held by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a paramilitary group, in Darfur, a region of western Sudan. In a statement as head of the Sudanese Revolutionary Awakening Council, his political group, he named Daqris, Shala and Kubar prisons in South and North Darfur.

The appeal has so far appeared in one Sudanese news report, and we could not confirm it with his council or the UN. The abuse allegations in it, including torture and killings, are Hilal’s own and are unverified.

A Darfur leader’s appeal puts the fate of detainees on the agenda while the war continues, but the claims behind it remain unverified.

What Hilal Asked For

Hilal asked for access for humanitarian and rights groups to detention sites, medical care for detainees and contact with their families. He also asked for the fate of missing and abducted people to be disclosed, for an end to detention for ransom and for accountability.

He argued that freeing detainees could build trust and prepare the way for future prisoner exchanges and for dialogue. The statement was addressed to the UN, the UN Human Rights Council (the UN’s rights body in Geneva), the ICRC and regional and rights organisations.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Sudan Email address Follow

Who Is Musa Hilal

Hilal is a leader of the Mahamid, an Arab tribe in North Darfur, with a base in Mistariha. He was arrested in November 2017 and freed in March 2021 under a pardon by Sudan’s Sovereign Council, then the transitional ruling body.

In February 2026 the RSF seized Mistariha, his home base, and his council said he survived a drone strike there. Hilal has publicly backed the army, which is in a war with the RSF that has spread to Kordofan, in southern-central Sudan.

File photo, 2013. A busy street beside a mosque near Omdurman Market, Sudan. Photo: عاصم الرشيد التوم, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Why It Matters

The treatment of detainees is one of the questions any ceasefire would have to settle, and prisoner exchanges are among the trust-building steps Hilal himself names. The UN fact-finding mission on Sudan, an independent UN-mandated panel, told the Human Rights Council in June 2026 that conditions in detention facilities held by both the army and the RSF remain deeply concerning.

Because Hilal backs the army, the appeal may also be read as a political move against the RSF, and readers should weigh it that way. Our earlier explainers set out the army, the RSF and their backers and the outside powers behind each side.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, an online market where users bet real money on events, lists an 11% chance of a Sudan civil war ceasefire by 31 December 2026, with US$119,643 traded across all deadlines in this market (18 November 2026). Prices are bets, not polls, and the trading panel showed 16 cents for a yes share at the same time.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for You

Treat the figures and allegations in this appeal as one side’s claims until the UN, the ICRC or another independent body visits the sites. Watch for any reply from the RSF or from the UN human rights office (OHCHR), which would show whether access is on the table.

What Is Not Known

It is not known how many people are held at the three prisons Hilal named, or whether any independent body has been allowed in. We found no response from the RSF, the UN or the ICRC to the appeal.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Musa Hilal?

Musa Hilal is a Darfur tribal leader and head of the Sudanese Revolutionary Awakening Council. Hilal has publicly backed Sudan’s army in its war with the Rapid Support Forces.

What did Hilal ask for?

He asked the UN, the Red Cross and rights groups to act to free detainees held by the RSF in Darfur. He also asked for access, medical care and family contact for detainees.

Has the RSF responded?

We found no RSF response to the appeal as of 18 November 2026. The allegations in it are Hilal’s own and have not been independently verified.

World.title: Hundreds Flee Abu Zabad in Sudan’s Kordofan
World.content:
Photo: Roman Deckert / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

Hundreds of people fled Abu Zabad, a town in Sudan’s West Kordofan state, on Saturday 14 November 2026 as the army said it was advancing towards areas held by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a paramilitary group. The International Organization for Migration (IOM), the United Nations migration agency, counted about 750 people leaving in a single day.

A report published in Sudan on 17 November put the total at 1,150 over three days and said about 3,000 people had fled the nearby area of Abu Qalb. We could not match those figures to an IOM release, so they are reported, not confirmed.

What We Know

IOM described the situation in Abu Zabad as tense and volatile. Most of those who left went to Al-Sunut, Al-Salam and Lagawa, all in West Kordofan.

The army and allied armed groups say they took Al-Khuwai, a town in West Kordofan, on Friday 13 November, and the army has announced an advance towards Al-Nuhud, a town in the same state. We reported the army’s claim in our earlier report on the Khuwei fighting.

On Sunday 15 November a strike hit Abu Qalb, an area of Abu Zabad locality, and Emergency Lawyers, a group of Sudanese lawyers, counted at least 13 civilians dead. The Kordofan Human Rights Observatory, a local monitoring group, counted 15, as set out in our report on the Abu Zabad strike.

File photo, 2024. A street in El Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan. Photo: Tawsol58, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Sudan Email address Follow

Reported but Not Confirmed

A report published in Sudan on 17 November said about 400 more people left Abu Zabad on 15 and 16 November, taking the total to 1,150 over three days. The same report quoted the Kordofan Human Rights Observatory as saying about 3,000 people had fled Abu Qalb.

We have not found an IOM release for these newer figures. We therefore treat them as reported, not confirmed.

Why It Matters

West Kordofan was already hosting about 421,578 displaced people as of 30 July 2026, according to IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix, a regular field survey cited by the EU Asylum Agency. Each new flight may add to that caseload while the fighting moves closer to towns such as Al-Nuhud.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, an online market where users bet real money on events, lists an 11% chance of a Sudan civil war ceasefire by 31 December 2026, with US$119,643 traded across all deadlines in this market (18 November 2026). Prices are bets, not polls, and the trading panel showed 16 cents for a yes share at the same time.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for You

Readers following Sudan should treat the newest displacement counts as provisional, because the only figure matched to an aid agency covers one day in one town. The next IOM update for West Kordofan may show whether the 17 November numbers hold.

What Is Not Known

The IOM count covers one town and one day, so it does not show the scale across West Kordofan. It is also not known how many people remain in Abu Zabad.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many people fled Abu Zabad?

IOM counted about 750 people leaving on Saturday 14 November 2026. A report of 17 November put the three-day total at 1,150, which we could not confirm.

Where did the displaced people go?

Most went to Al-Sunut, Al-Salam and Lagawa in West Kordofan, IOM said. IOM called the situation tense and volatile.

What are the Rapid Support Forces?

The Rapid Support Forces (RSF) are a Sudanese paramilitary group fighting the army since April 2023. The two sides are contesting Kordofan.

World.title: Mozambique Halts Car Subsidies for Officials
World.content:
Politics: Mozambique

Mozambique’s cabinet approved on Tuesday 17 November 2026 a decree that stops paying two perks to State officials: a car subsidy and a start-of-office payment. Government spokesperson Inocêncio Impissa announced the decree after the session of the Council of Ministers (the cabinet), AIM, Mozambique’s state news agency, reported on 17 November.

AIM said paying the benefits would need about 7.4 billion meticais, the national currency, over five years (about US$116 million, at 63.91 meticais per US$, the latest Bank of Mozambique average reference rate we could confirm (4 September 2026), used for all conversions). The move comes as Mozambique works toward a loan programme with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), an international lender, which held talks in Maputo in September.

The decree affects State officials in senior and appointed posts.

Key Facts Who. Mozambique’s Council of Ministers (the cabinet) approved a decree on Tuesday 17 November 2026.

What. Vehicle and start-of-office subsidies stop for State officials and agents.

Cost. Paying them would need about 7.4 billion meticais (US$116 million) over five years.

Numbers. 3,828 officials receive the vehicle subsidy; 10,677 receive the start-of-office subsidy.

Safeguard. Approved processes keep their payments and customs charges.

Mozambique’s cabinet on Tuesday paused two perks for State officials, as the country negotiates IMF support.

Where This Decree Comes From

Separately, the Medium-Term Fiscal Scenario for 2027 to 2029, approved by the Council of Ministers and seen by Lusa, the Portuguese news agency, aims to cut the State wage bill from 12% of GDP in 2027 to 11.5% in 2028 and 10.7% in 2029, according to Lusa on the website of RTP, Portugal’s public broadcaster, an undated page. The same document lists limits on hiring, stronger audits, faster retirements, and a review of subsidies and seniority payments as the tools.

The Ministry of Finance’s Fiscal Risks Report 2027 projects a squeeze, Club of Mozambique, a news site covering the country, reported on Tuesday 22 September 2026. Wages would absorb 65.3% of tax revenue in 2027 and debt service 30.7%, so about 96 meticais of every 100 collected are already committed.

File photo: Maputo City Hall. (Photo: Claus Wonnemann, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons)

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Mozambique Email address Follow

What the Decree Changes

The decree suspends the vehicle subsidy (subsídio de viatura) and the start-of-office subsidy (subsídio de início de funções) for State officials and agents, O País, a Maputo news outlet, reported on Tuesday 17 November 2026. AIM said it covers those in direction, chief and trust posts.

These are senior management and appointed jobs.AIM said 3,828 officials receive the vehicle subsidy and 10,677 the start-of-office subsidy, figures it took from Council of Ministers information.

The suspension lasts until economic and financial conditions improve, AIM wrote, while O País does not state a duration. Legally, the decree amends article 11 (number 5) and article 15 (number 1) of Decree 81/2018 of 21 December, the regulation on buying, renting and disposing of State vehicles, O País reported, quoting Impissa.

It also changes ceiling values for vehicle subsidies and State-paid customs charges, which a joint order of 16 November 2020 from the economy, finance and State administration ministries had set.

Rights already granted survive: processes approved before the decree takes effect keep their vehicle subsidy, start-of-office subsidy and State-paid customs charges, according to O País and AIM. The sources we found give no date for when the decree takes effect.

Why the Government Says It Is Acting

AIM said the earlier regime pressed on the budget line “Demais Despesas com Pessoal”, meaning other personnel costs. New beneficiaries enter every year, holders of senior posts rotate and new public bodies are created, all raising the need for money, AIM wrote.

Impissa said the decree aims “to rationalise public spending in Mozambique’s current socio-economic context”, O País reported. O Económico, a Maputo business outlet, quoted him on Tuesday 17 November 2026: “A situação de emergência financeira é cada vez mais séria” (the financial emergency is ever more serious).

O Económico said the decision came at the 33rd ordinary session of the Council of Ministers, citing the official communiqué of the Council’s secretariat. O País added that the same session approved changes to the Rovuma LNG gas project (Area 4), an offshore liquefied natural gas development.

Why It Matters

The mechanism is simple: the less money already promised, the more room the treasury has. The Fiscal Risks Report 2027 puts the room very small, with about 96 of every 100 meticais collected in tax in 2027 committed to wages and debt service and about 4 left, Club of Mozambique reported on Tuesday 22 September 2026.

The decree comes as Mozambique negotiates a possible IMF programme; an IMF mission held talks in Maputo until 18 September 2026. The Finance Ministry said on Friday 11 September 2026 that an IMF mission in Maputo was negotiating a possible programme under the Extended Credit Facility, which is concessional lending for low-income countries.

Finance Minister Carla Loveira said in the same statement, carried by AIM, that the treasury “continues to manage liquidity challenges”. AIM estimates the State would need about US$116 million over five years to keep paying the two benefits.

What to Watch

The Finance Ministry said on Friday 11 September 2026 that the talks “will lay the foundations for the conclusion of the Staff Level Agreement and its formal approval by the IMF Executive Board by the end of 2026”. A Staff Level Agreement is a preliminary deal between IMF staff and a government.

We found no exact date for that approval, and no other dated checkpoint from an official source.

What Is Not Known

The two outlets give different headline figures. AIM reported about 7.4 billion meticais over five years (US$116 million), while O Económico reported requests that had accumulated to about 7.8 billion meticais (US$122 million), and the two may measure different things.

We did not find the decree number, its Boletim da República (official gazette) publication date or its start date. We also found no named reaction from unions, opposition parties or watchdogs by Wednesday 18 November 2026.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Mozambique suspend?

On Tuesday 17 November 2026 the Council of Ministers approved a decree suspending the vehicle subsidy and the start-of-office subsidy for State officials and agents, AIM and O País reported.

How much money is involved?

AIM reported about 7.4 billion meticais over five years (about US$116 million). O Económico reported accumulated requests of about 7.8 billion meticais (about US$122 million), a figure that may measure something different.

Do current beneficiaries lose their payments?

No, according to O País and AIM. Processes approved before the decree takes effect keep the vehicle subsidy, the start-of-office subsidy and State-paid customs charges.

How long does the suspension last?

AIM wrote that it lasts until economic and financial conditions improve. O País does not state a duration, and the sources we found give no date for the decree taking effect.

Sources: Mozambique Finance Ministry statement via AIM, 11 September 2026 · AIM, 17 November 2026 · O País, 17 November 2026 · O Económico, 17 November 2026 · Club of Mozambique, 22 September 2026 · RTP/Lusa, undated, published before 18 November 2026

World.title: Ruling Party Offers Johannesburg Mayor Job
World.content:
File photo. Traffic at a central Johannesburg intersection, South Africa. Photo: Gsalamander, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

SOUTH AFRICA · POLITICS

The African National Congress (ANC), South Africa’s governing party since 1994, has reportedly proposed that its rival Herman Mashaba become mayor of Johannesburg. The offer went on Tuesday 17 November 2026 to ActionSA, a party Mashaba leads, and would sideline the Democratic Alliance (DA), the party that runs Cape Town.

The DA won the most seats in all three big cities, yet no party has a majority. Johannesburg, Tshwane (the Pretoria metro) and Ekurhuleni (the East Rand metro) cannot choose mayors until parties strike a deal.

Key Facts The offer The ANC reportedly proposed Herman Mashaba as Johannesburg mayor on 17 November.

The split Under the proposal, Nasiphi Moya stays mayor of Tshwane and the ANC takes Ekurhuleni.

The rival bid The DA also wrote to ActionSA, which objects to two DA mayoral names.

Prediction markets Polymarket last traded Mashaba at 52% for Johannesburg mayor (early on 18 November, US Eastern time).

As of 18 November 2026

South Africa’s ruling party has reportedly offered ActionSA the Johannesburg mayor’s chair, leaving the DA, the biggest party in all three metros, on the outside.

The Big Picture

South Africa held local elections on Wednesday 4 November 2026. The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC, the body that runs elections) later declared the results, and the DA came first in Johannesburg, Tshwane and Ekurhuleni.

No party won an outright majority in any of the three, so each council is hung. A hung council cannot elect a mayor until parties strike a deal.

Archive photo: the Union Buildings in Pretoria, seat of South Africa’s presidency, in the Tshwane metro.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Johannesburg (South Africa) Email address Follow

What the ANC Offered

According to people familiar with the talks, the ANC proposal would make Mashaba, a businessman and former Johannesburg mayor, mayor of Johannesburg again. Nasiphi Moya would stay mayor of Tshwane, and the ANC would take Ekurhuleni.

Mayoral committee posts, the senior jobs beside the mayor, would reportedly be shared. ActionSA would get three, and smaller parties, including the EFF (Economic Freedom Fighters, a left party), three.

The ANC is the biggest partner in the national Government of National Unity (GNU), the multi-party coalition that runs the country. One unnamed ANC source said: “we suffered a major blow in the election.”

Why ActionSA Holds the Balance

The DA is the largest party in each metro, but neither it nor the ANC can govern alone. That is why both have written to ActionSA, which holds the balance of power in all three councils.

The DA has also sent ActionSA its own proposal, according to people familiar with the talks. ActionSA has said it opposes a deal if the DA’s Helen Zille and Cilliers Brink are put forward as mayors.

Our earlier report on the Johannesburg talks shows how the DA and ActionSA have circled each other. The DA’s own aims are in our coalition principles report.

ActionSA national spokesperson Matthew George confirmed on Tuesday that the party had received coalition correspondence from both the ANC and the DA. He declined to say what the letters contain or when ActionSA will reply.

Why It Matters

Johannesburg is South Africa’s largest city and its economic hub, and its metro council runs water, power, roads and the city budget. Whoever becomes mayor shapes how those services work.

Johannesburg is the country’s largest city. Any governing deal must hold several parties together, because no party has a majority.

What to Watch

The first checkpoint is Thursday 19 November 2026, when inaugural council sittings are reported in Johannesburg and Tshwane. The Ekurhuleni sitting date is not confirmed.

The second is Sunday 22 November 2026, which is 14 days after the 8 November declaration, though the start date may differ, since the Municipal Structures Act 1998 requires a first council meeting within 14 days of results being declared. Our 14-day deadline guide explains the rule.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, a prediction market where users bet real money, was read early on Wednesday 18 November 2026, US Eastern time. Its “Next Mayor of Johannesburg?” market, with US$181,495 traded, last traded Herman Mashaba at 52% and Helen Zille at 8%, but bids and offers were far apart, so it is a thin market.

Treat these as bets, not polls, and read the prices loosely while trading is thin.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for US Readers

Stable local government matters to investors in the city that anchors South Africa’s economy. A mayor chosen without a stable majority can struggle to pass a budget.

The offer is a proposal, not a deal. Our coalition politics explainer explains how such deals work.

What Is Not Known

ActionSA has not said how it will answer the ANC or the DA. It is also unknown whether ANC structures have publicly approved the offer, where the EFF and other small parties stand, and how vote shares translate into council seats.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did the ANC offer ActionSA?

The ANC reportedly proposed that Herman Mashaba become Johannesburg mayor, Nasiphi Moya stay Tshwane mayor, and the ANC take Ekurhuleni. It is a proposal, not an agreement.

Why is the DA left out of the ANC offer?

The proposal would sideline the DA even though it is the largest party in all three metros. The DA has sent ActionSA its own proposal.

When must the councils first meet?

Inaugural sittings in Johannesburg and Tshwane are reported for Thursday 19 November 2026. Counted from the 8 November declaration, the 14-day limit falls on Sunday 22 November, though the start date may differ.

Has ActionSA accepted either offer?

No. Spokesperson Matthew George confirmed on 17 November that the party received letters from both the ANC and the DA, but declined to say when it will reply.

Sources: IEC results declared 8 November 2026; statements by ActionSA, the ANC and the DA as reported 16 to 18 November 2026; Municipal Structures Act 1998; Polymarket (read 18 November 2026).
