World.title: Jordanian military Black Hawk helicopter crashes during training, armed forces say
World.content:
A Jordanian military Black Hawk helicopter crashed ‌during ‌a training ‌exercise, the Jordanian Armed Forces General Command said on ‌Wednesday.

It ‌gave no ‌details of ‌any casualties ‌and said further updates would follow.

World.title: Military reinforcements mass outside Kataeb Hezbollah stronghold in Iraq as standoff escalates
World.content:
DUBAI: Military reinforcements continued to arrive in Babil province on Wednesday to deploy around Jurf Al-Sakher, according to videos circulating online, after Iraq’s Kataeb Hezbollah vowed not to leave its stronghold despite a government deadline to withdraw.

Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi has also postponed a visit to Lebanon until further notice, Iraq’s ambassador in Beirut, Mohammed Reza Al-Husseini, told the Iraqi News Agency on Tuesday. The ambassador gave no reason. Earlier on Tuesday, he had announced that Zaidi would visit Beirut on Wednesday as part of a tour of several Arab countries.

On Tuesday, a Kataeb Hezbollah commander told AFP that the Iran-backed militant group would not leave Jurf Al-Sakher, after Iraqi authorities called on it to withdraw and allow the army to enter.

“That will not happen, not even over our dead bodies,” Abu Taleb Al-Saidi said during a press visit to the stronghold.

On Monday, Zaidi gave Kataeb Hezbollah a deadline to withdraw from Jurf Al-Sakher, after the government said an investigative committee had confirmed oil smuggling in the area. A security source told AFP that the deadline was Friday.

Kataeb Hezbollah said in a statement on Sunday that Zaidi’s office was “fabricating lies.”

“Since they were unable in practice to twist our arm with the slogan of surrendering weapons, they resorted to weakening us with the slogan of — God forbid — smuggling oil,” Saidi told AFP. He held Tom Barrack, US special envoy for Iraq and Syria, responsible for the “escalation.”

But Saidi also stressed that the group had no record of “any high-level clash with the Iraqi government or the security services.”

“We and they are extremely keen to avoid bloodshed,” he said.

Saidi said that “understandings were reached at the end of September” regarding the group’s weapons, but that “the government refuses... to make it public.”

Iraq has been facing mounting US pressure to curb Iran’s influence and rein in Tehran-backed armed groups, which Washington designates as terrorist organizations — a difficult task in a country long caught between the two rivals.

Successive Iraqi governments have struggled to balance relations between the US and Iran, whose influence has grown significantly in Iraq since the 2003 US-led invasion that toppled Saddam Hussein.

Zaidi, who came to power early this year, has pursued closer ties with Washington, and Iraqi political sources told AFP that his relationship with Tehran has been strained.

Kataeb Hezbollah has recently issued several statements criticizing the prime minister, accusing him of corruption and threatening his government. Senior Iraqi politicians told AFP that Zaidi had repeatedly said he was ready to “confront” groups if they did not disarm.

A senior Iraqi politician said that “it has become personal” between Zaidi and Kataeb Hezbollah, adding that political leaders were working to defuse tensions.

World.title: Saudi Arabia’s renewable energy pipeline reaches 79 GW
World.content:
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia’s renewable energy project pipeline has reached approximately 79 gigawatts, Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman said, as the Kingdom targets a 50 percent renewable share of its electricity mix by 2030.

The expansion is intended to diversify electricity generation and reduce reliance on liquid fuels, Asharq Al-Awsat reported.

The minister announced the figure during the 31st UN Climate Change Conference, COP31, in Antalya, as the Saudi Power Procurement Co. opened prequalification for developers seeking to participate in the eighth round of the National Renewable Energy Program.

The round covers three solar and wind projects with a combined capacity of 3.2 GW: the 1.3 GW Al-Muzairah wind project in the Makkah region, the 900-megawatt Tumair solar project in Riyadh province and the 1 GW East Al-Amwah solar project in Asir. Together, they represent 1.9 GW of solar capacity and 1.3 GW of wind power.

Prequalification is the first stage of the competitive procurement process. SPPC conducts preliminary studies and tenders projects before selecting developers and signing power purchase agreements. The announcement therefore does not mean construction has begun or contracts have been awarded.

Projects at different stages

The expansion falls under the National Renewable Energy Program, which targets between 100 GW and 130 GW of renewable capacity by 2030, according to the project tracker published by the King Abdullah Petroleum Studies and Research Center, KAPSARC.

The figures reflect the scale of Saudi Arabia’s development pipeline but also highlight the importance of distinguishing planned capacity from projects already under construction or in operation.

KAPSARC’s September 2026 data tracked approximately 70 GW across 58 renewable energy projects, including 17 operational facilities, 24 projects under development and 17 offered for competitive bidding.

Energy storage expansion

Saudi Arabia’s renewable energy strategy extends beyond power generation to battery energy storage systems, which store electricity for later use, improve the utilization of renewable output and support grid stability.

According to the Kingdom’s second nationally determined contribution submitted under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, Saudi Arabia has tendered approximately 30 gigawatt-hours of energy storage capacity.

Of that total, 8 GWh is operational and connected to the grid, while the remaining 22 GWh is at various stages of development.

$8.2 billion in investments

Saudi renewable energy projects involve domestic developers and companies affiliated with the Public Investment Fund, including Acwa and Badeel, alongside Saudi Aramco Power Co.

On July 14, 2025, SPPC signed power purchase agreements for seven projects totaling 15 GW, with initial investments estimated at $8.3 billion. The projects involve a consortium led by Acwa and including Badeel and SAPCO.

In November 2025, Acwa announced financial close for the seven projects, valued at $8.2 billion (SR31 billion), securing financing for their development.

The portfolio comprises five photovoltaic solar plants totaling 12 GW — Bisha, Al-Humaij, Khulais, Afif 1 and Afif 2 — and two wind farms, Starah and Shaqra, with a combined capacity of 3 GW.

Spread across several regions of the Kingdom, the facilities are scheduled to enter service in phases during the second half of 2027 and the first half of 2028.

The projects form part of the National Renewable Energy Program overseen by the Energy Ministry, while the PIF aims to develop 70 percent of Saudi Arabia’s targeted renewable energy capacity by 2030.

World.title: UAE state oil firm says one missing after ship hit in Hormuz
World.content:
DUBAI: UAE state oil firm ADNOC said Wednesday that a crew member was missing after a ship belonging to the company was struck the night before in the Strait of Hormuz.

“All other crew members have been safely evacuated from the vessel. Eleven sustained injuries and where required are receiving medical care,” ADNOC said, adding that search and rescue operations were continuing.

World.title: Oil prices fall as higher US crude stocks temper supply risks
World.content:
SINGAPORE: Oil prices fell on Wednesday on data showing ‌an increase in US crude and fuel inventories last week, although ongoing US-Iran attacks and disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz limited losses.

Brent crude futures fell 61 cents, or 0.7 percent, to $92.53 a barrel at 08:50 a.m. Saudi time. US West Texas Intermediate futures lost $1.24, or 1.4 percent, to $84.77 a ​barrel.

“Crude is wedged between a persistent geopolitical risk premium from tanker attacks and escalating tit-for-tat US-Iran strikes, and an ​increasingly bearish sentiment from a chorus of analysts forecasting a sizeable market surplus,” said Vandana Hari, ⁠founder and CEO at Vanda Insights.

Meanwhile, the price spread between Brent and WTI has also widened in recent sessions, with ​WTI seen logging steeper declines during Wednesday trading. The prompt Brent/WTI spread was hovering at a more than two-week high, LSEG data showed.

“WTI arbitrage ​trades have been shut to Asia and North West Europe, thus WTI correcting more than Brent is the expected price movement to allow the arbitrage window to open again,” said June Goh, senior analyst at Sparta Commodities.

This is particularly so with crude stocks building in the US Gulf ​Coast, Goh added.

US crude stocks rose by 5.28 million barrels in the week ended Nov. 13, market sources said on Tuesday, ​citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. Gasoline stocks rose by 5.12 million barrels and distillate inventories by 351,000 barrels.

But continued tensions between the US ‌and Iran ⁠and ongoing risks to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz kept price declines limited.

Bahrain’s defence force said on Wednesday that it had intercepted Iranian aerial attacks on the country, which hosts the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet, marking another escalation in the conflict a day after the US and Iran traded strikes.

Both oil benchmarks had settled higher on Tuesday as the US-Iran conflict intensified, even as talks ​continued between Iran and mediators ​Oman and Qatar. Attacks on ⁠ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz also stoked continued supply worries.

Iranian drones attacked a US military radar system in Bahrain on Tuesday, and the US retaliated with strikes on a missile launch ​site on Iran’s Qeshm Island.

An LPG tanker was also struck by a projectile while sailing through ​the Strait of ⁠Hormuz off the coast of Oman on Monday, and crew had to evacuate the ship.

“Although regional supply may continue to recover through alternative routes, the latest vessel data suggests that normalization of flows through Hormuz is still not possible under current conditions,” LSEG analysts ⁠said in ​a note on Tuesday.

World.title: Trump says US has concluded ‘very big trade deal’ with Philippines
World.content:
MANILA: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that the United States has just concluded a “very big trade deal” with the Philippines, but he did not provide any details, and Manila did not announce any agreement. “We’ve just consummated a very big trade ‌deal, the ‌biggest trade deal we’ve ever ‌made so far, and it is a fair deal for both countries,” Trump said during a state luncheon at the Philippine presidential palace.

“We were very happy with that, and we didn’t know that was going to take place, but ‌it took place ‌very quickly and it’s a magnificent deal ‌for both.”

Negotiations on a trade deal ‌between the two allies were not mentioned in any of the schedules released by either country.

There was no immediate comment from ‌the office of Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr about the deal Trump was referring to. The Philippines’ ambassador to the United States also did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Trump said on Tuesday that Thailand would eliminate all tariffs and remove substantial non-tariff barriers on its imports from the United States as part of a trade deal expected to be finalized in the coming weeks.

World.title: Xi, Putin meet ahead of historic Trump trilateral summit
World.content:
Shenzhen, China: Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin began talks in Shenzhen on Wednesday, a day ahead of a historic three-way summit with Donald Trump in the southern Chinese city.

Thursday’s trilateral has triggered fears that the three powerful men could decide the fate of Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv and Europe, and seek to carve up the world into 21st-century spheres of influence.

Washington had signalled that Ukraine — something Xi vehemently sees as not China’s problem — was not expected to be addressed, before Trump said that it would.

China has said only that the leaders would hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations” on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting.

Also up for discussion are the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.

Beijing has long maintained that the US and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile.

In from the cold

Chinese and Russian news agencies reported at around noon on Wednesday that Xi and Putin had met for talks — the fifth time the two leaders have met this year, including once by video link.

Putin has been shunned by the West since launching Europe’s worst conflict since World War II with his 2022 attack on Ukraine.

Addressing the APEC gathering on Wednesday, he said he expected the trilateral summit with Xi and Trump to be “highly useful.”

“At a time when military-political risks are on the rise, what is desperately needed is unity rather than division... and dialogue rather than ultimatums,” Putin said.

He said Western sanctions imposed on Russia since his 2022 invasion of Ukraine had failed, arguing that they were “not capable of fully stopping growth or destroying the economies of the competition.”

Earlier, Xi called for greater international cooperation on AI and free trade.

“Starting by lowering tariffs, expanding access and exploring regulations and management standards, China will conduct deep-seated reform,” Xi said as he opened the event.

Xi and Putin were expected to discuss energy and finance and then — in a smaller format — foreign policy including Ukraine and North Korea, Russian officials said.

Kim incoming?

Trump was on Wednesday still in the Philippines where a day earlier he met fellow leaders of the Quad — Australia, Japan and India — for the first time in his second term.

The grouping is broadly aimed at counterbalancing China’s regional influence.

He said he was eyeing one-on-one talks with Putin and Kim Jong Un at his next stop in Shenzhen, saying the North Korean leader “would like” to meet in China.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday stopped short of confirming the meeting with Kim.

“If we have a problem with North Korea, the only way we’re ever going to solve it is if we engage with them,” Rubio said in Manila.

Trump was in the Philippines for a summit of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

His visit saw protests by around 2,000 people carrying banners reading “Trump out now” and “Reject Pax Silica” — a reference to a US supply chain initiative.

Tariffs, chips and rare earths

While ASEAN leaders grappled with a raft of regional issues, the spectre of Trump’s ongoing tariff blitz has loomed large.

Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday slammed what he called a “countercurrent of unilateralism and protectionism” while touting Beijing’s own expanding trade with the bloc.

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Canada’s Mark Carney sang a similar tune on trade, with both explicitly citing a need to wean themselves off dependence on the US market.

On Tuesday, a combative Trump showed no let-up in his trade war with Beijing, saying the United States would catch China in rare-earths production “within 10 months.”

Hours before Trump touched down in Manila, Washington announced new rules on the transfer of advanced AI chips, a move that could potentially rankle ASEAN members.

Companies shipping high-end chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia will now require a special license, as the countries were said to represent a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion.”

Singapore responded by saying it was now exploring ways to facilitate “trusted access” for firms based in the city-state.

World.title: Rubio says ‘zero’ information that US outages are linked or caused by a malign actor
World.content:
MANILA: Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday sought to assure Americans that there’s “zero” information that the cascade of service outages, which snarled travel, cut off work, limited bank access and disrupted classified communications, are related to each other or to a malign actor.

Rubio sought to calm Americans as he traveled with President Donald Trump and they prepared to leave the Philippines for key meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in the tech hub of Shenzhen, China.

“We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyberhackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind,” Rubio said.

In recent days, Microsoft, Chase Bank, air traffic control and the National Security Agency have all been affected by technical failures and outages. Trump has faced a groundswell of criticism as friends and foes alike said the White House must answer for disruptions — and even staunch Trump allies have accused the administration of lying to Americans or hiding information about the true cause.

Trump was dismissive when asked whether he was concerned about the Chase outage on Tuesday.

“It’s life. When you’re big and powerful and you have all the money, things like that happen. It’s fine,” Trump said in Manila, declaring that “things like that happen.”

But as concern mounted, Rubio appeared to publicly address American concerns from the other side of the world.

There has been a steady stream of outages this week

Trump’s nonchalance was not shared by those already distrustful of the government and big institutions. And for Americans across the political spectrum, the drip-drip-drip of alarming and frustrating outages was an unsettling reminder of perils posed by interconnected tech networks.

The series of outages began on Thursday, when Microsoft’s email and other tools went down, paralyzing millions of workers who rely on them. Microsoft traced the issue to “an earlier network capacity upgrade.”

Flights across the country were grounded the next day in the longest so-called ground stop since 9/11. The Federal Aviation Administration blamed a router upgrade.

By Monday, the banks were in the spotlight, as customers reported difficulty accessing online accounts at several major financial institutions and the money transfer service Zelle after a technical issue at JPMorgan Chase caused ripple effects throughout the financial system. Chase said it was caused by “a software bug” and was “not cyber-related.”

The same day, United Airlines said that it had resolved an internal system outage that delayed departing flights.

And on Tuesday, an internal network that the National Security Agency uses to communicate classified information was offline after what the agency described as “routine maintenance.”

Trump’s nonchalance was not shared by some of his allies

Earlier on Tuesday, Karoline Leavitt, Trump’s former press secretary, said that the White House needed to do more to explain the situation.

“What I would say to the White House is: transparency is key,” Leavitt said on Fox News. Later on social media, she praised the White House for having Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton address the outages in an interview on Fox Business Network.

“Looking very diligently across the landscape, we are not seeing this as a cyberattack incident,” Clayton said, explaining that the US government believes the incidents were caused by security upgrades that took longer than planned or encountered unexpected hiccups.

Tricia McLaughlin, a former spokesperson for Trump’s Department of Homeland Security, was skeptical of the lack of information from the federal government.

“Americans aren’t stupid,” she posted on social media. “We want and deserve to know what’s really going on.”

Meghan McCain, a conservative commentator who is sometimes at odds with Trump and his allies, voiced similar concerns.

“Someone high in the administration needs to get on TV and tell the American people NOW what is going on,” McCain, who is also the daughter of late GOP Sen. John McCain, wrote on X. “No one who lived through COVID is believing this is all a coincidence.”

After Trump and other administration officials failed to offer reassurance on those cascading tech problems, Rubio seemed to take on the role of reassurer-in-chief when he appeared unexpectedly in Manila to take questions. The secretary of state is seen as a potential 2028 presidential candidate, though he lately has declined to comment on whether he would consider a campaign to try to succeed Trump.

But Trump’s role in the immediate moment was a pressing concern, even for supporters in his Make America Great Again movement.

“Our leaders are lying to us. This is very clearly a coordinated cyberattack,” Laura Loomer, a right-wing personality known for her incendiary social media presence, wrote on X. “President Trump should come back to the United States.” She did not present any evidence of an attack.

Conservative commentator Kylie Jane Kremer, writing on X, demanded accountability. “And why does it feel like we’re being told everything is fine while the very systems our country depends on are experiencing serious failures?” she said.

World.title: Iraqis celebrate security forces removing Iran-backed militias from Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi is reportedly pressing for the departure of Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah from Jurf al-Sakhar in Babil Governorate, citing claims of oil theft and smuggling in the militia-controlled territory.

According to reports, Al-Zaidi met with Iranian Quds Force Commander Esmail Qaani in Baghdad to arrange the armed faction’s quiet exit.

However, no meeting or agreement has been formally verified.

The encounter comes after a government inquiry allegedly turned up proof of illicit oil activities in Jurf al-Sakhar, also known as Jurf al-Nasr.

Baghdad has vowed to eliminate armed organizations who abuse the country’s oil infrastructure.

Kataib Hezbollah has dominated the region since 2014, with allegations of military bases, weapons dumps, and detention facilities.

Additional Iraqi security personnel have been dispatched to Babil, where locals are seen applauding their arrival and shouting in support of the Counter-Terrorism Service and attempts to reestablish government authority.

Kataib Hezbollah leader Abu Talib al-Saeedi has denied the government’s charges and warned that his forces would not leave, heightening the prospect of a violent clash.

The issue has also revealed schisms within Iraq’s Coordination Framework political group, with some militia commanders apparently opposing Al-Zaidi’s planned action.

The events are a major test for Baghdad’s attempts to impose governmental control over armed groups, investigate suspected oil smuggling, and allow the ultimate return of displaced inhabitants to Jurf al-Sakhar.

World.title: Iraqi PM vows to pursue firearms held outside state control
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi vowed on Tuesday to pursue anyone carrying weapons outside state control, declaring that there is no place in Iraq for unauthorized arms or corruption.

During his meeting with security commanders and tribal leaders in the central province of Najaf, al-Zaidi said that authorities will confront any armed group operating outside state institutions to protect public security and national resources, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Al-Zaidi ordered security forces to act firmly against suspicious activities and violations that disrupt stability. He instructed the interior minister to equip Najaf’s police and local security units with the resources needed to maintain order.

The prime minister tied the disarmament effort to “Operation Dawn,” an anti-corruption campaign launched in late June. The operation has led to dozens of arrests of high-profile officials and lawmakers.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks come a few days after senior security and oil officials were dismissed in a move against alleged illicit oil-smuggling networks.

The Iraqi government said that the end of the US-led coalition operation on September 30 eliminated any further justification for autonomous armed groups; thus, it set a June 30, 2027, deadline for bringing all weapons under state control.

While armed factions such as Asaib Ahl al-Haq and Kataib al-Imam Ali have started to sever their autonomous ties to fully integrate into official governmental institutions, other armed groups such as Kataib Hezbollah, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada refused to disarm as long as any foreign military presence remains in the country.

World.title: Gulf nations on alert after US strikes Iranian island
World.content:
Tehran – Kuwait said on Wednesday it was countering “hostile drone attacks”, as Washington’s Gulf allies remained on alert hours after the United States struck Iran’s Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.

Bahrain said its air defences intercepted attacks from Iran early Wednesday, a day after Tehran’s Revolutionary Guards said they attacked a base in the country used by Washington.

The interceptions come as the United States and Iran remain in a standoff over the key waterway, a conduit for global energy shipments, despite a lull in the war triggered by US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February.

The conflict has spilled over to Gulf states that host US military facilities, as Tehran stepped up retaliatory attacks.

Kuwait’s military said Wednesday its air defences were “responding to hostile drone threats”, urging its public to follow security and safety advice.

Earlier, Iran’s official IRNA news agency cited a regional official as saying the United States had hit Qeshm Island without causing serious damage.

US fighter jets “used precision munitions to strike an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) missile launch site on Qeshm Island”, an American official told AFP on condition of anonymity, adding that the strike was in response to Iranian “aggression targeting US personnel and assets”.

Washington and Tehran have vied for control over the Hormuz strait, with the US military working to protect ships transiting the waterway in defiance of Iran’s attempts to close it.

– Alleged Iran plot –

Despite Washington and Tehran holding back from a full resumption of hostilities, tensions remain high.

On Tuesday, US President Donald Trump said he was taking “very seriously” reports that Iran was developing plans to use a so-called “dirty bomb” in Washington.

CNN cited seven anonymous US officials as saying Iran was plotting how to target senior administration figures with a bomb laced with chemical or radioactive material, though they stopped short of saying Iran planned to carry out such an attack.

“If there is (such a threat), they will pay a price the likes of which no other country has ever paid before,” Trump said, adding: “I hope it’s not, but we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy.”

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed the report and called it “Iraq War-style propaganda”.

Earlier on Tuesday, explosions boomed across Bahrain’s capital as a mobile phone alert warned residents to seek safety.

Bahrain’s armed forces said they “confronted, intercepted and destroyed a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks today… before they could achieve their objectives”, while Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a US-operated radar system.

“Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain,” the Guards’ Sepah news website said.

The attack was in response to the “repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones”, it added. The Guards also said they had intercepted and captured a US drone south of Qeshm.

Bahrain, which hosts the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet, was heavily targeted earlier in the war that started with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, but had not been hit for weeks until Iranian drone attacks on Friday and Sunday.

– ‘Fear and anxiety’ –

“I was on my way to work when the warning sirens went on,” Abdulrahman Abdullah, a Bahraini civil servant in his forties, told AFP on Tuesday.

“Fear and anxiety rise as attacks increase… We hope things will go back to how they were.”

The violence came as the United States moved the USS Theodore Roosevelt into the region, bringing the number of American carrier strike groups in the region to three.

The deployment adds to an already large US naval presence, which includes two other supercarriers — the George H W Bush and the George Washington — and more than a dozen destroyers.

Iranian drone attacks have resumed ahead of this week’s unprecedented trilateral summit between Trump and his Chinese and Russian counterparts.

Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin will discuss “world peace” at the talks in Shenzhen, according to China. Trump has said he plans to discuss the Iran war at the meeting.

World.title: Iraq’s Kataib Hezbollah refuses to withdraw from Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iran-backed militant group Kataib Hezbollah has publicly refused an Iraqi government order to withdraw from its stronghold in Jurf al-Sakhar, also known as Jurf al-Nasr, in Iraq’s central province of Babil.

According to reports, Iraqi and Iranian officials reached a mediation deal on Tuesday to defuse the crisis.

Kataib Hezbollah accused the government of fabricating allegations to weaken the group and blamed US special envoy Tom Barrack for the escalation.

On Monday, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered security forces to prepare to enter the area, located about 60 kilometers southwest of Baghdad. Kataib Hezbollah was given a deadline until November 20 to vacate the area.

The confrontation escalated after an Iraqi judicial committee reported uncovering evidence of major oil smuggling operations in Jurf al-Sakhar.

Kataib Hezbollah fighters blocked the judicial committee from accessing parts of the site to complete its investigation. An anonymous Kataib Hezbollah official told the Associated Press (AP) that two local facilities refine oil strictly to provide fuel for the group’s vehicles and generators.

Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani arrived in Baghdad on Monday evening on an urgent mission to defuse tension between the Iraqi government and the armed faction.

World.title: Israel vows retaliation after UK sanctions firms for West Bank settlements
World.content:
London – Britain on Tuesday unveiled sanctions against eight Israeli companies involved in planning and building West Bank settlements, drawing a sharp warning that Israel would hit back.

The new measures, aimed at hindering expansion of the settlements, which are considered illegal under international law, also follow what the UK government has called a reset of its approach to the issue in September.

Unveiling the curbs, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said they were part of efforts to protect the so-called two-state solution aimed at resolving the decades-old Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

“Do not bid, do not build, and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution,” Britain’s top diplomat said in a statement.

Within hours Israel slammed the move and vowed retaliation.

“Israel views the additional sanctions against it… with the utmost gravity,” Israeli caretaker foreign minister Gideon Saar wrote on X.

“As in the past, Israel will take countermeasures against the British move.”

European leaders have already condemned plans to construct more than 1,200 homes in the occupied West Bank, which were put out to tender in August.

And the UN secretary-general has said the so-called E1 project posed an “existential threat” to a contiguous Palestinian state.

– We’ll build more’ –

The UK’s Foreign Office said Tuesday’s sanctions “target construction and property development firms involved in settlement expansion”.

“The UK has taken firm action against eight construction and property development firms which will disrupt their flows of finance and ability to support further construction in the West Bank,” it added.

The move results in asset freezes for the companies and groups as well as director disqualifications.

One of the blacklisted Israeli companies, real estate developer Harey Zahav, sparked controversy in 2023 when it posted a slogan on social media voicing hopes of returning settlers to Gaza.

It has gained a reputation for constructing wildcat settler outposts in the occupied West Bank without Israeli government authorisation.

In response to the British move, the high-profile head of a body representing the settlements vowed to ramp up their construction, accusing Britain of being a “colonialist, plundering and hypocritical country”.

Yossi Dagan, who leads the Samaria Regional Council, in the northern West Bank, added in a statement “we will build even more”.

– ‘Intolerable suffering’ –

Britain has toughened its position on Israel and the settlements since the centre-left Labour Party took power in mid-2024, sanctioning various Israeli individuals and organisations.

London’s stance appears to have hardened further since Andy Burnham replaced Keir Starmer as prime minister in July.

Less than two months later, newly appointed foreign minister Miliband accused the Israeli government of turning a “blind eye” to “ethnic cleansing” by West Bank settlers as he announced an import ban on goods from settlements.

Tuesday’s measures also included sanctioning the Tzav 9 Israeli activist group, which Britain accused of blocking aid from reaching the devastated Gaza Strip.

The announcement comes amid heavy criticism of Israel for failing to let desperately needed supplies of tents and timber into the ravaged territory, which this month saw tens of thousands of tents swept away amid heavy rains.

The Foreign Office, citing the UN, said “over 150,000 tents and 300,000 tarpaulins that humanitarian partners and donors purchased are outside Gaza ready to go in but are being held by the Israeli authorities”.

It said the floods had led to “nearly 4,000 households left without shelter and 1.4 million people living in tents or makeshift shelters”.

And it accused Israeli authorities of blocking “timber from entering, leaving no emergency shelter kits available in Gaza”.

“We will not stand by while those blocking desperately needed aid deepen the intolerable suffering of civilians in Gaza,” Miliband said.

World.title: US-Israeli war created ‘horrific’ situation for Iranians: Amnesty
World.content:
Paris – Iranian authorities have intensified their repression of the country’s population in response to the Middle East war, which began weeks after their deadly crackdown on anti-government protests killed thousands of people, Amnesty International said on Tuesday.

An internet blackout imposed at the time of the crackdown on January 8 and 9 and the scale of the casualties meant it was not yet possible for the group to quantify the number of people killed, Amnesty’s lead Iran researcher, Raha Bahreini, said.

But she told AFP in an interview that “there is no doubt that thousands were massacred in less than 48 hours”.

She added that the Middle East war, which began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28 “with Iranians still reeling from the January massacres, created a horrific situation for the people in the country”.

“The authorities used the cover of wartime conditions to intensify repression,” she said.

Bahreini said authorities have increased politically motivated executions “at a rate unprecedented in recent decades”, with at least 39 people executed in connection with the January protests.

With authorities threatening fast-track justice, “the time between arrest, conviction, sentencing and implementation has collapsed to a few weeks in some cases”.

There is now an “extreme militarisation of public spaces”, with pick-up trucks equipped with mounted machine guns patrolling the streets, she said.

“The authorities are conflating peaceful dissent with treason and support for foreign enemies.”

Demonstrations initially broke out over economic concerns last December and ultimately spiralled into the broader anti-government protest movement that peaked in January before being quelled.

– Even greater repression –

Bahreini lamented that the international community had shifted its attention away from the Iranian people to the geopolitical consequences of the conflict.

“The massacres that took place in January, which should have moved then global consciousness, have faded away from attention.”

On Wednesday, Bahreini is to address a roundtable at the French parliament alongside the United Nations rapporteur and the head of the UN fact-finding mission on rights in Iran.

Amnesty has already documented the killings of more than 3,000 people in the previous major protests in Iran in 2022, calling for the establishment of an international tribunal to punish those responsible.

But Bahreini said the repression in January was “on an even more staggering scale”.

Like in 2022, authorities fired on protesters with shotguns filled with metal pellets, which wound indiscriminately, she said.

But in 2026, they made even greater use of “military grade weapons”, such as assault rifles, and fired on people’s heads and torsos “from the rooftops” of residential buildings.

US-based Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) has said 7,007 people were killed, including 6,488 protesters. Norway-based Iran Human Rights says it has documented the killing of 4,200 people. Both groups have warned these estimates represent a minimum.

Iranian authorities reported more than 3,000 deaths, attributing the violence to “terrorist acts” orchestrated by the United States and Israel.

“Without access to official records, burial records and access to the country we may never be able to get a sense of the horror that took place in terms of its scale,” said Bahreini.

But it was “one of the deadliest episodes of protest dispersal ever recorded by Amnesty International in its history”.

World.title: Quds Force commander meets Iraqi officials, leaders of armed factions in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani arrived in Baghdad on Monday evening on an urgent mission to defuse tension between the Iraqi government and the Iran-backed armed faction Kataib Hezbollah.

Reports mentioned that Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei dispatched Qaani directly to prevent the dispute from turning into an armed confrontation.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi issued a deadline requiring Kataib Hezbollah to vacate the strategic Jurf al-Sakhar district in Iraq’s central province of Babil by the weekend or face a military assault by Iraqi Counter-Terrorism forces.

The government’s attempts to organize weapons under state control and deal with suspected faction-linked smuggling in the region—which Kataib Hezbollah disputes—are the root causes of the issue. According to reports, both sides have increased their military presence in the district.

Qaani met with members of the Kataib Hezbollah Shura Council and leaders of the Coordination Framework to advocate for political involvement in opposition to a military solution and to call for de-escalation.

There has not been any immediate progress in the initial discussions. According to reports, al-Zaidi turned down a meeting with Qaani, insisting that the government’s attempt to reclaim Jurf al-Sakhar is unavoidable, despite ongoing backchannel attempts.

World.title: Iraq resumes oil flows via rehabilitated Kirkuk–Ceyhan pipeline
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq officially resumed on Tuesday crude oil exports through the rehabilitated Kirkuk–Ceyhan pipeline to Turkey.

Pumping restarted at an initial rate of 120,000 barrels per day following a 12-year hiatus.

Operations began at 120,000 barrels per day from the IT1A station through a 46-inch pipeline to the MS metering station.

Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair confirmed that flows will gradually scale up to 500,000 barrels per day, though a specific timeline for reaching full target capacity has not been announced.

Technical teams from the state-run North Oil Company completed extensive maintenance, hydrostatic testing, and operational checks to restore the federal line.

The 960-kilometer pipeline had been inactive since March 2014 due to severe damage caused by repeated attacks carried out by the terrorist group of ISIS.

The restart operates under a one-year interim agreement signed between Baghdad and Ankara in August 2026. That deal sets a minimum transportation capacity of 750,000 bpd through the Turkish system to the Mediterranean port of Ceyhan.

Baghdad has prioritized northern and overland export corridors since the outbreak of the military conflict in the Middle East in late February 2026, which severely disrupted maritime shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: SCBA urges Supreme Court to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against advocate
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court Bar Association on Tuesday moved a petition, with the attorney general R Venkataramaniâs consent, requesting the SC to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against advocate Pravin Singhal who on Monday had created an unruly scene inside the courtroom and questioned the CJIâs integrity.

SCBA general secretary Pragya Baghel requested a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana for urgent listing of the petition. The CJI asked, âWhy do you want to make a hero of that advocate?â

But Baghel said that if such unruly and contemptuous behaviour is not nipped in the bud, it would cause grave damage to the image, dignity and reputation of the institution. The CJI agreed to list the matter as soon as possible.



SCBA was activated into drafting a criminal contempt petition and sought the legally required consent of the AG after it received a written complaint from advocate Meenesh Dubey who witnessed the unsavoury behaviour of Singhal, who threw papers towards the CJI-led bench after questioning the integrity of the CJI for not listing a petition for hearing.

SCBA said Singhal, after being removed from the courtroom by security personnel, continued shouting and using abusive and derogatory language against the CJI outside the courtroom.





The AG gave consent for filing of the criminal contempt petition on Tuesday.

âThe dignity and authority of the SC is integral to maintenance of public confidence in the administration of justice and the Rule of Law. The deliberate and intentional scandalous statements (by the advocate) knowing that it would lower the authority of the SC warrants strict action against the Respondents in accordance with law,â it said.

World.title: 'Heavens will not fall': SC on ED plea challenging Azam Khan's interim bail
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Wednesday refused to stay the Allahabad high court order granting interim bail to Samajwadi Party leader

in a money laundering case. The court observed that "heavens will not fall" if the order was allowed to stand.

However, a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant agreed to hear the

's appeal on Thursday.

The ED had approached the Supreme Court challenging the high court's decision, arguing that the interim bail order was passed in haste and without giving the agency adequate opportunity to present its case.

When the ED sought a status quo on the high court order, a bench comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana refused to intervene immediately.



"Let him be on interim bail. Heavens will not fall if we do not stay the HC order," the bench said.

Appearing for the ED, Additional Solicitor General SV Raju submitted that the high court had effectively decided the matter finally through an interim order. He also argued that the agency was not allowed to file its complete counter-affidavit and that its request for a trial court report on the service of arrest papers to Khan was not considered.





The CJI directed that the matter be listed for hearing on Thursday.

The Allahabad High Court had granted interim bail to the 78-year-old SP leader on Tuesday in the money laundering case, observing that the ED had failed to furnish written grounds of arrest when taking him into custody on October 31.

The high court had also described the proceedings as "motivated" and "mala fide", pointing out that Khan was arrested moments after being released from jail in another case.

World.title: Unvaccinated yellow fever-risk travellers may face six-day quarantine; new airport rules propose changes
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Travellers arriving in India from countries like Nigeria, Kenya, and Venezuela affected by yellow fever without a valid vaccination certificate could face quarantine for up to six days, with the cost to be borne by them, while airlines will have to pay for their transportation to designated facilities.

This is among the key changes proposed in the draft Indian Aircraft (Public Health) Rules, 2026, which seek to replace the 1954 regulations.

Under the existing rules, unvaccinated travellers could be isolated for up to nine days from the last possible exposure. The new draft proposes a maximum six-day quarantine counted from the date of departure from the yellow fever-affected country. Travellers unwilling to undergo quarantine can be denied entry and sent back without leaving the airport transit area.



The proposed rules also seek to widen airport health oversight beyond specific infectious diseases to cover pandemics, public-health emergencies and chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear and explosive hazards.

Airport food outlets and flight kitchens will have to be licensed under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Drinking water quality will have to be tested at source, with regular reports submitted to Airport Health Officers, who can order unsafe food to be discarded and close establishments or water sources found unsafe.





The 1954 rules required aircraft disinsection in specific situations, including flights arriving from areas affected by mosquito-borne diseases or yellow fever. The 2026 draft proposes making disinsection mandatory for all arriving aircraft, while also requiring airport premises and surrounding areas extending at least 400 metres beyond the airport perimeter to be kept free of mosquitoes, rats and other disease-carrying vectors.

Airlines will face more detailed reporting obligations, including submission of passenger manifests and information on illness or deaths on board. Airport Health Officers can seek passenger locator forms, contact details, destinations, travel itineraries and seat numbers, even outside a public-health emergency.

The draft also introduces a defined penalty schedule and a two-stage appeal mechanism against orders passed by Airport Health Officers.

It specifies monetary penalties for different violations, while appeals can be filed within 30 days and should, as far as possible, be disposed of within 60 days.

The health ministry has invited comments from government departments, airport operators, airlines and other stakeholders within 30 days of its November 16 memorandum. The draft will be forwarded to the Ministry of Civil Aviation for further action after the suggestions are examined.

World.title: In just one week, how security forces avenged attack on CRPF personnel in Kulgam
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Security forces on Wednesday eliminated top

commander Lateef Bhat in an encounter in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district, avenging the attack on

personnel. The terror strike, which left three security personnel injured, took place seven days ago.

Bhat, described by security forces as the last active local terrorist in the Valley, was trapped inside a mosque after an extensive search operation involving CCTV footage and repeated intelligence inputs. He refused to surrender despite repeated appeals by security forces and was eventually neutralised.

Union home minister Amit Shah hailed the operation, praising the "coordinated efforts" of the forces.

Shah wrote on X, "With the coordinated efforts of JKP, Indian Army, CRPF and intelligence agencies, Lashkar's last known active local terrorist in the valley, Lateef Bhat, was neutralised in an operation in Kulgam in the early morning hours today.



One of his terrorist associates, Umar Nisar, was also neutralised in Kulgam, the day before. The entire operation was marked by a very high level of synergy."

Bhat's alleged associate, Umar Nisar Dar, had been killed two days earlier.

Also Read|

November 11: Attack on CRPF post leaves three personnel injured

Two armed men opened fire on a CRPF post in Akhran village in Kulgam district, injuring three personnel, one of them critically. Officials initially received reports that the attackers had arrived on a motorcycle.





However, subsequent ground verification established that the two men had approached the checkpost on foot from a nearby forested area.

According to officials, one attacker opened fire while the other provided cover. Both fled towards Naupur through the tree line. "The area has dense vegetation resembling a small forest, which the terrorists used as cover before and after the attack," an official told news agency PTI.

Security forces launched a cordon-and-search operation, increased deployments and began examining CCTV footage from the surrounding areas.

November 10-15: CCTV footage helps investigators trace movements

Investigators examining footage from November 10 and 11 identified Bhat and Dar at multiple locations, including Mir Bazar, Akhran, Hablish and Kilam. According to police, the two had conducted reconnaissance at these locations to identify potential targets and plan attacks against security forces.

The footage also documented their movements while fleeing after the November 11 attack on the CRPF naka at Akhran, police said.

âDuring the analysis of CCTV footage from November 10 and 11, security agencies found both Umar Nisar Dar and Lateef Bhat captured on multiple CCTV cameras installed at the identified locations,â officials said.

âThe footage documented their movements while conducting reconnaissance and subsequently fleeing after the Akhran attack.â

Investigators also found that Dar had allegedly been providing shelter and logistical assistance to Bhat for five to six months. His family had lodged a missing-person report at Kulgam police station after he disappeared. Investigators subsequently established that Dar had joined The Resistance Front (TRF), an offshoot of LeT, after the November 11 attack, officials said.

Also Read|

November 16: Umar Nisar Dar killed, Bhat escapes

Following intelligence inputs about the movement of two suspected terrorists near Laru bypass, the Army and the Special Operations Group of Jammu and Kashmir Police launched a cordon-and-search operation.

The suspects fled towards two nearby schools situated close to an apple orchard, where students were present. Officials said security forces prioritised evacuating the children before beginning the operation.

The evacuation took around 90 minutes, according to officials quoted by PTI. Dar was subsequently killed in the encounter, while Bhat managed to escape.

Officials said Bhat was believed to have sustained bullet injuries.

Security forces continued searches across the surrounding area to trace him.

November 17: Search operation widened

Security forces extended the search to dozens of villages around the encounter site, with drones and sniffer dogs deployed to locate Bhat. Officials said additional forces were positioned to strengthen the cordon, while teams searched suspected hideouts and carried out door-to-door searches at identified locations.

The police also reiterated their findings about the alleged reconnaissance conducted by Bhat and Dar before the attack on the CRPF post.

The prolonged security restrictions, however, drew criticism from political leaders in Kashmir, who said ordinary residents were facing hardship.

November 18: Bhat trapped in Kulgam, refuses to surrender

Acting on specific intelligence inputs, security forces launched another cordon-and-search operation in Zangalpora village in the Devsar area of south Kashmir.

Officials said contact with Bhat was re-established early Wednesday morning, leading to a renewed encounter.

The operation began before morning prayers, with security forces offering him an opportunity to surrender after trapping him inside the cordon.

Videos of security personnel appealing to him to surrender circulated on social media. However, officials said Bhat refused.

According to Kulgam Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Anayat Ali Chowdhary, the encounter escalated when the terrorist opened fire at around 2:45 pm.

"An encounter was initiated based on credible intelligence gathered through proper planning and a coordinated effort by the Jammu and Kashmir Police alongside other security forces, successfully cordoning off the area where a local terrorist named Lateef is trapped," Chowdhary said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

He added, "Throughout this operation, security forces have maintained maximum restraint to protect the mosque situated within the cordon, strictly following standard operating procedures while handling the situation over time with patience and careful planning."

The SSP said security forces attempted to persuade Bhat to surrender through a lengthy video call involving him, the SSP and the chief executive officer of the 9 Rashtriya Rifles.

"Despite these appeals, the terrorist refused to surrender and instead entered a mosque, prompting repeated public announcements urging him to come out," Chowdhary said. Police sources subsequently confirmed that Bhat had been killed. They said he was trapped inside the mosque during the operation and that no damage was caused to the structure.

Reacting to the operation, Director General of the CRPF GP Singh posted on X, "Congratulations, guys. Some dishes are best served cold, even in cold weather."

World.title: NMC asks medical colleges to vet draft rules seeking tighter checks on animal experiments
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The use of laboratory animals in medical research could face tighter restrictions, with draft rules requiring researchers to explore alternatives to live animals wherever scientifically possible, minimise their numbers and reduce pain and suffering.

The proposals also seek to prohibit experiments involving severe suffering that is likely to be prolonged and cannot be alleviated.

In a public notice issued on Monday, the National Medical Commission (NMC) asked Deans, Principals and Heads of medical colleges and institutions to submit their comments, objections and suggestions to the Committee for Control and Supervision of Experiments on Animals (CCSEA) within 30 days.



The draft rules were notified on September 30 and published in the Gazette of India on October 6.

The rules place the principles of replacement, reduction and refinement at the centre of animal research. They classify experiments as non-recovery, mild, moderate and severe, and prohibit those likely to cause prolonged, severe suffering that cannot be alleviated.

Veterinary supervision would be mandatory for all experiments, with every establishment involved in animal research or breeding required to appoint a veterinarian.





Each establishment would also have to set up a nine-member Institutional Animal Ethics Committee, with a three-year tenure, to oversee experiments. The committee would include scientists, a biologist, a veterinarian and four CCSEA nominees, and meet at least twice a year.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The draft also seeks to avoid death as an experimental endpoint wherever possible, requiring researchers to use early humane endpoints. Where death is unavoidable, the number of animals affected and the duration and intensity of suffering must be minimised.

Establishments would have to maintain records of euthanasia, including the method, dosage and reason.

The use of stray and feral domestic animals would be restricted, with exceptions allowed only when their use is scientifically justified. Experiments on non-human primates would be permitted only for narrowly defined research purposes where no other species can serve the objective.

All establishments conducting animal experiments or breeding, housing and trading laboratory animals would require CCSEA registration and face inspections at least twice a year. Violations could invite a 15-day notice to rectify deficiencies, followed by suspension or cancellation for repeated non-compliance. Immediate action would be allowed in cases of imminent risk to animal welfare.

World.title: India ranks 10th in Climate Risk Index, with 78,000 deaths and $170 billion in losses from 436 extreme weather events over 1996–2025
World.content:
NEW DELHI: More than 9,00,000 people lost their lives worldwide due to weather extremes, resulting in direct economic losses totalling more than $4.7 trillion in the past 30 years (1996-2025), with India figuring as the 10th most affected country by recording 78,000 deaths and losing $170 billion due to 436 extreme events during the period, shows a Climate Risk Index (CRI) 2027 report by a Germany-based environment and development organisation released on Tuesday.

In annual terms, the report, released on the sidelines of the ongoing UN climate conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkiye, put the number of extreme weather events in 2025 at 367 â it means the world averaged one disaster every single day last year.

The events in 2025 caused nearly 35,000 fatalities, affected more than 100 million people and caused direct economic losses exceeding $158 billion worldwise. The year-wise index put India at 12th position, with the CRI annual ranking flagging Jamaica, Sri Lanka and Spain as the first three most affected countries, followed by Thailand, the Philippines, Pakistan, Indonesia, Bolivia, Mozambique and Vietnam in the top 10.



In the previous yearâs report, India was placed at ninth position on the long-term (1995-2024) index and at 15th rank in the year-wise index of 2024. As per the CRI, a lower rank means less risk. In the long term, China figures at 11th position in both 1995-2024 and 1996-2025 CRIs.

The analysis shows that heat waves were by far the deadliest extreme weather events in 2025 that caused nearly 70% of all reported disaster fatalities (more than 24,000 deaths).





Over the past 30 years, heatwaves have accounted for the largest share of reported fatalities (40%).

On the other hand, storms are by far the costliest hazard over the three-decade period, accounting for 58% of economic losses in 1996â2025. In 2025, storms also caused the greatest economic losses (41% of all such losses, nearly $65 billion in total).

Climate Risk Index 2027

âAmong the ten countries most affected in the past 30 years, the Bahamas is the only one that is per definition a high income country.

At the top of the list are nine countries that have been particularly hard-hit by devastating tropical cyclonesâoften repeatedly, with subsequent storms destroying structures that had already been rebuilt,â said Laura SchÃ¤fer, one of the authors of the CRI report, released by Germanwatch.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The CRI shows that the affected countries had unequal climate impacts. Over the 30-year period, the results confirm that lower-income countries that have contributed the least to climate change bear its heaviest costs.

In 1996â2025, nine of the 10 most affected countries were from the lower- and upper-middle-income groups, with the Bahamas as the only high-income country.

CRI analyses the number of deaths, people affected, and economic damage caused by extreme weather events â both in absolute terms and in relation to population size and gross domestic product. It is compiled based on data from the International Disaster Database on extreme weather events and socio-economic data from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank.

World.title: From Rajasthan painting to Kashmiri carpet: What PM Modi gifted to Asean, Quad leaders during Manila visit
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

presented a range of traditional Indian artworks and handicrafts to world leaders during his visit to Manila, the Philippines, offering gifts that showcased the country's diverse regional craftsmanship, textile traditions and cultural heritage.

The gifts included a Golden Pichwaai painting from Rajasthan for US President Donald Trump, a traditional Kashmiri silk carpet for Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr and a Chola bronze sculpture for Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto.

also presented a Dokra artwork boat to Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet, Bidriware silver inlay vases to Myanmar and Brunei, a royal blue Banarasi silk stole to Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, and a Jaipur blue pottery artefact to Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.



The presents drew on traditional art forms and crafts from different parts of India, including Rajasthan, Kashmir, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh and the Deccan region.

What Modi gifted to Trump, Marcos and other leaders

US President Donald Trump: Golden Pichwaai painting

PM Modi gifted Trump a Golden Pichwaai painting from Nathdwara in Rajasthan. The traditional cloth-painting art is known for its intricate detailing, luminous colours and elaborate compositions.





Created on finely prepared cloth using mineral pigments and gold detailing, Pichwaai paintings feature motifs such as lotuses, cows and trees, along with ornamental borders. Their golden finish gives the artwork a distinctive regal appearance.

Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr: Kashmiri silk carpet

The Philippine President received a traditional Kashmiri silk carpet, a hand-knotted craft admired for its sheen, soft texture, intricate designs and durability.

Made from fine silk, the carpets involve thousands of knots tied by skilled artisans. Some take months or even years to complete. Their designs often draw inspiration from Kashmir's natural beauty, featuring floral patterns, chinar leaves and geometric motifs.

Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto: Chola bronze sculpture

PM Modi presented a traditional Chola bronze sculpture to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto.

The art form flourished between the ninth and thirteenth centuries under the Chola dynasty in South India.

The sculptures are made using the traditional lost-wax casting technique, known as Madhuchista Vidhana. Each piece is individually handcrafted, making it unique.

Known for their anatomical precision, graceful forms and expressive details, Chola bronzes also offer insights into the clothing, jewellery, hairstyles and artistic traditions of the period.

They represent Tamil Nadu's metallurgical skills and artistic heritage.

Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim: Silver worked urli

PM Modi gifted Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim a traditional silver worked urli, a decorative Indian vessel adorned with intricate silver embellishments that showcase the skill of the country's metalworkers.

Traditionally filled with water and decorated with floating flowers, the urli symbolises purity, prosperity, hospitality and harmony.

Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet: Dokra artwork boat

Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet received a traditional Dokra artwork boat. The metal craft is made using the lost-wax casting technique, a tradition dating back more than 4,000 years.

The handcrafted piece depicts a boat carrying figures and birds, reflecting community life and harmony with nature. Each artwork is individually modelled in wax before being cast in metal.

The boat symbolises unity, cooperation, resilience and collective progress. The craft also preserves traditional skills and supports artisan livelihoods.

Myanmar and Brunei: Bidriware silver inlay vases

PM Modi gifted Bidriware silver inlay vases from Bidar, Karnataka, to Myanmar and Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah of Brunei.

Bidriware is a traditional metal craft made from a zinc-and-copper alloy and decorated with intricate pure silver inlay.

Artisans engrave patterns, insert silver wire and treat the surface to create its characteristic deep black finish, which contrasts with the silver designs.

The floral and geometric motifs draw inspiration from the architectural heritage of Bidar Fort. The craft has a Geographical Indication (GI) tag and represents the artistic traditions of the Deccan region.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi: Banarasi Katan silk stole

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi received a royal blue Banarasi Katan silk stole presented in a Sadheli box.

Woven from fine Katan silk, the stole showcases the centuries-old textile traditions of Banaras. Its intricate motifs reflect the craftsmanship and precision of generations of weavers.

The royal blue colour symbolises dignity, wisdom and harmony, while the presentation in a Sadheli box represents India's warmth and cultural esteem.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese: Jaipur blue pottery artefact

PM Modi gifted Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese a traditional Jaipur blue pottery artefact from Rajasthan.

The craft is known for its glossy white surface and luminous cobalt-blue designs. Its pieces feature hand-painted floral patterns, birds, geometric motifs and decorative borders.

Lao Prime Minister Sonexay Siphandone: Rose quartz elephant with gold work

PM Modi gifted Lao Prime Minister Sonexay Siphandone a rose quartz elephant with gold work, a decorative craft associated with Rajasthan's stone-carving centres, particularly Jaipur.

The artwork is carved from natural rose quartz and polished to bring out its soft, translucent sheen. It is then decorated with intricate hand-painted gold detailing, floral motifs and traditional ornamental designs.

Combining gemstone carving with miniature painting, the elephant symbolises strength, wisdom, dignity and royal grandeur in Indian tradition. Its gilded detailing reflects India's heritage of luxury handicrafts and royal decorative arts.

Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul: Rogan art painting

Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul received a traditional Rogan art painting from Kutch, Gujarat. Practised by a handful of artisan families in Nirona village, Rogan art is a rare, centuries-old textile painting tradition.

The technique uses a thick, elastic paint prepared by boiling castor oil and mixing it with natural pigments. Artisans create intricate designs freehand on fabric using a slender metal stylus.

The cloth is then folded to transfer a symmetrical mirror image onto the other half.

Traditionally used in bridal trousseaus and festive attire, Rogan art is known for its intricate patterns, geometric precision and craftsmanship. It represents Kutch's cultural heritage and the ingenuity of its artisans.

Timor-Leste Prime Minister Kay Rala Xanana GusmÃ£o: Handcrafted agate bowl

PM Modi gifted Timor-Leste Prime Minister Kay Rala Xanana GusmÃ£o a handcrafted agate bowl from Khambhat, Gujarat.

Made from agate, a semi-precious gemstone, each bowl has distinctive natural bands, colours and textures, making every piece unique.

Khambhat has been a centre of agate processing and stone carving for centuries. Skilled artisans carefully cut, shape and polish the stone to create decorative and functional objects.

Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung: Traditional Indian leather wall hanging

Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung received a traditional Indian leather wall hanging, a handcrafted decorative artwork rooted in the country's folk-art heritage.

Artisans soften and stretch treated leather before creating intricate designs through perforation, embossing and painting. The artworks feature floral, geometric and wildlife motifs, often made using natural vegetable dyes.

Rooted in rural traditions and passed down through generations, the craft reflects regional artistic styles and storytelling. It also helps preserve traditional skills and support artisan livelihoods.

World.title: India, Japan set to review defence ties as Rajnath, Jaishankar arrive in Tokyo
World.content:
India and Japan are set to review their bilateral defence ties and strategic cooperation as Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar arrived in Tokyo on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) for the fourth edition of the 2+2 ministerial dialogue.

Mr. Singh and Mr. Jaishankar will co-chair the Foreign and Defence Ministers' Dialogue (2+2) with their Japanese counterparts, Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said in a statement.

The two-day visit comes a day after the Quad leaders' summit in Manila, Philippines and as India hosts a joint humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) exercise involving the four member countries.

The Quad, comprising India, the U.S., Japan and Australia, is a strategic grouping focused on promoting a free, open and rules-based Indo-Pacific through cooperation in maritime security, technology, infrastructure and disaster response.

The India-Japan 2+2 dialogue follows the previous round held in New Delhi on August 20, 2024.

India and Japan will review the full range of bilateral strategic and defence cooperation, exchange views on regional and global developments and reaffirm their shared commitment to a free, open, inclusive and rules-based Indo-Pacific, the MEA said.

The two sides are expected to discuss defence equipment and technology, maritime security, joint military exercises across all three services and defence industrial partnerships, it said.

Mr. Singh will also hold a bilateral meeting with Mr. Koizumi, while Mr. Jaishankar will hold the 19th India-Japan Foreign Ministers' Strategic Dialogue with Motegi.

The meeting between Mr. Singh and Mr. Koizumi will be their third this year, following their engagements in New Delhi in August and on the sidelines of the ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus in Cebu in October.

In a post on X ahead of the visit, Mr. Singh said India and Japan shared a common vision for a "free, open, and rules-based Indo-Pacific", grounded in mutual trust and democratic values.

He said he would review progress in defence and security cooperation and explore new opportunities to deepen collaboration in technology, maritime security and regional stability.

Mr. Koizumi, replying to Mr. Singh's post, said he looked forward to discussing a range of issues, including maritime security cooperation.

He also said he would welcome the Indian minister to his hometown of Yokosuka and take him on a tour of a Mogami-class frigate.

Mr. Singh said on Wednesday (November 18) that he was on his way to the Japan Maritime Self-Defence Force's naval base at Yokosuka, adding that his Japanese counterpart was "playing the perfect host".

New Delhi and Tokyo will also review understandings reached during the 15th and 16th India-Japan annual summit meetings, held in August 2025 and July 2026, respectively.

Mr. Jaishankar will also participate in the third edition of Raisina Tokyo during the visit.

India and Japan share a "Special Strategic and Global Partnership" anchored in democratic values, mutual trust and respect for the rule of law, with both countries committed to a free, open, peaceful and prosperous Indo-Pacific, the MEA said.

The Indian Embassy in Japan said Ambassador Nagma Mallick welcomed Mr. Singh and Mr. Jaishankar on their arrival in Tokyo on Wednesday (November 18).

The visit comes a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi joined the leaders of the U.S., Australia and Japan for the Quad summit in Manila on Tuesday (November 17).

India is also hosting the annual joint HADR exercise, 'Sahayata Setu', at the Air Force Station in Jamnagar from November 17 to 19.

The MEA said Australia, India, Japan and the U.S. were participating as observers in the exercise, hosted by the Indian Air Force.

India, as chair of the Quad HADR Working Group, also convened a meeting to review progress in disaster response and strengthen cooperation in regional preparedness, it said.

The Quad's Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) framework seeks to strengthen coordination among the four countries in responding to natural disasters and humanitarian emergencies.

World.title: When does the 24-hour countdown begin after arrest? Supreme Court answers
World.content:
The story so far: The Supreme Court on November 5, 2026, held that the 24 hours timeline as mandated under clause (2) of Article 22 of the Constitution of India would commence from the date and time of a person’s detention when their liberty is curtailed and not from the time of their formal arrest.

A Bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S. Chandurkar examined the Article 22(2) of the Constitution which says that every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within a period of twenty-four hours of such arrest excluding the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the court of the magistrate and no such person shall be detained in custody beyond the said period without the authority of a magistrate.

World.title: Pakistani man convicted of plotting to kill Trump is sentenced to over 27 years in prison
World.content:
A U.S. ​judge sentenced a Pakistani man to more than 27 ⁠years in prison for plotting in 2024 to kill President Donald Trump and other prominent U.S. politicians at the behest of Iran, the Department of ‌Justice said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

"Earlier today, in federal court in Brooklyn, Asif Merchant, 48, of Pakistan, was sentenced by U.S. ‌District Judge Eric R. Komitee to 330 months in prison ‌for ⁠attempting to commit an act of terrorism transcending national boundaries ⁠and murder for hire," the DOJ said in a statement.

Prosecutors said Merchant tried to recruit people in the U.S. in a plan targeting Mr. Trump and others ​in retaliation for Washington's killing of ‌Iranian military commander Qassem Soleimani in 2020, when Mr. Trump was in his first term.

Targets in the 2024 plot also included then-President Joe Biden and Nikki Haley, who ran against Mr. Trump that ‌year for the Republican presidential nomination, federal prosecutors said.

A federal ​jury in March convicted Merchant of travelling to the U.S. to arrange for political assassinations on American soil, according ⁠to the Justice Department.

That trial in the New York City borough of Brooklyn started in late February, days before Mr. Trump ordered ‌an assault on Iran, carried out with Israel, that marked the start of the Iran war.

Merchant testified at his trial that he joined the plot with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps but did so unwillingly, to protect his family in Tehran.

Merchant said he was never ordered to kill a specific person, but that his ‌Iranian handler named three people in the course of conversations in the Iranian ​capital.

Law enforcement thwarted the plan before any attack occurred. A person Merchant contacted in April 2024 to help with the ⁠plot reported his activities and became a confidential informant, the DOJ ⁠said. Merchant was arrested and pleaded not guilty that year.

Tehran has denied that it targeted or plotted to attack Mr. Trump ‌or other U.S. officials.

U.S.-Israeli attacks on Iran since February 28 have killed thousands and displaced millions. Many top Iranian leaders, including ​then-Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, have been killed, too.

World.title: Cancel wetland excavation project in eastern Assam grazing grounds, CM urged
World.content:
Farmers and fishing community members in eastern Assam’s Teok region have urged Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma to scrap an ongoing “anti-people” project in “historic” grazing grounds and natural wetlands. They submitted a memorandum to the Chief Minister after staging a sit-in protest in Guwahati on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) against the project being implemented “in the guise of” a Flood Mitigation by Capacity Augmentation of Wetlands scheme.

The Teok Ban Niskashan Nala Khanan Dabi Samiti, a collective of villagers around the 7,598 bighas (almost 2,512 acres) under excavation, organised the protest. They said the authorities began implementing the project in January without any open public hearings, independent Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), Social Impact Assessment (SIA) or public consent.

Located in Jorhat district, Teok is about 330 km east of Guwahati.

The Hindu had reported on the first resistance in February-March after police served a notice to Debanga Sourav Gogoi, the Samiti’s advisor, for allegedly instigating villagers against the project involving the grazing grounds and the Jelengitup-Ghorachowa, Kenduguri, Garchiga and Kawaimari wetlands.

These wetlands are located within 5 km of the Brahmaputra River’s southern bank.

Mr. Gogoi said representatives from various progressive organisations, farmer organisations, political parties, students’ unions and civil society participated in Tuesday’s protest to express solidarity with the Samiti.

The other organisations and parties included Rabha Hasong, Asom Nagarik Samaj, Bhumi Adhimar Joutha Sangram Samiti, Silsako Uchchhed Protirudhi Raij, Darabil Go-Soroniya Pothar Suraksha Samiti Raijor Dal, Asom Jatiya Parishad, Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist), and Students’ Federation of India.

Samiti president Ramesh Duara said the organisation listed three demands in the memorandum to the Chief Minister.

The organisation wants the government to stop the excavation work; conduct a transparent and open public hearing in each project area involving independent environmental experts, public representatives, agriculturists, livestock farmers, fishermen and other affected citizens; and ensure legal protection of ancestral rights over the grazing grounds and traditional fishing rights in the targeted wetlands.

World.title: CCMB study points to new way of tackling fungal infections
World.content:
Scientists at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB), Hyderabad, have identified a promising new strategy to combat fungal infections by preventing disease-causing fungi from becoming invasive, rather than killing them outright.

A drawback of current antifunal drugs
