World.title: COP31 AI pledge fails to lure US Big Tech
World.content:
PROTEST. Activists and locals attend the People’s Climate March as part of a global day of action, “demanding climate justice, an end to fossil fuels and a just transition that puts people and the planet before corporate profit”, where the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) is also taking place, in Antalya, Turkey, on November 14, 2026.

Climate campaigners say the AI pledge would only work if the US hyperscalers signed up and if it were mandatory

ANTALYA, Turkey – China’s Alibaba is the only big tech company so far to have signed a UN-backed promise to reduce the environmental impact of artificial intelligence, as major US companies have stayed away.

The Antalya AI Pledge, launched on Monday, November 16, by Turkey, the host of COP31 climate talks until the end of this week, calls on governments and companies to take voluntary measures to power AI with cleaner energy.

Signatories are also urged to support more efficient infrastructure, track emissions, and improve access to AI in developing countries.

Publicized for weeks in advance of the summit on Turkey’s Mediterranean coast, the promise attracted 90 endorsements at its launch, including just nine countries and Chinese e-commerce and technology conglomerate Alibaba. Private companies, think tanks and nongovernmental organizations were also among those to back the pledge.

Meta, Microsoft, and Google, which operate global data-center networks, AI, and internet infrastructure at enormous scale, and chipmaker Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment.

Amazon declined to comment on the pledge, but said it had a new target to reduce the carbon intensity of its electricity consumption by 65% by 2030 from a 2019 baseline and reiterated its commitment to net-zero carbon emissions by 2040.

A report released on Monday found the United States’ more than 400 hyperscale data centers emit roughly as much carbon dioxide as Denmark.

South Korea and small countries sign

South Korea, a significant user of AI, was among the countries that signed, but the other government signatories represented small countries.

The United States has stayed away from the UN climate talks for a second year in succession after President Donald Trump withdrew from the UN climate process. Trump has championed both untrammeled expansion of AI and the continued use of fossil fuel.

But companies such as Amazon also face a different pressure from some shareholders concerned about the growing environmental impact and social opposition to the data centers their business requires.

The UN’s technology agency, the International Telecommunication Union, said it is engaging with major tech companies as part of its outreach effort, and would keep the pledge open to signatures until the next UN climate talks, COP32, at the end of next year.

Tech firms had been among the most visible corporate participants at previous UN climate summits, promoting goals, including carbon-negative operations and net-zero emissions.

But the rapid expansion of AI and data centers has complicated those ambitions.

While still investing in renewable energy, some of the companies have supported new natural gas generation.

Climate campaigners said the AI pledge would only work if the US hyperscalers signed up and if it were mandatory.

“Voluntary standards alone are not enough,” Julie Cerqueira, chief program officer at the Natural Resources Defense Council, said. – Rappler.com

World.title: House prosec: VP Duterte’s GenCorp SALN entry can’t be honest mistake
World.content:
Former Rep. Robert Ace Barbers —Screenshot from an INQUIRER.net video

MANILA, Philippines — House prosecutors on Wednesday rejected the suggestion that Vice President Sara Duterte’s declaration of a business interest in a firm in her Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALNs), despite not being listed as one of its stockholders, could be considered an honest mistake.

Prosecution spokesperson and former Surigao del Norte Rep. Ace Barbers, along with prosecution panel member Manila Rep. Joel Chua, made these remarks during an online press briefing in response to statements made by former Duterte administration spokesperson Salvador Panelo in a television interview. Panelo had questioned how Duterte’s action could constitute a crime if it was merely an honest mistake.

READ: Witness: SALN does not prove Sara Duterte’s ownership of GenCorp

Article continues after this 

“She (Duterte) knows very well about her investment in that company, and because people from their camp are saying that this was an honest mistake, for us it is just a palusot (excuse),” Barbers said.

“An Honest mistake? You declared it for two consecutive years. So, if your staff was responsible for that, then fire your staff,” Barbers said.

House prosecutors noted that Duterte declared having business interests in GenCorp Industries Inc. on her SALNs in 2024 and 2025.

However, last week, Atty. Suzette Balucanag-Punay, in-house counsel of fast food franchisee GenCorp, told the Senate Impeachment Court that Duterte had no stakes in GenCorp.

“An honest mistake seems unlikely because, first and foremost, the Vice President is very familiar with the company’s history,” Chua said.

Article continues after this 

“She even declared the previous corporations that existed before GenCorp was established, up until they became GenCorp. So, this cannot be considered an honest mistake because the history is clear [in the SALN]: four corporations, different corporations, over different years, were all declared by the Vice President,” he also said.

Chua was referring to Davao Bounty Times Food Corp., the original entity in which the vice president had an investment.

Article continues after this 

The business venture subsequently went through corporate transitions involving Great Jolly Times Foods Corp. and Times Square Bee Foods Corp. before eventually becoming GenCorp Industries Inc., which operates five fast food franchises in Davao City.

Also, Punay told the court that GenCorp had remitted a total of P2,142,369.14 from 2022 to 2025 to the vice president as “return of capital” for her original “loose investment.”

READ: Duterte’s ‘loose’ investment yields over P2M return in 4 years – witness

Barbers said claims that Duterte’s SALN declaration was an honest mistake or “inadvertence” would not absolve her of the alleged constitutional violation.

House prosecutors have previously noted that Article VII, Section 13 of the 1987 Constitution prohibits officials from indirectly or directly having business interests.

“I think inadvertence will not exonerate or exculpate VP Sara for the violation that occurred,” Barbers said, adding that claims of an honest mistake are just “diversionary.” /jpv

World.title: Iligan students stage walkout vs. Pax Silica, Trump visit
World.content:
Students of Mindanao State University – Iligan Institute of Technology (MSU-IIT) in Iligan City staged a campus-wide walkout on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, to protest the US-led Pax Silica Initiative and the state visit of US President Donald Trump in Manila. Photo from Silahis page.

ILIGAN CITY — Students from the seven colleges of Mindanao State University–Iligan Institute of Technology (MSU-IIT) staged a campus-wide walkout on Tuesday to oppose the US-led Pax Silica initiative and US President Donald Trump’s visit.

The Pax Silica Initiative includes the construction of the proposed high-tech manufacturing and semiconductor hub in New Clark City, Capas, Tarlac.

The project drew a multisectoral opposition over concerns about possible displacement, threats to ancestral lands and agricultural livelihoods, and the potential strain on local water and energy resources, as raised by groups opposing the initiative.

Article continues after this 

READ: Rally vs Pax Silica greets US president’s arrival

In a social media post, Silahis, the university’s official student publication, said that while the mobilization centered on Pax Silica and Trump’s visit, they also raised concerns over local water crisis, energy privatization, insufficient funding for education, and corruption, among others.“Carrying calls against neglect, the seven colleges of Mindanao State University–Iligan Institute of Technology (MSU-IIT) are currently uniting in a student walkout within the university,” Silahis said in its post.The mobilization drew allegations of police surveillance, with Philip Abriol of Kabataan Partylist (KPL) Iligan City Chapter saying students documented an Iligan City Police Mobile vehicle with two police personnel inside during the protest at around 2 p.m.

Abriol also reported the presence of several individuals whom students suspected of conducting intelligence operations within the university premises. Some were reportedly photographed or recorded, while others were not captured in videos or photographs.

The allegations, however, have not been independently verified.

READ: Donald Trump arrives in the Philippines to kick off Asia trip

Article continues after this 

“Instead of respecting the students’ legitimate exercise of their democratic rights, state forces responded with surveillance and intimidation—even within the confines of the university campus,” KPL said in a statement posted on its social media page.

Kabataan Partylist–Iligan City Chapter condemned what it described as state surveillance, infiltration and harassment directed against students, saying such actions could discourage young people from exercising their rights to peaceful assembly and free expression.

Article continues after this 

The group maintained that universities should remain safe spaces for critical thinking, collective action and academic freedom rather than venues for surveillance and intimidation.

As of press time Wednesday, the Iligan City Police and MSU-IIT administration have yet to issue statements on the alleged surveillance of students./coa

World.title: Barbers: VP Duterte’s witnesses deepen her ‘impeachment sinkhole’
World.content:
Former Rep. Robert Ace Barbers —Screenshot from an INQUIRER.net video

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte’s choice of witnesses for her impeachment trial has done little to rescue her defense and may instead have driven her deeper into an “impeachment sinkhole,” former Rep. Robert Ace Barbers, House impeachment adviser and spokesperson, said in a statement on Tuesday.

Barbers said the defense’s failure to present several witnesses who could have directly addressed the allegations of undeclared wealth cited under the second impeachment article left critical questions unanswered.

“When the defense had the opportunity to bring forward witnesses who could have clarified and rebutted these allegations, such as her alleged P817 million undeclared wealth, they failed to do so convincingly,” Barbers said.

Article continues after this 

READ: Prosecution questions VP Duterte’s choice of witnesses

According to Barbers, the problem was compounded by the performance of witnesses who did take the stand.

“What we saw was not a defense getting stronger under questioning. We saw serious questions piling up,” Barbers said. “A witness is supposed to help establish the truth and reinforce the credibility of the defense. If the testimony creates more doubts than answers, then the defense has a much bigger problem.”

Barbers said the problem for the vice president isn’t merely that her witnesses were questioned hard.

“It’s that, when the hard questions came, several could not provide the answers needed to close the gaps in her defense,” he said.

Article continues after this 

“Property records did not line up. A salary payment required further explanation. An alleged ‘loose investment’ had no clear documentary foundation. And witnesses themselves admitted limits to what they knew. Then the defense withdrew all 16 bank witnesses who could have faced questions about the financial records. At the end of the first four days, the central ₱817.87-million allegation remained unanswered,” he explained.

Barbers pointed out that several senator-judges themselves openly raised questions about the credibility of the witnesses and their responses to particular issues. For him, that is significant because credibility is central to any defense, especially when the witnesses are being presented to explain or contradict allegations at the heart of an impeachment case.

Article continues after this 

“The Senate is not a courtroom where a witness can simply make an assertion and expect everyone to accept it,” Barbers said. “The witnesses are there to answer hard questions. If they cannot provide clear, consistent, and convincing answers, they don’t close the case — they widen the cracks in the defense.”

READ: Ridon: December verdict possible as VP defense nears final witnesses

He stressed that the issue goes beyond political camps and personalities.

“The public deserves answers, particularly when the allegations involve wealth and financial declarations by a high-ranking public official,” he said. “The burden of an impeachment defense is not merely to produce witnesses. It is to produce credible witnesses who can withstand scrutiny and actually answer the questions being raised.”

Your subscription could not be saved. Please try again. Your subscription has been successful. Subscribe to our daily newsletter SIGN ME UP

“Instead of climbing out of the hole, Sara’s defense appears to have dug it deeper,” Barbers added. “The more the witnesses were questioned, the more difficult it became to ignore the unanswered issues. If the defense cannot convincingly account for the allegations, then it is the evidence—and the credibility of those testifying—not political rhetoric that must ultimately speak for itself.” /atm

World.title: Rescued serpent eagle freed in Cotabato province
World.content:
The rescued Philippine serpent eagle was released into the wild on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, in North Cotabato province. Photo by DENR-12

COTABATO CITY – Environment officials in North Cotabato province released an adult Philippine serpent eagle (Spilornis holospilus) into the wild on Tuesday after receiving medical clearance from local authorities.

Maria Elvira Lumayag, regional executive director of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Region 12 (DENR-12), said the raptor was first rescued on Nov. 16 by a vigilant resident in Barangay Midpapan, Pigcawayan, North Cotabato, and immediately surrendered to the Municipal Environment and Natural Resources Office (MENRO).

From an initial check-up with Pigcawayan’s municipal veterinarian, the eagle was transferred to the Community Environment and Natural Resources Office in Midsayap town for proper custody and documentation.

Article continues after this 

READ: PH eagle ‘Lakpue’ soars again in Leyte forests

Lumayag said another examination was also conducted shortly before its release through the Office of the Municipal Agriculturist (OMAG) of Midsayap.

The OMAG confirmed that the bird is healthy and free from injuries or illness, declaring it fit for release under DENR protocols.

“The successful recovery emphasizes the importance of wildlife conservation,” Lumayag said in a statement.

“Protecting endemic raptors like the Philippine serpent eagle is essential for maintaining ecological balance, as these birds of prey help control rodent and snake populations in the forest ecosystems,” she added.

Article continues after this 

She said the cooperation among locals, MENRO, and CENRO demonstrates how community involvement directly safeguards vulnerable biodiversity.

She added that by promptly reporting and surrendering displaced wildlife instead of keeping them in captivity, residents play a critical role in ensuring native species survive, thrive, and continue to support the health of local environments./coa

World.title: VP Duterte urged to personally explain bank-SALN discrepancies, GenCorp interests
World.content:
Vice President Sara Duterte —File photo by Grig C. Montegrande

MANILA, Philippines — The prosecution urged Vice President Sara Duterte on Tuesday to personally explain the discrepancies between what she declared in her statements of assets, liabilities, and net worth (SALNs) and her substantial bank balances, allegedly undeclared properties, and business interests as they appeared in other financial documents.

Benjamin “Jay” Tolosa Jr., a spokesman and counsel for the prosecution, renewed the call in a statement urging Duterte to take the witness stand, as she would be in the best position to explain apparent discrepancies.

According to the prosecution statement, records presented before the Senate impeachment court showed that Duterte did not declare cash on hand or bank deposits in her SALNs from 2019 to 2025, even as bank documents identified substantial balances involving accounts linked to her and Carpio.

Article continues after this 

READ: VP Duterte urged to show proof of business divestment

Prosecution forensic accounting expert Alexander Cabrera estimated at least P817.87 million in alleged unexplained wealth and undeclared assets from 2022 to 2025 based on bank transactions, financial disclosures, corporate records, and other documents, although Duterte’s defense disputes his findings.

Tolosa also raised questions about Duterte’s declared financial interest in GenCorp Industries Inc. and transactions he associated with the vice president’s brother, Mayor Sebastian Duterte, in Davao City, arguing that these financial relationships deserved a direct explanation.

During the defense’s presentation of evidence, GenCorp corporate counsel Suzette Balucanag-Punay acknowledged that the vice president received approximately P2.14 million from the company between 2022 and 2025, describing the payments as returns of capital from an earlier investment rather than compensation for participating in its operations.

The testimony raised further questions about Duterte’s financial interests because her SALNs identified connections to GenCorp even though its corporate records did not list her as a registered shareholder, while the prosecution maintained that the payments merited closer examination.

Article continues after this 

READ: VP defense turns to gov’t witnesses over P817-M wealth

The Senate impeachment court has admitted major financial records under the second impeachment article, although the admissibility of documentary evidence does not automatically establish the allegations against Duterte, who has consistently denied wrongdoing.

Article continues after this 

Tolosa maintained that prosecutors were prepared to question the vice president if her lawyers eventually decided to present her as a defense witness.

Duterte’s defense has not committed to presenting her as a witness, with the choice remaining part of its litigation strategy as the Senate impeachment court prepares to resume hearings on Nov. 19. /atm

World.title: Cayetano, Hontiveros raise concerns over corruption, divisions
World.content:
Photo courtesy of the Office of Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano

MANILA, Philippines — Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano and Sen. Risa Hontiveros on Wednesday raised concerns over corruption and political divisions in the country, calling for accountability, unity, and prayer.

Article continues after this 

Speaking at the 51st National Prayer Breakfast, Hontiveros cited Filipinos who gathered in public demonstrations to demand accountability over alleged irregularities in flood control projects.

She also pointed to community pantries established during the COVID-19 pandemic and the efforts of ordinary Filipinos to help flood-affected neighbors as examples of people looking after one another despite difficult circumstances.

Unity over divisiveness

For Hontiveros, national unity does not require people to share the same political beliefs, religion, or social standing.

READ: Rally vs Pax Silica greets US president’s arrival

Article continues after this 

“Dito ko nakikita na kahit magkakaiba ang ating pulitika, relihiyon, social status sa buhay, anupaman, maaari tayong magtulungan tungo sa mabuting buhay,” she said.

(Here, I see that even if we have different political beliefs, religions, or social backgrounds, we can still work together toward a better life.)

Article continues after this 

“After all, Amen, there are more things that unite us than that divide us,” Hontiveros added.

Hontiveros described unity as an expression of solidarity and a shared responsibility to look after one another, emphasizing that people must be willing to act on their concern for others.

She also sang portions of “Pananagutan” a song composed by her uncle, Father Eddie Hontiveros, to underscore her message that no one lives solely for themselves.

Cayetano admits questioning purpose when pressures come

Cayetano, meanwhile, described the Philippines as facing a crisis of values, identity, and purpose, saying prayer and a shared sense of responsibility were particularly important amid the country’s challenges.

To illustrate his point, he admitted that even he sometimes questions his own purpose due to alleged pressures.

“Ako minsan, what will I do? Ano ba ako ngayon sa gobyerno? Sino ba ako ngayon? Susundin ko ba si Lord ngayon or I will give in to pressure? Iba na pag kulungan na ang pinag-uusapan,” Cayetano said.

(Sometimes, I ask myself, ‘What will I do? What is my role in government now? Who am I now? Should I follow the Lord, or should I give in to pressure? Things are different when imprisonment is at stake.)

“Pag-iimbentuhan ka, can you imagine? Lalapitan yung mga witness sa amin, sasabihin pag hindi kayo pumirma, plunder kayo. Pag pumirma kayo, plunder si Alan,” he said.

(Can you imagine? They would approach our witnesses and tell them, ‘If you don’t sign, you’ll be charged with plunder. If you do sign, Alan will be charged with plunder.’)

READ: Cayetano tells Dizon to resist ‘pressure’ in Taguig project probe

He did not identify the individuals allegedly involved in the pressure or provide further details about the case during his remarks.

Unity and prayer

Moreover, in an interview following the event, Cayetano expressed hope in the uniting power of prayer which he said the country needs now.

“Whether we accept it or not, we’re a nation in crisis. May identity crisis tayo, may crisis tayo sa relationships with each other, trust in government, may crisis tayo sa corruption,” he said.

(Whether we accept it or not, we’re a nation in crisis. We are facing an identity crisis, a crisis in our relationships with one another, a crisis of trust in government, and a crisis of corruption.)

Asked about the impeachment proceedings against Vice President Sara Duterte, Cayetano said he hoped the evidence presented would be clear enough to support either a conviction or an acquittal.

READ: Sara Duterte Impeachment Trial: Everything you need to know

He warned that an unclear basis for the outcome could further divide the country.

World.title: PNP warns on use of socmed vs. public safety during Asean Summit
World.content:
Police equipped with riot shields and batons block the road in front of Liwasang Bonifacio in Manila in anticipation of the protesters’ planned march to the PICC. (Photo by ZACARIAN SARAO / Inquirer)

MANILA, Philippines—The Philippine National Police (PNP) warned against social media posts allegedly inciting violence during rallies.

It also ordered an investigation into those behind the content as the country hosts the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits.

“We will not allow the misuse of social media to threaten public safety or undermine the peaceful conduct of the Asean Summit,” said PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. in a statement on Wednesday.

Article continues after this 

“Freedom of expression carries responsibility, and those who use online platforms to incite violence must be held accountable under the law,” PGEN Nartatez said.

The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Council (CICC) earlier flagged online posts and other content exploiting the confrontation between protesters and police to incite and encourage violence.

For its part, Anti-Cybercrime Group (ACG) had been directed to identify those responsible for the posts.

These publications allegedly used images and other online materials to incite people to commit violent acts and engage in disorderly behavior.

Nartatez called on social media users to exercise responsibility in their online activities, emphasizing that these platforms should serve as spaces for constructive discussions.

Article continues after this 

The PNP chief also urges the public to report posts containing threats to authorities, instead of spreading them further.

Earlier, the National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) warned the public against misleading information on the 49th Asean Summit.

Article continues after this 

Read: NCRPO denies selective law enforcement for INC members

The NCRPO rejected claims of selective law enforcement after social media posts alleged that police would spare protesters identified as members of the Iglesia ni Cristo (INC) from arrest.

Meanwhile, police personnel remain on heightened alert as they continue to secure the remaining activities of the Philippines’ hosting of the Asean Summit, in coordination with other government agencies.

United States President Donald Trump left the Philippines on Wednesday following a brief visit, with Air Force One departing Manila at 2:35 p.m..

World.title: MMDA: Asean Summit traffic schemes, road closures remain in effect
World.content:
SUMMIT SECURITY / NOVEMBER 10, 2026Personnel from the Philippine Marines deploy near the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC) in Pasay City on Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026, to conduct security protocols ahead of the 49th ASEAN Summit. Security forces have intensified presence around key diplomatic venues across Metro Manila in preparation for foreign leaders and international delegates attending the regional summit.INQUIRER PHOTO / NIÑO JESUS ORBETA

MANILA, Philippines — The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) on Wednesday, Nov. 18, reminded motorists that security exclusion zones and other traffic schemes implemented for the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summit remain in effect.

In an advisory, the MMDA said that it continues to strictly implement restrictions around the Cultural Center of the Philippines complex, Philippine International Convention Center, and other key areas used for the regional gathering.

The agency said the move is to ensure safe and smooth travel for foreign delegates as the 49th Asean Summit formally ended on Tuesday.

Article continues after this 

Among the foreign leaders scheduled to leave the country on Wednesday afternoon is United States Donald Trump.

READ: MMDA announces Nov. 15-18 road closures, rerouting for Asean Summit

“Pinapayuhan ang mga motorista na planuhin ang biyahe, gumamit ng mga alternatibong ruta, at maglaan ng mas mahabang oras sa biyahe,” the agency stated in a statement.

(Motorists are advised to plan their trips, use alternative routes, and allot more time for their travel.)

Meanwhile, the MMDA also used a stop-and-go scheme to make way for the convoys of Asean delegates passing along the Epifanio de los Santos Avenue (Edsa) intersections and designated exclusive Asean lanes.

Article continues after this 

The affected lanes are as follows:

Roxas Boulevard (Northbound lane): Stretch of Roxas-EDSA Flyover, going to Buendia to Vicente Sotto St.

Roxas Boulevard (Southbound lane): Stretch of Roxas Blvd. Katigbak to Roxas Blvd. Edsa

The MMDA also instructed trucks coming from Anda Blvd. or Bonifacio Drive intending to use the southbound lane to turn left towards P. Burgos then right to Finance Road, before turning right San Marcelino towards Osmeña Highway Southbound.

Article continues after this 

The agency said that trucks would be allowed from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. to pass through both northbound and southbound lanes of Roxas Blvd. from Roxas Katigbak up to Buendia.

“Pansamantala namang sarado sa daloy ng trapiko ang bahagi ng Roxas Boulevard mula Buendia patungong Burgos kung saan service road na lamang ang maaaring daanan ng mga sasakyan,” it said.

(Meanwhile, the section of Roxas Boulevard from Buendia toward Burgos is temporarily closed to traffic, with vehicles restricted to using only the service road.)
